The passage states that Jagan "summoned him to his throne and said, 'My son is writing a book.' The head cook...evinced interest in the literary progress of Mali. 'He is going to earn twenty-five thousand rupees out of it, and he says he is going to finish it before September, wonderful boy!'"
Q12: What philosophy of living did Jagan say he hoped his son would emulate?
A) Accumulating wealth and living in luxury
B) Simple living and high thinking, as Gandhi taught
C) Following his father's path of running a successful business
D) Pursuing creative writing and artistic expression
Answer: B
Jagan said "I hope he will also emulate my philosophy of living. Simple living and high thinking, as Gandhi has taught us."
Q13: What did Jagan's cousin say about why Jagan ran his sweetmeat trade and accumulated wealth?
A) Jagan did it out of a sense of duty to provide for others
B) Jagan did it because he enjoyed the process of making money
C) Jagan did it to maintain his status and reputation in the community
D) Jagan did it because he was unable to follow Gandhi's teachings
Answer: A
The cousin said "It's not that, my dear fellow, Mine is the biggest sweetshop in the country. Have you any doubt about it?"
Q14: What did Jagan say about his refusal to use essences and flavorings in his sweets?
A) He did it to maintain the purity and quality of his products
B) He did it to keep costs down and maximize profits
C) He did it to differentiate his sweets from the competition
D) He did it to adhere to Gandhi's principles of simplicity
Answer: A
Jagan asserted "I'll never use them as long as I am the master of this establishment."
Q15: What did Jagan's cousin say about the "false and illusory" nature of using artificial flavorings?
A) He agreed with Jagan's stance and praised his commitment to purity
B) He criticized Jagan for being too rigid and unwilling to adapt
C) He argued that artificial flavorings were necessary for commercial success
D) He was indifferent to the issue and changed the subject
Answer: A
The cousin "expressed unqualified approval of this statement" about Jagan's refusal to use artificial flavorings.
Q16: How did Jagan feel when he looked through the keyhole and saw his son just sitting and brooding in his room?
A) He felt proud that his son was deep in thought about his writing
B) He felt disappointed that his son was not actively writing
C) He felt concerned that his son was depressed or unmotivated
D) He felt relieved that his son was taking a break from his writing
Answer: B
The passage states that Jagan "felt disappointed that the boy was not writing."
Q17: What did Jagan hope to see when he looked through the keyhole at his son's room?
A) He hoped to see his son furiously writing and creating
B) He hoped to see his son reading and studying his college books
C) He hoped to see his son resting and relaxing after a long day
D) He hoped to see his son planning out his writing in detail
Answer: A
The passage describes Jagan's imaginings, saying "He had imagined the writer burning the midnight oil and littering the table with sheets of paper in a delirium of inspiration."
Q18: What did Jagan tell his son when he finally went into his room to talk to him about his writing?
A) He scolded his son for not working hard enough on his writing
B) He offered to buy his son supplies and a better desk to support him
C) He demanded to know all the details about the story his son was working on
D) He expressed his full approval and said he liked his son's "idea" of being a writer
Answer: D
The passage states that Jagan told his son "Boy, I like your idea. Come on, let us talk about it."
Q19: How did Jagan's son react when his father said he was also "a kind of writer"?
A) He was excited and wanted to learn more about his father's writing
B) He was skeptical and didn't believe his father was actually a writer
C) He dismissed it and said his father didn't understand what real writing was
D) He asked his father for advice on how to become a successful writer
Answer: C
The son simply said "Father, you do not understand. I want to write something different."
Q20: What reason did Jagan's son give for cutting out the competition coupon from the library magazine?
A) He wanted to prove his cleverness to the librarian
B) He didn't have money to buy the magazine itself
C) He was worried the librarian wouldn't let him use it
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The passage indicates all of these were reasons the son gave for cutting out the coupon from the library magazine.
Q21: How did Jagan's son characterize his ordinary college friends who were just focused on getting degrees?
A) He said they were good friends who supported his writing
B) He said they were only readers and not good for anything else
C) He said they were misleading him and discouraging his writing
D) He said they were also aspiring writers like him
Answer: B
The son said "They are all ordinary fellows who are not good for anything else."
Q22: What was the specific writing competition that Jagan's son had seen in Ananda Vikatan magazine?
A) A poetry competition with a 25,000 rupee prize
B) A short story competition with a September 30th deadline
C) A novel competition with a 25,000 rupee prize and September 30th deadline
D) An essay competition with a coupon to fill out in the magazine
Answer: C
The passage states the details of the novel competition Jagan's son had seen in Ananda Vikatan.
Q23: What did Jagan's son say when his father kept asking about the story he was writing?
A) He became defensive and accused his father of examining him
B) He calmly explained the overall plot and themes of the story
C) He refused to share any details and said it might end up as a poem
D) He promised to show the story to his father once it was finished
Answer: A
The passage states the son "shrank away from him and repeated, 'Are you examining me?' in an ominous manner."
Q24: What reason did Jagan's son give for not wanting to show his story to anyone until it was finished?
A) He was worried his father wouldn't understand or approve of it
B) He wanted to keep it a surprise until the competition deadline
C) He felt his father was just examining him and didn't really care
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The passage indicates the son had multiple reasons for not wanting to share the details of his story with his father.
Q25: How did Jagan's cousin react when Jagan said he hoped his son would emulate his "philosophy of living"?
A) He agreed and said simple living and high thinking was the best approach
B) He challenged Jagan and said his son should pursue his own path
C) He was skeptical and didn't understand why Jagan ran a successful business
D) He ignored the comment and changed the subject to the use of artificial flavorings
Answer: C
The cousin said "What can I do? Moreover, I work, because it's one's duty to work." He then questioned why Jagan would "run a trade, make money, and accumulate it" if he believed in simple living.

mcqs.question: What was the reason Mali did not want to study anymore?
options: He was being bullied in college
He did not find his studies interesting
He wanted to get a job
He wanted to start his own business
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Mai said "I do not find it interesting, that's all" when explaining why he did not want to study anymore.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do for his son's meals?
options: He engaged a cook to prepare the meals
He cooked the meals himself
He sent his son to the college canteen for meals
He allowed his son to cook for himself
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan spent all his time cooking for his son, especially after his wife's death.

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan not want to mention college or class to his son?
options: He was afraid his son would get angry
He wanted his son to focus on his meals
He did not want his son to attend college
He was embarrassed about his son's studies
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan felt "afraid to mention class or college" as his son "might scream at the mention of the college or kick away his breakfast."

mcqs.question: What did Mai say about Jagan cooking for him?
options: He said he didn't want Jagan to cook for him anymore
He said he preferred the college canteen food
He said Jagan should engage a cook instead
He said Jagan's cooking was not good enough
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Mai said "I do not want you to cook for me hereafter."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan have an "almost maternal obsession" about his son's feeding?
options: He wanted to ensure his son ate a healthy diet
He enjoyed cooking for his son
It started after his wife was hospitalized
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text explains that Jagan's obsession with cooking for his son started after his wife's hospitalization, and that he spent all his time cooking for his son.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan tell his cousin when he arrived in the evening?
options: He wanted to discuss his son's refusal to study
He wanted his cousin to try the new sweets
He wanted his cousin to help with the shop
He wanted to discuss his wife's illness
mcqs.explanation: The text states that when Jagan's cousin arrived in the evening, Jagan "cried the moment he sighted him" to discuss his son's refusal to study.

mcqs.question: What was the material of the glass tile that the morning sun came through?
options: Stained glass
Crystal
Regular glass
Colored glass
mcqs.explanation: The text specifies that the "morning sun came through a glass tile", indicating it was made of regular glass.

mcqs.question: What was the dish that Jagan made for his son's breakfast?
options: Idli
Dosa
Uppumav
Vada
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions "a little heap of uppumav on his plate" as part of Mai's breakfast.

mcqs.question: What was the reaction of Mali when Jagan said he would speak to his college?
options: He looked up angrily
He smiled grimly
He kicked away his breakfast
He screamed at the mention of college
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "The boy looked up angrily" when Jagan said he would speak to his college.

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan end up sleeping at night after his discussions with his son?
options: In his son's room
In the kitchen
On the veranda
In his own room
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that after his discussions with his son, "he would spend a few moments staring at the door, then rise and unroll his mat in the open veranda in the second block and fall asleep."

mcqs.question: What was the reason given by Jagan for not engaging a cook in his sweetmeat shop?
options: They were specialists and technicians
He did not believe in engaging cooks
The shop was like a factory
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that when his son asked why he didn't engage cooks in the sweetmeat shop, Jagan replied "Oh, that's different. It's like a factory and they are specialists and technicians," indicating all the reasons given in the options.

mcqs.question: When did Jagan have a long conference with his son about his diet?
options: In the morning before breakfast
In the afternoon after lunch
In the evening before dinner
At night before retiring
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that "At night before retiring, he held a long conference with his son on not only what he had eaten during the day but what he would prefer to eat next day."

mcqs.question: What was Mai's reaction when Jagan asked where he would eat if he left college?
options: He smiled grimly
He got angry and yelled
He calmly explained his plans
He ignored the question
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "His son smiled grimly and replied, 'Why do you bother when you keep saying one need not eat?'"

mcqs.question: What did Mai do after telling Jagan he didn't want to study anymore?
options: He went to his room and locked the door
He left for college on his bicycle
He helped Jagan in the sweetmeat shop
He skipped his breakfast and left
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that after telling Jagan he didn't want to study anymore, "He put on his yellow shirt, picked up his bicycle, and was off."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin do when he first arrived?
options: He went straight to the kitchen to try the sweets
He sat down with Jagan to discuss his son's issues
He asked about Jagan's wife's health
He helped out in the sweetmeat shop
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan's cousin "wantedFirst of all to go through and try the sweets as they came out of the frying pan."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think would happen with his cousin in the kitchen?
options: He thought his cousin would get bored and leave soon
He thought his cousin would enjoy the sweets too much
He thought his cousin would get tired from the heat and smoke
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan thought "He is bound to come out sooner or later. No one can stay long in all that heat and smoke. Moreover, he will reach satiety soon with these sweets..."

mcqs.question: How did Mai describe Jagan's cooking when he said he didn't want Jagan to cook for him anymore?
options: He said Jagan's cooking was not good enough
He said the college canteen food was better
He said he could look after himself
He didn't provide any specific description
mcqs.explanation: The text does not mention Mai providing any specific description of Jagan's cooking when he said he didn't want Jagan to cook for him anymore.

mcqs.question: What was the reason given by Jagan for not engaging a cook even at home?
options: Food is similar to breathing, so one shouldn't engage a cook
He preferred to cook the meals himself
He didn't trust cooks to prepare the food properly
He couldn't afford to hire a cook
mcqs.explanation: When his son asked why he didn't engage a cook at home, Jagan replied "Do we engage a servant to do the breathing for us? Food is similar."

mcqs.question: What was the relationship between Jagan and his son described in the passage?
options: Distant and strained
Affectionate and caring
Argumentative and confrontational
Formal and professional
mcqs.explanation: The passage depicts an argumentative and confrontational relationship between Jagan and his son, with the son becoming "brusque and aggressive" in communicating with his father.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan react when Mai said he didn't want to study anymore?
options: He immediately agreed and supported his son's decision
He got angry and threatened to punish his son
He tried to understand his son's reasons and talked to him
He avoided the topic and changed the subject
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "merely repeated, 'If it's something I can do, tell me'" in response to Mai's statement that he didn't want to study anymore.

mcqs.question: What was the purpose of Jagan holding long conferences with his son about his diet?
options: To ensure his son was eating a healthy and balanced diet
To bond with his son and discuss his daily activities
To control and micromanage his son's eating habits
To prepare elaborate menus for his son's meals
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that Jagan's nightly conferences with his son about his diet were an "obsession" and a way for Jagan to "brood over the question night and day".

mcqs.question: How did Mai's behavior and demeanor change when he told Jagan he didn't want to study anymore?
options: He became more mature and serious
He got angry and confrontational
He remained calm and composed
He became playful and jovial
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Mai "had suddenly grown up" and "had never spoken to his father in this tone before", indicating a more mature and serious demeanor.

mcqs.question: What was the purpose of Jagan's cousin coming to visit him in the evening?
options: To try the new sweets being made in the shop
To discuss Mai's refusal to continue studying
To help Jagan with running the sweetmeat shop
To check on Jagan's wife's health
mcqs.explanation: The text clearly states that when Jagan's cousin arrived, Jagan "cried the moment he sighted him" in order to discuss his son's refusal to study.

mcqs.question: What was the significance of the "morning sun" coming through the glass tile and touching the "heap of uppumav" on Mai's plate?
options: It created a beautiful, sparkling effect on the food
It signified the start of a new day for the family
It distracted Jagan from the serious conversation
It emphasized the importance of the meal for Mai
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes how the "morning sun came through a glass tile and touched up with radiance the little heap of uppumav on his plate—a piece of green chili and some globules of oil made the stuff sparkle, catching Jagan's eye insistently for a moment".

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when Mai said he didn't want to study anymore?
options: He got angry and threatened to punish Mai
He calmly tried to understand Mai's reasons
He avoided the topic and changed the subject
He immediately agreed and supported Mai's decision
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "merely repeated, 'If it's something I can do, tell me'" in response to Mai's statement, indicating he tried to understand the situation. Set 2

mcqs.question: Why didn't Jagan give away free sweets to the children who looked at his shop display?
options: He didn't have enough money to provide free sweets
He believed the children's parents should buy them sweets
He didn't want to be seen as giving out charity
The shop's profits were too low to afford free sweets
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan felt "It's up to their parents to provide them with the money for sweets. I can't be handing out charity packets."

mcqs.question: What reason did Jagan give for not demanding that parents spend more money at his shop?
options: The parents were too poor to afford it
He didn't want to pressure the parents
He was worried about losing business
He felt the sweets were overpriced
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "Per capita income is three annas" and "Poor country! Most people cannot afford even rice for two meals a day."

mcqs.question: When Jagan's cousin emerged from the kitchen, what did Jagan say to him?
options: He asked the cousin to try the new sweets
He discussed his son's strange notions about not studying
He complained about the high cost of ingredients
He pondered how fortunate people were in their circumstances
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan said to his cousin, "Do you realize how few ever really understand how fortunate they are in their circumstances?"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say in response to Jagan's statement about young men being a problem?
options: He disagreed and said young men were the future
He sympathized and said educational methods were the issue
He changed the subject to the cost of ingredients
He said young men forget or get used to their circumstances
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "Especially young men, they are a problem everywhere. I was reading a little while ago somewhere"—and then stated "They all forget or get used to things; that's the way of the world."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's educational background according to the passage?
options: He had a B.A. degree
He had to leave college due to Gandhi's call for non-cooperation
He failed several times in the B.A. and became a private candidate
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage covers all these details about Jagan's educational background.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say he could have done if he had passed the B.A.?
options: He could have become a teacher
He could have had a better job
He could have done many other things
He could have opened a better sweetmeat shop
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "If I had passed the B.A., I could have done so many other things."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan's cousin want to find out what Mai was thinking?
options: He was genuinely concerned about Mai's wellbeing
He wanted to use it against Mai later
He thought the educational methods today were the issue
He was curious to understand Mai's strange notions
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "It'd be best to know what the boy is thinking, our educational methods being what they are today."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan ask his cousin to do regarding Mai's strange notions?
options: He asked the cousin to talk to Mai and find out more
He asked the cousin to come up with a solution
He asked the cousin to convince Mai to continue studying
He asked the cousin to report back to him that night
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan told his cousin "You must do something about it and tell me tonight."

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan and his cousin go to have their conversation at night?
options: They stayed in Jagan's house
They went to the college canteen
They went to the foot of the Lawley Statue
They went to Mai's room
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that they "strolled down the road to the foot of the Lawley Statue, and settled comfortably on the granite platform there."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan wish he had done regarding his son's room that night?
options: He wished he had knocked on the door
He wished he had peeped through the keyhole
He wished he had talked to his son directly
He wished he had left his son alone
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "wished you had peeped in—you'd have seen what he was doing," referring to his son's room.

mcqs.question: What detail did Jagan provide about the cost of ingredients for his sweets?
options: Sugar costs one and thirty per kilogram
Flour and butter cost thrice as much as sugar
Nutmegs cost seventy paise each
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage includes all these details about the high cost of ingredients for Jagan's sweets.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when he saw the school children looking at the display in his shop?
options: He felt happy that they were interested in his sweets
He felt guilty for not providing them free sweets
He felt indifferent and just watched them from his seat
He felt annoyed that they were blocking the display
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "watched them from his seat without emotion."

mcqs.question: What figure did Jagan cite regarding the per capita income in India?
options: Three annas
Eight annas
One rupee
Three rupees
mcqs.explanation: Jagan cited the figure of "per capita income is three annas" from a book he had read.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's cousin react when Jagan discussed the "strange notions" of his son?
options: He expressed concern and offered to talk to Mai
He criticized Mai and said he was being difficult
He agreed that young men were a problem everywhere
He assumed a "definite stand" and said he would look into it
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the cousin "suddenly assumed a definite stand and said, 'It'd be best to know what the boy is thinking, our educational methods being what they are today.'"

mcqs.question: What was the reason Jagan gave for not being able to afford providing free sweets to the children?
options: The shop's profits were too low
The ingredients were too expensive
He didn't have enough money
He believed it was the parents' responsibility
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "It's up to their parents to provide them with the money for sweets. I can't be handing out charity packets."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about young men being a "problem everywhere"?
options: He disagreed and said young men were the future
He sympathized and said educational methods were the issue
He changed the subject to the cost of ingredients
He said young men forget or get used to their circumstances
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "Especially young men, they are a problem everywhere. I was reading a little while ago somewhere"—and then stated "They all forget or get used to things; that's the way of the world."

mcqs.question: What was the reason Jagan gave for leaving college before completing his B.A.?
options: He had to attend to his sweetmeat shop
He was not performing well in his studies
Gandhi ordered them to non-cooperate
He could not afford the college fees
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "I had to leave the college when Gandhi ordered us to non-cooperate."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin mean when he said "The only person to whom I'm not a cousin"?
options: He considered Mai as his nephew
He had no familial relationship with Mai
He had a special bond with Mai as an uncle
Mai was the only one who didn't call him "cousin"
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the cousin said "The only person to whom I'm not a cousin," indicating that Mai was the only one who didn't address him as "cousin."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when his cousin suggested talking to Mai to find out his reasons?
options: He eagerly agreed and asked the cousin to do it
He refused and said he didn't want to interfere
He challenged the cousin to do it instead of him
He acknowledged it was a good idea but didn't act on it
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan said "Why don't you?" in a "tone of pointless challenge" when the cousin suggested talking to Mai.

mcqs.question: What detail did the passage provide about the Lawley Statue where Jagan and his cousin went?
options: It was located in the college campus
It was situated at the end of Matkee Road
It had Sir Frederick's head amidst the stars
It was made of granite and had a platform to sit on
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes them going "to the foot of the Lawley Statue, and settling comfortably on the granite platform there."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when he noticed the light was still on in Mai's room at night?
options: He went to check on Mai and see what he was doing
He resisted the impulse to peek through the keyhole
He knocked on Mai's door to talk to him
He assumed Mai was studying late and left him alone
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "resisted an impulse to peep through the keyhole" after noticing the light was still on in Mai's room.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say was the "basic qualification one should have"?
options: A B.A. degree
A high school diploma
A professional certification
Any college degree
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "I was always hoping that he'd be a graduate and that's the basic qualification one should have, don't you think so?"

mcqs.question: What was the reason given by Jagan's cousin for being cautious in criticizing Mai?
options: He didn't want to upset Jagan
He didn't want to anger Mai
He didn't know Mai well enough
He didn't want to undermine Jagan's authority
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the cousin was "ever a man of caution" in his response, indicating he was cautious about being critical of Mai.

mcqs.question: What detail was provided about the "cost of seasoning" for Jagan's sweets?
options: Nutmegs cost seventy paise each
Spices cost three times the price of sugar
Seasonings made up a significant portion of the costs
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage specifically mentions that "Nutmegs, seventy paise each—mark it, each!" as an example of the high cost of seasoning.

mcqs.question: What was the overall tone and mood conveyed in the passage?
options: Jagan was content and satisfied with his business
Jagan was frustrated and worried about his son's behavior
Jagan was introspective and philosophical about societal issues
Jagan was actively trying to find solutions to his son's problems
mcqs.explanation: The passage portrays Jagan as more focused on contemplating broader societal and economic issues, rather than being solely concerned with his son's situation. Set 3

mcqs.question: What did Jagan initially think his son was doing when he said he wanted to be a "writer"?
options: Counterfeiting money
Murdering someone
Becoming a clerk
Applying for a job in America
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that in Jagan's "dictionary" the word "writer" meant "only one thing—a 'clerk'—an Anglo-Indian, colonial term since the days when Macaulay had devised a system of education to provide a constant supply of clerical staff for the East India Company."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he learned his son wanted to be a "writer"?
options: He was proud and supportive of his son's ambition
He was shocked and thought it was a degrading idea
He was curious and wanted to know more about it
He was indifferent and didn't see it as a serious plan
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "felt aghast" and cried "It's degrading!" when he heard his son wanted to be a "writer".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about how Jagan had tried to shape his son into an "aristocrat"?
options: He thought Jagan was being too ambitious for his son
He agreed with Jagan's efforts to provide his son a good life
He said Jagan should have let his son pursue his own interests
He didn't comment on Jagan's efforts to shape his son's life
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the cousin noted Jagan was "trying to shape the boy into an aristocrat with a bicycle, college life, striped shirts, and everything".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son tell his friends at college about possibly going to America?
options: He said his father was sending him to America
He said he wanted to go to America to become a writer
He said he was leaving college to pursue his writing dreams
He didn't actually say anything about going to America
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan's son "had to tell them something before leaving the college" and said "My father has other plans—probably he is sending me to America."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he learned his son wanted to be a "writer"?
options: He was excited and supportive of his son's ambition
He was concerned that his son would become a clerk
He was relieved that his son didn't want to become a criminal
He was confused about what kind of "writer" his son meant
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "The truth finally dawned on Jagan. 'Oh, how stupid am I? Yes, of course, 'writer,' I know. I've become illiterate, I think,' he cried happily."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the possibility of his son becoming a famous writer?
options: He was doubtful and skeptical about his son's writing abilities
He was enthusiastic and encouraged Jagan to support his son
He said writers could earn a lot of money and become famous
He didn't have any specific opinions on his son's writing potential
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "I have heard that writers earn a lot of money nowadays, They become famous."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son do with his class books when the cousin met him?
options: He carefully put them away in his bag
He tore the pages of the books savagely
He gave the books to the cousin to take home
He left the books at the college before leaving
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan's son "had his class-books in his hand. [...] He suddenly tore up the pages of his books savagely, beckoned an attendant, and said, 'Put these in the fire in the kitchen.'"

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when he heard his son had torn up his class books?
options: He was proud that his son was rejecting his education
He scolded the cousin for not stopping his son's actions
He tried to explain to his son the importance of respecting books
He didn't have a strong reaction and let it pass without comment
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "cried, 'Could you not stop him? Didn't you tell him that books must be treated respectfully, being a form of the goddess Saraswathi? How could this boy ever pass his B.A.?'"

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's cousin respond when Jagan scolded him for not stopping his son from tearing up the books?
options: He apologized and said he should have intervened
He defended his inaction, saying it seemed appropriate
He changed the subject to avoid further criticism
He insisted that Jagan should have talked to his son directly
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "No. When he tore the books it seemed very appropriate, our education being what it is. . . ."

mcqs.question: What was the verse that Jagan's son composed after sending his books to the fire?
options: "Let us show gratitude to the Great Fire that consumes our horrid books"
"Down with the educational system and its oppressive books!"
"Burn the books, free the mind!"
"Books are shackles, fire is liberation"
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan's son "made up a verse on the spot: 'Let us show gratitude to the Great Fire that consumes our horrid books—' or something like it."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction to his son's verse and his gluttony at the restaurant?
options: He was disappointed and disapproving
He was amused and proud of his son's cleverness
He was concerned about his son's rejection of education
He was indifferent and didn't comment on it
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan was "gratified by his son's verse as well as his gluttony."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial concern when the cousin said his son wanted to be a "writer"?
options: That his son would become a clerk or colonial administrator
That his son would get involved in criminal activities
That his son would waste his time and not have a proper career
That his son would embarrass the family with his writing
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that in Jagan's "dictionary" the word "writer" meant "only one thing—a 'clerk'—an Anglo-Indian, colonial term".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the Ananda Bhavan restaurant that Jagan disliked?
options: The cousin said the restaurant had tried to blackmail Jagan
The cousin said the restaurant had a loud speaker that was deafening
The cousin said the restaurant served poor quality food
Both A and B
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the cousin mentioned both the restaurant's loud speaker and their attempt to "blackmail" Jagan with sales tax.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when his cousin mentioned the Ananda Bhavan restaurant?
options: He became angry and told the cousin to stop talking about it
He defended the restaurant and said there was nothing wrong with it
He asked the cousin to focus on what his son had said instead
He reminisced about his past issues with the restaurant
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "implored, 'I want to hear nothing about the Ananda Bhavan Restaurant. Tell me about the boy, please.'"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about his son's reaction to the word "college"?
options: His son was excited and happy to go to college
His son hated his lessons and syllabus at college
His son was indifferent and didn't have strong feelings about college
His son wanted to drop out of college and go to America
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "The very word 'college' drives him crazy, although you like it so much. He hates his lessons; he hates his syllabus and all his books. The very thought infuriates him."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say was the reason his son tore up his class books?
options: His son was frustrated with the poor quality of education
His son was rebelling against the rigid educational system
His son wanted to spite his father who valued education
His son was having a fit of anger and lost control
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "No. When he tore the books it seemed very appropriate, our education being what it is. . . ."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say his son did after tearing up his books?
options: He threw the torn pages away
He handed the books to the cousin
He asked the attendant to put the torn pages in the kitchen fire
He left the torn books on the table and walked away
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan's son "beckoned an attendant, and said, 'Put these in the fire in the kitchen.'"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say his son did after sending his books to the fire?
options: He left the restaurant without eating
He ate a lot of food and the bill was 3 rupees
He composed a verse praising the fire that burned his books
He told the cousin he was going to become a famous writer
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan's son "made up a verse on the spot: 'Let us show gratitude to the Great Fire that consumes our horrid books—' or something like it."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when he heard about his son's verse praising the fire that burned his books?
options: He was upset and scolded his son for disrespecting books
He was impressed and proud of his son's poetic abilities
He was confused and didn't understand the meaning of the verse
He ignored the verse and focused on his son's gluttony instead
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan was "gratified by his son's verse as well as his gluttony."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about his son's statement that his father was probably sending him to America?
options: He agreed that Jagan was planning to send his son to America
He said his son was just making up the statement to impress his friends
He advised Jagan not to take his son's statement seriously yet
He didn't have any opinion on what his son meant by that statement
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "Don't be hasty. He had to tell them something before leaving the college. Until he demands to be sent to America, don't take notice of it."

mcqs.question: What was the initial reason Jagan gave for not engaging a cook in his sweetmeat shop?
options: He believed food was similar to breathing and shouldn't be outsourced
He wanted to save money by not hiring a cook
He enjoyed cooking the sweets himself
He didn't trust cooks to prepare the sweets properly
mcqs.explanation: In the previous passage, Jagan had said "Do we engage a servant to do the breathing for us? Food is similar."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's concern about his son becoming a "writer"?
options: He was worried his son would become a clerk or colonial administrator
He was afraid his son would bring disgrace to the family
He thought being a writer was a degrading profession
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "felt aghast" and cried "It's degrading!" when he heard his son wanted to be a "writer".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the possibility of his son becoming a famous writer like Bharati or Tagore?
options: He was skeptical and didn't think his son had that potential
He encouraged Jagan to be open-minded and supportive
He said it was too early to judge and his son could achieve greatness
He changed the subject to avoid speculating about his son's future
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "Well, he may become a second Bharati or Tagore or Shakespeare some day. How can you judge now?"

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's immediate reaction when he realized his son meant "writer" in the creative sense, not as a clerk?
options: He became angry and scolded his son
He felt relieved and happy about his son's ambition
He remained skeptical and doubtful about his son's abilities
He didn't have a strong reaction and just wanted more details
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "cried happily. It was a great relief that the son was not attempting to be the other kind of writer."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about why he didn't try to stop his son from tearing up his books?
options: He didn't want to interfere and thought it was an appropriate reaction
He was afraid his son would get angry if he tried to stop him
He didn't think it was a big deal since the books were going to be burned
He assumed Jagan would handle the situation better than he could
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "It didn't occur to me to argue with him, that's all; what use would it be anyway?" Set 4

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel he needed to forgo his son's college education and focus on his writing dreams?
options: He realized his son was unhappy with college and wanted to support him
He wanted his son to become a famous writer like Kalidasa
He hoped his son's writing would bring the family status and respect
He was worried his son would get into trouble if he stayed in college
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "realized that the time had come for him to forget college education and get completely identified with Mali's fantasies, at least until he came out of his gloom."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do when he saw the light on in his son's room at night?
options: He knocked on the door and demanded to know what his son was doing
He peeked through the keyhole to see what his son was up to
He waited until morning to speak to his son about his activities
He left his son alone and did not interfere with his nighttime routine
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "Through the keyhole he saw the light burning in Malli's room."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan imagine his son would be doing as a writer, based on the story of Kalidasa?
options: Jagan imagined his son "burning the midnight oil and littering the table with sheets of paper in a delirium of inspiration"
Jagan imagined his son composing a great poem that would be on everyone's lips for a thousand years
Jagan imagined his son would suddenly burst into inspired song like Kalidasa
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes Jagan's various imaginings about how his son would write as a great poet, inspired like Kalidasa.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son react when Jagan said he liked his "idea" of becoming a writer?
options: He was excited and grateful for his father's support
He remained doubtful and suspicious of his father's intentions
He explained his writing plans in detail to his father
He dismissed his father's interest and changed the subject
mcqs.explanation: The passage states the son "followed him mutely, his misgivings not totally gone."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan offer to provide for his son to support his writing?
options: A new desk with many drawers
White paper and a good pen
A separate room for his writing
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage lists all of these items that Jagan offered to get for his son to support his writing.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son respond when Jagan asked what story he was writing?
options: He explained the plot in detail
He said it might turn out to be a poem instead
He refused to share any details about his writing
He asked Jagan if he was examining him
mcqs.explanation: The son responded "Are you examining me?" when Jagan asked about the story he was writing.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say about his friends in relation to being writers?
options: His friends were also aspiring writers
His friends were just ordinary people focused on getting degrees
His friends were misleading him and encouraging his writing dreams
His friends were supportive of his writing ambitions
mcqs.explanation: The son said "They are all ordinary fellows who are not good for anything else."

mcqs.question: What was the reason Jagan's son gave for not wanting to share his story with anyone?
options: He was still developing the story and didn't want feedback
He was worried his father wouldn't understand or approve
He wanted to keep it a surprise until the competition deadline
He felt his father was just examining him and didn't really care
mcqs.explanation: The son said "I am not the sort to show my story to anyone before I finish it."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say he had seen about a writing competition in Ananda Vikatan magazine?
options: They would pay 25,000 rupees for the best novel
The deadline to submit was September 30th
He needed to fill out a coupon in the magazine
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage states all of these details about the writing competition that Jagan's son had seen.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son react when Jagan kept asking questions about the story he was writing?
options: He became defensive and accused Jagan of examining him
He calmly explained the details of the story he was working on
He avoided answering and changed the subject to something else
He got angry and told Jagan to stop interfering in his writing
mcqs.explanation: The passage says the son "shrank away from him and repeated, 'Are you examining me?' in an ominous manner."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when he realized his son wanted to be a writer, not a clerk?
options: He was disappointed and tried to convince his son to go to college
He was relieved and enthusiastic about supporting his son's writing
He was skeptical and didn't believe his son had the talent to be a writer
He was indifferent and didn't see it as a serious career option for his son
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "cried happily. It was a great relief that the son was not attempting to be the other kind of writer."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel about the invisible barrier between him and his son?
options: He was frustrated and wanted to break through it
He was indifferent and didn't see it as an issue
He blamed his son for creating the barrier
He accepted it and didn't try to change the situation
mcqs.explanation: The passage says "Secretly his mind was bothered as to why there was always an invisible barrier between them."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do to try and make up with his son and understand his writing dreams?
options: He left his son alone and gave him space to focus on his writing
He engaged a cook to prepare meals so he could spend more time with his son
He applied his eye to the keyhole to observe his son's activities in private
He beat upon his son's door and invited him to discuss his writing plans
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes how Jagan "beat upon the door with both fists" and then told his son "Boy, I like your idea. Come on, let us talk about it."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say when Jagan asked if his friends were also writers?
options: His friends were all aspiring writers like him
His friends were ordinary people just focused on getting degrees
His friends were misleading him and encouraging his writing dreams
His friends were very supportive of his writing ambitions
mcqs.explanation: The son said "They are all ordinary fellows who are not good for anything else."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son respond when Jagan offered to buy him writing supplies like paper and a desk?
options: He was grateful and excited by the offer
He remained doubtful and suspicious of his father's intentions
He dismissed the offer and said he didn't need any help
He demanded more expensive or elaborate supplies
mcqs.explanation: The passage states the son was "poised between doubt and trust" when Jagan made these offers.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he realized his son wanted to be a "writer" rather than a clerk?
options: He was proud and supportive of his son's creative ambition
He was concerned that being a writer was a degrading profession
He was confused and didn't understand what kind of writer his son meant
He was angry and tried to convince his son to pursue a more respectable career
mcqs.explanation: The passage states "The truth finally dawned on Jagan. 'Oh, how stupid am I? Yes, of course, 'writer,' I know.'"

mcqs.question: What was the reason Jagan's cousin gave for why Kalidasa was able to become a great poet without going to college?
options: Kalidasa was blessed by the goddess Saraswathi
Kalidasa was naturally gifted and didn't need formal education
There were no colleges in India 3000 years ago when Kalidasa lived
Both A and B
mcqs.explanation: The passage includes both of these reasons given by Jagan's cousin.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say about the relationship between his writing and his college studies?
options: He said the two were completely separate and non-interfering
He said his writing conflicted with and interfered with his studies
He said his writing would supplement and enhance his studies
He didn't directly address the relationship between the two
mcqs.explanation: The son said "the one interfered with the other" when explaining why he was tearing up his college books.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son characterize his ordinary friends who were just focused on getting degrees?
options: He said they were good-for-nothing fellows
He said they were misleading him and encouraging his writing
He said they were supportive of his writing ambitions
He said they were also aspiring writers like him
mcqs.explanation: The son said his friends "are all ordinary fellows who are not good for anything else."

mcqs.question: What was the specific writing competition that Jagan's son had seen in Ananda Vikatan magazine?
options: A poetry competition with a 25,000 rupee prize
A short story competition with a September 30th deadline
A novel competition with a 25,000 rupee prize and September 30th deadline
An essay competition with a coupon to fill out in the magazine
mcqs.explanation: The passage states the details of the novel competition Jagan's son had seen in Ananda Vikatan.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son react when Jagan kept asking questions about the story he was writing?
options: He became increasingly open and shared more details
He avoided answering and changed the subject
He got angry and accused Jagan of examining him
He explained the overall plot and themes of the story
mcqs.explanation: The passage says the son "shrank away from him and repeated, 'Are you examining me?' in an ominous manner."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan imagine his son would be like as a writer, based on the story of Kalidasa?
options: He imagined his son composing inspired poetry that would be famous for centuries
He imagined his son burning the midnight oil and furiously writing pages of manuscript
He imagined his son suddenly bursting into inspired song like Kalidasa
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes Jagan having all of these imaginings about how his son would write as a great poet.

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan's son say he couldn't tell his father the story he was writing?
options: He was worried his father wouldn't understand or approve of it
He wanted to keep it a surprise until the competition deadline
He felt his father was just examining him and didn't really care
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage indicates the son had multiple reasons for not wanting to share the details of his story with his father.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do to try and show his son he was supportive of his writing dreams?
options: He bought his son expensive writing supplies and a new desk
He left his son alone and didn't interfere with his nighttime activities
He beat on his son's door and invited him to discuss his writing plans
He praised his son's verse about burning the college books
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes how Jagan "beat upon the door with both fists" and then told his son "Boy, I like your idea. Come on, let us talk about it."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel about the "invisible barrier" that existed between him and his son?
options: He was indifferent and didn't see it as a problem
He was frustrated and wanted to break through it
He blamed his son for creating and maintaining the barrier
He accepted its existence and didn't try to change the situation
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "Secretly his mind was bothered as to why there was always an invisible barrier between them." Set 5

mcqs.question: What was the rare type of brain tumor that Jagan's wife had, according to the doctor?
options: Benign growth
Malignant growth
Inoperable tumor
The doctor didn't specify the type
mcqs.explanation: The passage states the doctor said it was "a very rare type of brain tumour" and that "Nature would sooner see us dead. She has no use for a brain affected by malignant growth."

mcqs.question: What did the doctor tell Jagan to do when he left to go to his car?
options: To go back and be with his wife in her final hours
To publish his book on nature cure as soon as possible
To take his son Mali with him to protect him
To call another doctor for a second opinion
mcqs.explanation: The doctor told Jagan "Go back, go back to your wife for the few hours left. Your son is watching us. Protect him."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan react when the doctor told him about his wife's terminal condition?
options: He remained calm and composed
He broke down and wailed loudly
He argued with the doctor about nature cure
He rushed to his wife's bedside immediately
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "at the boy's question, Jagan lost his nerve completely, held his son's hands, and broke into a loud wail."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son Mali react when he saw his father crying and wailing?
options: He comforted and consoled his father
He watched his father with a look of dismay and puzzlement
He ran out of the house to be with his friends
He blamed his father for his mother's condition
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Mali "had shaken himself off and watched his father from a distance with a look of dismay and puzzlement."

mcqs.question: What was the effect of Jagan's reaction to his wife's illness on his relationship with his son?
options: It brought them closer together
It created an invisible barrier between them
It made his son resent him
It had no long-term impact on their relationship
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "From that day, the barrier had come into being. The boy had ceased to speak to him normally."

mcqs.question: What story about a black monkey did Jagan used to tell his son at night?
options: A story from the Panchatantra
A story he had read in a book
A story he had made up himself
The passage does not provide any details about the story
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that "The boy showed no sign that he remembered those days or wanted to be reminded of them. He showed no reaction."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say about wanting to write something different from what his father had written?
options: He wanted to write a novel instead of stories
He wanted to write something more profound and meaningful
He wanted to write something that would shock and challenge his father
He wanted to write something completely unrelated to his father's work
mcqs.explanation: The son said "Father, you do not understand. I want to write something different."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son obtain the coupon from the Ananda Vikatan magazine for the writing competition?
options: He bought a copy of the magazine
He carefully cut it out from the library copy
He asked the librarian for the coupon
He downloaded it online from the magazine's website
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that the son "had cut out the coupon from the magazine on his college library table, risking punishment and humiliation if caught. 'I did it with a blade, under the very nose of the librarian,' the boy said with a hint of laughter."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when his son told him he had cut out the coupon from the library magazine?
options: He was proud of his son's resourcefulness
He was concerned that his son had broken the rules
He thought his son should have just bought the magazine
He didn't have a strong reaction and just focused on the competition
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "If this is from Vikatan you could have bought a copy for four annas, or as many copies as you needed."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say about wanting to "teach that librarian a lesson"?
options: He was angry at the librarian for not allowing him to use the library
He wanted to get back at the librarian for being too strict
He felt the librarian thought he was too clever and needed to be humbled
He was joking and didn't actually have any ill will towards the librarian
mcqs.explanation: The son said he had "always wanted to teach that librarian a lesson; he always thought he was too clever."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan react when he told the head cook that his son was writing a book?
options: He boasted about his son's genius and earning potential
He was humble and downplayed his son's writing ambitions
He asked the cook for advice on how to support his son
He was nervous and worried about his son's unconventional path
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "summoned him to his throne and said, 'My son is writing a book.' The head cook...evinced interest in the literary progress of Mali. 'He is going to earn twenty-five thousand rupees out of it, and he says he is going to finish it before September, wonderful boy!'"

mcqs.question: What philosophy of living did Jagan say he hoped his son would emulate?
options: Accumulating wealth and living in luxury
Simple living and high thinking, as Gandhi taught
Following his father's path of running a successful business
Pursuing creative writing and artistic expression
mcqs.explanation: Jagan said "I hope he will also emulate my philosophy of living. Simple living and high thinking, as Gandhi has taught us."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about why Jagan ran his sweetmeat trade and accumulated wealth?
options: Jagan did it out of a sense of duty to provide for others
Jagan did it because he enjoyed the process of making money
Jagan did it to maintain his status and reputation in the community
Jagan did it because he was unable to follow Gandhi's teachings
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "It's not that, my dear fellow, Mine is the biggest sweetshop in the country. Have you any doubt about it?"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about his refusal to use essences and flavorings in his sweets?
options: He did it to maintain the purity and quality of his products
He did it to keep costs down and maximize profits
He did it to differentiate his sweets from the competition
He did it to adhere to Gandhi's principles of simplicity
mcqs.explanation: Jagan asserted "I'll never use them as long as I am the master of this establishment."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the "false and illusory" nature of using artificial flavorings?
options: He agreed with Jagan's stance and praised his commitment to purity
He criticized Jagan for being too rigid and unwilling to adapt
He argued that artificial flavorings were necessary for commercial success
He was indifferent to the issue and changed the subject
mcqs.explanation: The cousin "expressed unqualified approval of this statement" about Jagan's refusal to use artificial flavorings.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel when he looked through the keyhole and saw his son just sitting and brooding in his room?
options: He felt proud that his son was deep in thought about his writing
He felt disappointed that his son was not actively writing
He felt concerned that his son was depressed or unmotivated
He felt relieved that his son was taking a break from his writing
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan "felt disappointed that the boy was not writing."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan hope to see when he looked through the keyhole at his son's room?
options: He hoped to see his son furiously writing and creating
He hoped to see his son reading and studying his college books
He hoped to see his son resting and relaxing after a long day
He hoped to see his son planning out his writing in detail
mcqs.explanation: The passage describes Jagan's imaginings, saying "He had imagined the writer burning the midnight oil and littering the table with sheets of paper in a delirium of inspiration."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan tell his son when he finally went into his room to talk to him about his writing?
options: He scolded his son for not working hard enough on his writing
He offered to buy his son supplies and a better desk to support him
He demanded to know all the details about the story his son was working on
He expressed his full approval and said he liked his son's "idea" of being a writer
mcqs.explanation: The passage states that Jagan told his son "Boy, I like your idea. Come on, let us talk about it."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son react when his father said he was also "a kind of writer"?
options: He was excited and wanted to learn more about his father's writing
He was skeptical and didn't believe his father was actually a writer
He dismissed it and said his father didn't understand what real writing was
He asked his father for advice on how to become a successful writer
mcqs.explanation: The son simply said "Father, you do not understand. I want to write something different."

mcqs.question: What reason did Jagan's son give for cutting out the competition coupon from the library magazine?
options: He wanted to prove his cleverness to the librarian
He didn't have money to buy the magazine itself
He was worried the librarian wouldn't let him use it
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage indicates all of these were reasons the son gave for cutting out the coupon from the library magazine.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's son characterize his ordinary college friends who were just focused on getting degrees?
options: He said they were good friends who supported his writing
He said they were only readers and not good for anything else
He said they were misleading him and discouraging his writing
He said they were also aspiring writers like him
mcqs.explanation: The son said "They are all ordinary fellows who are not good for anything else."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's son say when his father kept asking about the story he was writing?
options: He became defensive and accused his father of examining him
He calmly explained the overall plot and themes of the story
He refused to share any details and said it might end up as a poem
He promised to show the story to his father once it was finished
mcqs.explanation: The passage states the son "shrank away from him and repeated, 'Are you examining me?' in an ominous manner."

He wanted to keep it a surprise until the competition deadline
He felt his father was just examining him and didn't really care
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The passage indicates the son had multiple reasons for not wanting to share the details of his story with his father.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's cousin react when Jagan said he hoped his son would emulate his "philosophy of living"?
options: He agreed and said simple living and high thinking was the best approach
He challenged Jagan and said his son should pursue his own path
He was skeptical and didn't understand why Jagan ran a successful business
He ignored the comment and changed the subject to the use of artificial flavorings
mcqs.explanation: The cousin said "What can I do? Moreover, I work, because it's one's duty to work." He then questioned why Jagan would "run a trade, make money, and accumulate it" if he believed in simple living.

C) He was proud
D) He was concerned
Answer: C
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan "felt gratified that his son was pursuing a fresh course, all his own."
Q3: What was the word that "intoxicated" Jagan and "explained everything" for him?
A) Meditation
B) Philosophy
C) Service
D) Freedom
Answer: C
Explanation: The text states that the word "service" "intoxicated him, sent a thrill through his whole being, and explained everything" for Jagan.

B) The subject matter of his writing
C) His experience and knowledge to be a writer
D) All of the above
Answer: D
Explanation: The text mentions Jagan's concerns about the language Mali was writing in, the type of content he was writing (stories, poems, philosophy), and his equipment/experience to be a writer.

A) They argued frequently
B) They had open conversations
C) They were distant and detached
D) They had a close relationship
Answer: C
Explanation: The text states that Mali "seemed to have become detached, more detached than ever" and that the "only link between them was the five-rupee currency note."

A) At home
B) At the Ananda Bhavan restaurant
C) At a friend's place
D) At a café

He was worried about Mali's safety and well-being
Both B and C
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "felt shocked for a moment" and also said "Without my permission or help, without telling me anything? I thought he was in his room."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan justify his non-interference in Mali's decision to end his education?
options: He believed in allowing Mali to develop independently
He thought Mali had lost interest in his studies
He was disappointed that Mali had given up his education
He didn't have a clear justification for his non-interference
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan said he "left him free" because he believed "Perhaps he wants to educate himself in the school of life."

mcqs.question: According to the cousin, what were some of the details that Mali had worked out for his trip to America?
options: He had arranged for a loan to finance the trip
He had made arrangements for his American clothes
He had secured a recommendation from Jagan's friend
Both B and C
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that the cousin said "He is getting his American clothes made in Madras" and "The librarian has a brother in the aeroplane company and he has done everything for Mali."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he heard that Mali wanted to go to America?

He was indifferent and didn't care either way
He was furious and thought it was a bad idea
He was skeptical but open to discussing it

mcqs.question: How did Jagan justify his decision to not interfere with Mali's education?

He thought Mali had lost interest in his studies
He was disappointed that Mali had given up his education
He didn't have a clear justification for his non-interference
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan said he "left him free" because he believed "Perhaps he wants to educate himself in the school of life."

mcqs.question: What was the cousin's reaction when Jagan suggested trying to stop Mali from going to America?

He was indifferent and believed Mali had made up his mind
He actively undermined Jagan's efforts and enjoyed his predicament

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's plan for the cash he had saved in the loft?
