To invest it in a business venture
To transfer it to a safer location in the puja room
To keep it hidden and untouched
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "considered transferring it all, in due course, to a casket behind the family Gods in the puja room."

content.value: # Chapter 5
# Set 1
Q1: What made Jagan feel superior?
A) His daily routine
B) His son being in America
C) His discussions about weather and politics
D) His visits to the Truth Printing Works
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan felt superior because his son was in America, which seemed worth all the money and separation.
Q2: How did Jagan react when he received his son's airmail letter?
A) With disappointment
B) With indifference
C) With joy, almost as if his son had come back
D) With confusion about the contents
Answer: C
Ex- When the airmail letter arrived after days of waiting, Jagan felt almost the same joy as if his son had come back.
Q3: What did Jagan's son Mali mention in his letter that slightly disturbed Jagan?
A) The tall buildings in New York
B) The thousands of motor cars in the street
C) The difficulty with food
D) Going to school rather than college
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan was somewhat disturbed at Mali's mention of "school" rather than "college" in the letter.
Q4: How long did Jagan spend reading and re-reading his son's letter?
A) A few minutes
B) Nearly an hour
C) The whole morning
D) The entire day
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan sat on the hall bench and pored over Mali's letter for nearly an hour, scanning every word.
Q5: Who did Jagan first share the good news of his son's letter with?
A) The chemist
B) The adjournment lawyer
C) Nataraj at the Truth Printing Works
D) A dozen random people on the street
Answer: C
Ex- The first place Jagan went to share the news was the Truth Printing Works, where he told Nataraj.
Q6: What was Nataraj doing when Jagan entered the Truth Printing Works?
A) Talking to visitors
B) Looking at proofs at his desk
C) Arguing with an employee
D) Taking a nap
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan entered, Nataraj was at his desk, looking up from his proofs and smiling at the visitor.
Q7: According to Jagan, why wouldn't his son waste money on sending a telegram?
A) He didn't have enough money
B) He was too busy to send one
C) He was prudent and a letter cost much less
D) Telegrams were not allowed from America
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan said his son was prudent and wouldn't waste ten rupees on a telegram when a ten cent letter would suffice.
Q8: How much did Jagan think a cent was worth in Indian currency?
A) Around four rupees
B) Exactly seven rupees
C) Jagan couldn't calculate the exact amount
D) A hundred rupees
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan tried to calculate the exchange rate but gave up the attempt at multiplication and division.
Q9: What did Jagan hope regarding his son's room in America?
A) That it would be on the ground floor and not too high up
B) That it would have a nice view
C) That it would be spacious and well-furnished
D) That it would be close to his school
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan hoped Mali would have a room on the ground floor in America and not too high up in the tall buildings.
Q10: How did Nataraj respond to Jagan's news about his son?
A) He was indifferent and uninterested
B) He said American boys are very clever and can take care of themselves anywhere
C) He warned Jagan about the dangers in America
D) He asked for more details about Mali's arrival
Answer: B
Ex- Nataraj agreed that Indian boys like Mali are very clever and can take care of themselves anywhere in the world.
Q11: Who did Jagan meet on his way to the shop after leaving the Truth Printing Works?
A) The chemist
B) The postman
C) The adjournment lawyer
D) A dozen acquaintances
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan caught a glimpse of the adjournment lawyer at the turning of Kabir Lane while heading to his shop.
Q12: What was the adjournment lawyer's initial reaction when Jagan stopped him?
A) He was happy to chat with Jagan
B) He said he had to go home as some parties were waiting for him
C) He asked about Jagan's son in America
D) He ignored Jagan and kept walking
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan stopped him, the lawyer said he had to go home as some parties were waiting for him.
Q13: How did Jagan know the adjournment lawyer?
A) They were neighbors
B) They had been classmates at the Albert Mission
C) They worked together at Jagan's shop
D) They had met recently at the court
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan and the lawyer had been classmates at the Albert Mission more than a generation ago.
Q14: What annoyed Jagan about people's reactions to his son's letter?
A) Their lack of interest in the news
B) Their obsession with wanting to know if Mali had sent a telegram
C) Their criticism of Mali's decision to go to America
D) Their doubts about the letter's authenticity
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan felt annoyed at people's tendency to get obsessed with telegrams when he mentioned Mali's letter.
Q15: How long did the adjournment lawyer think it took for a letter to reach from America?
A) Four days
B) A week
C) Ten days
D) At least fifteen days
Answer: D
Ex- The lawyer said Jagan must be mistaken and that it takes at least fifteen days for a letter to come from America.
Q16: What was Jagan's reaction to the lawyer's statement about the letter's travel time?
A) He agreed that he may have been mistaken
B) He thought the lawyer was presumptuous to talk about America
C) He provided evidence to prove his point
D) He changed the topic of discussion
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan thought it was presumptuous of the lawyer to talk of America when he was there to provide first-hand information.
Q17: Who did Jagan meet next on his way to the shop?
A) The postman
B) Nataraj
C) The adjournment lawyer
D) The chemist
Answer: D
Ex- Ahead of the lawyer, Jagan saw the chemist at his door, looking down the street.
Q18: How did the chemist greet Jagan?
A) With a lot of friendliness
B) In a hurried and disinterested manner
C) With surprise at seeing Jagan late
D) With questions about his son
Answer: A
Ex- The chemist greeted Jagan warmly and with a lot of friendliness.
Q19: What did the chemist inquire about first?
A) The postage cost to America
B) Jagan's son's safe arrival in America
C) The reason for Jagan being late
D) The contents of Mali's letter
Answer: C
Ex- The chemist first asked Jagan if he was rather late today.
Q20: Why did Jagan say he was late to the shop that day?
A) He had overslept
B) He was waiting for the postman who arrived late
C) He had been busy reading his son's letter
D) He got stuck in traffic on the way
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan told the chemist he was late because the postman had arrived rather late that day.
Q21: What was Jagan's response to the chemist's question about Mali reaching America safely?
A) He scolded the chemist for asking
B) He said he had been anxious for two or three days
C) He refused to share any information
D) He showed the chemist Mali's letter
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan said he was somewhat anxious for two or three days regarding his son reaching America safely.
Q22: According to Jagan, what would other boys have done upon reaching America?
A) Wasted money on a telegram
B) Written a long, detailed letter
C) Called their parents immediately
D) Waited for a few weeks before contacting home
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan said other boys would have wasted money on sending a telegram upon reaching America, but his son was prudent.
Q23: What did the chemist want to send for from America?
A) Some medicines
B) A free catalogue from Sears Roebuck
C) A letter to his relatives
D) Some chemicals for his shop
Answer: B
Ex- The chemist wanted to send for a free catalogue from Sears Roebuck in America.
Q24: Why did the chemist want the Sears Roebuck catalogue?
A) To order some products for his shop
B) To get wonderful ideas on all sorts of things
C) To compare prices with Indian markets
D) To gift it to Jagan for his son
Answer: B
Ex- The chemist found the Sears Roebuck catalogue interesting as it would give wonderful ideas on all sorts of things.
Q25: What made Jagan almost groan during his conversation with the chemist?
A) The chemist's lack of interest in his son
B) The chemist asking him about the postage cost to America
C) The chemist's ignorance about America
D) The chemist's continuous questions
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan almost groaned when the chemist asked him the equivalent cost of fifty cents, which was the postage for the catalogue.
# Set 2
Q1: Who did Jagan consider the best listener to his news about Mali?
A) The head cook
B) The chemist
C) The adjournment lawyer
D) His cousin
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan felt his cousin was the best listener and deserved all the sweets he ate for his listening capacity.
Q2: What did Jagan think about other people in the town regarding America?
A) They were well-informed
B) They were interested in learning more
C) They were obsessed with their own notions and resisted enlightenment
D) They were eager to share their own experiences
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan thought all the others in the town were obsessed with their own notions, were ignorant, and resisted enlightenment on the subject of America.
Q3: What did Jagan tell the head cook about America?
A) It's a small country with few cars
B) It's a huge country with a lot of motor cars and everyone has a car
C) It's a country with many tall buildings but no cars
D) It's a country with a lot of universities
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan told the cook that America is a huge country with a lot of motor cars and everyone has a car there.
Q4: How did the head cook react to Jagan's news about Mali?
A) He asked about telegrams and the equivalent of a cent
B) He listened respectfully and turned away without comment
C) He showed great enthusiasm and asked for more details
D) He seemed disinterested and changed the topic
Answer: B
Ex- The cook listened respectfully to Jagan's news and turned away without any comment.
Q5: What did Jagan show his cousin as a special favor?
A) A photograph of Mali in America
B) A map of America
C) A fragment of Mali's airmail letter
D) An American coin
Answer: C
Ex- As a special favor, Jagan afforded his cousin a glimpse of a fragment of Mali's airmail letter.
Q6: What did Jagan's cousin suggest he should do after hearing about Mali's safe arrival?
A) Offer a couple of coconuts to Ganesha at the corner temple
B) Throw a party to celebrate
C) Call Mali and congratulate him
D) Send Mali some Indian sweets
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan's cousin suggested that he must offer a couple of coconuts to Ganesha at the corner temple.
Q7: How did Jagan respond to his cousin's suggestion about offering coconuts to Ganesha?
A) He refused, saying it was unnecessary
B) He agreed, as if there was a specific contract between him and God about Mali's safety
C) He said he would think about it
D) He laughed it off as a joke
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan agreed to the suggestion, as if there were a specific contract between himself and God in the matter of his son's safety.
Q8: Who offered to buy the coconut for the offering?
A) Jagan
B) Jagan's cousin
C) The head cook
D) The chemist
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan's cousin offered to buy the coconut for the offering on his way.
Q9: How did Jagan feel after receiving Mali's letter?
A) Worried and anxious
B) Indifferent and unaffected
C) A great burden off his head
D) Disappointed with the content
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan felt a great burden off his head after receiving Mali's letter confirming his safe arrival.
Q10: What was Jagan's main concern about Mali in America?
A) The quality of education
B) The cost of living
C) Walking carefully in the streets
D) Making friends and connections
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan hoped that Mali would walk carefully in the streets, amidst the many tall buildings and cars everywhere.
Q11: How did Jagan describe America based on Mali's letters?
A) A country of poverty and struggle
B) A country of millionaires where everyone is rich
C) A country of great natural beauty
D) A country of hard-working immigrants
Answer: B
Ex- Based on Mali's letters, Jagan said America is a country of millionaires and everyone is so rich.
Q12: What did Jagan consider doing with Mali's letters?
A) Burning them after reading
B) Hiding them in a safe place
C) Binding them into a neat volume at Truth Printing
D) Sending them back to Mali with his comments
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan considered binding Mali's letters into a neat volume at Truth Printing if only Mali had left proper margins in his epistles.
Q13: How did Jagan's reading habits change after receiving Mali's letters?
A) He stopped reading altogether
B) He started reading more books about America
C) His reading of the Bhagavad Gita was replaced by the blue airmail letters
D) He lost interest in reading and focused on his business
Answer: C
Ex- Gradually, Jagan's reading of the Bhagavad Gita was replaced by Mali's blue airmail letters.
Q14: What did Jagan do with Mali's letters when he went out?
A) Left them at home for safekeeping
B) Carried them in his jibba pocket for reading to others
C) Mailed them to relatives to share the news
D) Kept them in his shop drawer
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan stuffed his jibba pocket with Mali's letters and pulled them out for choice reading of passages to all and sundry.
Q15: Who was the most patient listener to Jagan's readings from Mali's letters?
A) The head cook
B) The chemist
C) Jagan's cousin
D) Nataraj from Truth Printing
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan's cousin remained an uncomplaining listener as Jagan read passages from Mali's letters.
Q16: What did Jagan's acquaintances fear about his behavior?
A) That he was becoming forgetful
B) That he was losing interest in his business
C) That he was afflicted with the talking disease
D) That he was planning to move to America
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan's acquaintances feared that he was afflicted with the talking disease as he constantly spoke about America.
Q17: How did Jagan react when he saw a familiar face on the road?
A) He avoided them and walked away
B) He greeted them and continued on his way
C) He scanned the landscape and pounced on them to talk about America
D) He pretended not to see them
Answer: C
Ex- From the minute he stepped out of his house, Jagan scanned the landscape for a familiar face, pounced on the unwary victim, and held him enthralled with talk of America.
Q18: What did Jagan do when he stopped a vagrant on the culvert?
A) Gave him some food and money
B) Asked him for directions
C) Described the Grand Canyon to him
D) Invited him to his house for a meal
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan stopped the vagrant on the culvert one day in order to describe the Grand Canyon to him.
Q19: How much did Jagan give the vagrant for listening to him?
A) Five rupees
B) Ten paise
C) Five paise
D) Nothing
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan gave the vagrant five paise for listening to his description of the Grand Canyon.
Q20: How did people generally react when Jagan spoke to them about America?
A) They listened with great interest
B) They seemed restless and tried to slip away
C) They asked him many questions
D) They shared their own experiences
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan found everyone restless when he spoke, but he rushed through his narration breathlessly.
Q21: What did Jagan resist when his cousin wanted to see Mali's letters?
A) Letting his cousin touch the letters
B) Reading the letters aloud to his cousin
C) Sharing any information from the letters
D) Allowing his cousin to keep the letters
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan resisted the idea of allowing his cousin to touch Mali's letters, which he held in sacred trust.
Q22: What did Jagan's cousin do with the information he gathered from Mali's letters?
A) Kept it to himself
B) Shared it with Jagan's acquaintances
C) Wrote his own letters to Mali
D) Passed it on to his own circle of listeners
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan's cousin collected information on American life and manners from Mali's letters and passed them on to his own circle of listeners.
Q23: What did most people in Malgudi soon know about America from Jagan and his cousin?
A) The number of human lives lost in road accidents every year
B) The popular tourist destinations
C) The best universities for higher education
D) The average income of an American family
Answer: A
Ex- Most people in Malgudi soon knew that fifty thousand human lives were lost in road accidents every year in America.
Q24: What significant event in American history did Jagan describe as if he had witnessed it himself?
A) The assassination of Abraham Lincoln
B) The attack on Pearl Harbor
C) The moon landing
D) The assassination of John F. Kennedy
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan felt quite competent to describe, as if he had watched it himself, the events related to the assassination of John F. Kennedy.
Q25: What detail did Jagan not spare his listeners while recounting Kennedy's assassination?
A) The name of the assassin
B) The type of gun used
C) The exact time of the assassination
D) Oswald's death later
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan did not spare his listeners any detail of Oswald's death after he had described the events of Kennedy's assassination.
# Set 3
Q1: Which letter from Mali did Jagan rigorously suppress?
A) The one about Mali's arrival in America
B) The one about Mali's decision to eat beef
C) The one about Mali's marriage to Grace
D) The one about Mali's request for money
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan suppressed the letter in which Mali wrote about taking to eating beef in America.
Q2: What did Mali suggest India should do instead of begging for food from America?
A) Increase agricultural production
B) Import more food from other countries
C) Slaughter useless cows that wander in the streets
D) Distribute food more efficiently
Answer: C
Ex- Mali suggested that India should slaughter useless cows that wander in the streets and block traffic, instead of begging for food from America.
Q3: According to the shastras, what headed the list of the five deadly sins?
A) Stealing
B) Lying
C) Killing a cow
D) Adultery
Answer: C
Ex- According to the shastras, the killing of a cow headed the list of the five deadly sins.
Q4: How did Jagan plan to respond to Mali's letter about eating beef?
A) By ignoring it completely
B) By writing a letter incorporating quotations from the shastras and Gandhi's writings on the cow
C) By calling Mali and expressing his disapproval
D) By asking his cousin to intervene and advise Mali
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan planned to write a letter to Mali, incorporating quotations from the shastras and Gandhi's writings on the cow, to make his feelings felt on the subject.
Q5: What did Jagan receive from Mali one morning, while he was still contemplating his response to the beef letter?
A) Another letter with more details about American food
B) A package containing American souvenirs
C) A cable announcing Mali's arrival home with another person
D) A phone call from Mali asking for his blessing
Answer: C
Ex- While Jagan was still thinking about how to respond to the beef letter, he received a cable from Mali announcing his arrival home with another person.
Q6: Why was Jagan unable to talk to his cousin about the cable announcing Mali's arrival with another person?
A) His cousin was out of town
B) He feared his cousin might spread the news all over town
C) He wanted to keep it a secret from everyone
D) He didn't trust his cousin's advice
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan couldn't talk to his cousin about the cable because he feared his cousin might spread the news of "another person" all over town.
Q7: What filled Jagan with uneasiness and a feeling of inferiority when Mali arrived at the railway station?
A) Mali's foreign accent and mannerisms
B) Mali's expensive clothing and accessories
C) The sight of the streamlined suitcases and corded cartons
D) Mali's lack of respect towards him
Answer: C
Ex- The very sight of the streamlined suitcases and corded cartons that Mali brought with him filled Jagan with uneasiness and a feeling of inferiority.
Q8: How did the old porter at the railway station react to the quantity of Mali's baggage?
A) He refused to carry it, saying it was too much
B) He could hardly handle it, although normally he would carry scores of boxes and baskets without a thought
C) He demanded extra payment for carrying the baggage
D) He called for a trolley to transport the baggage
Answer: B
Ex- The old porter could hardly handle the quantity of Mali's baggage, although normally he would seize and carry scores of boxes and baskets without a thought.
Q9: Whom did the old porter call for assistance with Mali's baggage?
A) Jagan and his cousin
B) Other porters at the station
C) The station master
D) The boy at the cigarette shop
Answer: D
Ex- The old porter had to call in the boy at the cigarette shop for assistance with Mali's baggage.
Q10: What did Mali mutter about his baggage without moving his head or lips too much?
A) "I don't need help carrying it"
B) "Be careful, it's very heavy"
C) "Be careful, awful lot of things that might break; have spent a fortune in airfreight"
D) "Don't touch my belongings"
Answer: C
Ex- Mali muttered, "Be careful, awful lot of things that might break. Have spent a fortune in airfreight," without moving his head or lips too much.
Q11: How did Mali's appearance change during his time in America?
A) He seemed to have grown taller, broader, and fairer
B) He looked thinner and paler
C) He had grown a beard and mustache
D) He looked exactly the same as before
Answer: A
Ex- Mali seemed to have grown taller, broader, and fairer during his time in America.
Q12: What did Mali wear when he arrived at the railway station?
A) A traditional Indian outfit
B) A dark suit with an overcoat
C) Casual jeans and a t-shirt
D) A business suit and tie
Answer: B
Ex- Mali wore a dark suit with an overcoat when he arrived at the railway station.
Q13: How did Jagan feel when he saw Mali approaching him at the railway station?
A) Excited and eager to embrace him
B) Proud of his son's accomplishments
C) As if he was following a stranger
D) Relieved to see him safe and sound
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan felt that he was following a stranger when he saw Mali approaching him at the railway station.
Q14: What did Jagan try to do when Mali extended his hand to greet him?
A) Shake his hand firmly
B) Embrace him warmly
C) Shrink away and shield himself behind his cousin
D) Offer him a traditional Indian welcome
Answer: C
Ex- When Mali extended his hand to greet him, Jagan tried to shrink away and shield himself behind his cousin.
Q15: What did Jagan struggle with when he had to speak to Mali?
A) Finding the right words to express his emotions
B) Understanding Mali's American accent
C) Restraining himself from calling Mali "sir" and employing the honorific plural
D) Remembering Mali's childhood nicknames
Answer: C
Ex- When he had to speak to his son, Jagan had difficulty restraining himself from calling Mali "sir" and employing the honorific plural.
Q16: Who did Mali introduce to Jagan as his wife?
A) An American woman named Grace
B) A Japanese woman named Sakura
C) A Chinese woman named Mei
D) An Indian woman named Priya
Answer: A
Ex- Mali introduced Grace to Jagan, saying, "This is Grace. We are married."
Q17: What was Jagan's initial reaction to Mali's announcement of his marriage to Grace?
A) Complete confusion and disbelief
B) Anger and disapproval
C) Joy and excitement
D) Indifference and apathy
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan's initial reaction to Mali's announcement of his marriage to Grace was complete confusion, wondering when they were married and why Mali didn't inform him.
Q18: What did Jagan think about Grace's appearance when he first saw her?
A) She looked like an American
B) She looked like a Chinese or Japanese
C) She looked like a traditional Indian bride
D) He couldn't tell her ethnicity
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan thought Grace looked like a Chinese, and then wondered if she might be Japanese, unsure how to find out without asking indiscreet questions.
Q19: What recent event made Jagan think it was inappropriate for Mali to marry a Chinese person?
A) The Indo-China war
B) The Cultural Revolution in China
C) The Chinese invasion of Indian borders
D) The establishment of diplomatic relations between India and China
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan thought one couldn't marry a Chinese nowadays because they had invaded Indian borders.
Q20: What did Jagan do after introducing Grace and Mali, feeling panicked?
A) He welcomed Grace warmly into the family
B) He asked Mali about their wedding ceremony
C) He threw a panicky look at his cousin and fled on the pretext of supervising the loading of the baggage
D) He invited everyone to a celebratory dinner
Answer: C
Ex- Feeling panicked, Jagan threw a look at his cousin and fled on the pretext of supervising the loading of the baggage into Gaffur's taxi.
Q21: How did the small crowd at the railway station react to Mali's arrival?
A) They ignored him and went about their business
B) They followed Mali and Grace to the car, murmuring, "He's come from America"
C) They asked for his autograph and took pictures with him
D) They welcomed him with garlands and sweets
Answer: B
Ex- A small gaping crowd followed Mali and Grace to the car, murmuring, "He's come from America."
Q22: What did Mali say to Gaffur about his taxi?
A) "I'll buy you a new one"
B) "Jalopy going strong?"
C) "Let me drive it"
D) "It needs a new paint job"
Answer: B
Ex- Mali took notice of Gaffur by saying, "Jalopy going strong?"
Q23: Where did Jagan and his cousin sit in the taxi?
A) In the back seat with Mali and Grace
B) In the front seat with Gaffur
C) In a separate car
D) On the roof of the taxi
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan and his cousin sat with Gaffur in the front seat, leaving the back for Grace and Mali.
Q24: What did Mali say when Gaffur asked him why he didn't bring a car?
A) "I don't know how to drive"
B) "I prefer riding in taxis"
C) "Wish you had told me; oh, I sold my Pontiac before leaving"
D) "I'll buy a car in India"
Answer: C
Ex- When Gaffur asked Mali why he didn't bring a car, Mali said, "Wish you had told me; oh, I sold my Pontiac before leaving."
Q25: What did Grace find charming during the taxi ride?
A) The streets and bazaars
B) The people and their traditional attire
C) The cows and other animals on the road
D) The ancient temples and monuments
Answer: A
Ex- During the taxi ride, Grace gazed with fascination at the streets and bazaars and cried, "Oh, charming! Charming! Charming!"
# Set 4
Q1: How did Grace react to Jagan's offer to get her anything she wanted?
A) She was offended by his suggestion
B) She ignored his offer and remained silent
C) She was genuinely pleased with his attention
D) She asked for a specific item from his shop
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "Oh, how kind of you!" and was genuinely pleased with Jagan's attention.
Q2: What did Grace do when Jagan said he was a very active man?
A) She asked him to tell her more about his active lifestyle
B) She drew a chair for him and asked him to be seated
C) She seemed disinterested in his statement
D) She asked him to demonstrate his active nature
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan mentioned he was a very active man, Grace drew a chair for him and said, "Please be seated yourself; you must be tired."
Q3: Why did Jagan cut short his sentence about the secret of human energy?
A) He realized he was running late for his shop
B) He noticed a slight bewilderment in Grace's face
C) He heard Mali calling for him from the bathroom
D) He suddenly felt tired and needed to sit down
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan cut short his sentence about the secret of human energy when he noticed a slight bewilderment in Grace's face.
Q4: What did Jagan do after Grace told him to go and attend to his work?
A) He stayed and continued the conversation
B) He asked her to accompany him to the shop
C) He cried from the passage, "Make yourself comfortable," and hurried out
D) He waited for Mali to come out of the bathroom
Answer: C
Ex- After Grace told him to attend to his work, Jagan cried from the passage, "Make yourself comfortable," and hurried out while Mali was still in the bathroom.
Q5: Why did Jagan start avoiding people after Mali's return?
A) He was too busy with his work at the shop
B) He was afraid people would inquire about his daughter-in-law
C) He didn't want to discuss Mali's future plans
D) He was upset with Mali for marrying a foreigner
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan's anxiety was that people like the lawyer or the printer would stop him in the street to inquire about his daughter-in-law, so he began avoiding them.
Q6: How did Jagan's behavior change towards his cousin after Mali's return?
A) He became more talkative and shared every detail about Mali
B) He grew unwilling to talk about his son and had great stretches of silence
C) He asked his cousin to move in with them to help with the family
D) He started arguing with his cousin about Mali's choices
Answer: B
Ex- Even Jagan's cousin found great stretches of silence when they met, as Jagan had grown unwilling to talk about his son.
Q7: What did Jagan's cousin want to know about Grace?
A) Her educational qualifications
B) Her family background and caste
C) Her cooking skills and favorite dishes
D) Her plans for the future
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan's cousin was dying to know who that casteless girl at home was.
Q8: How did Jagan respond to his cousin's indirect question about Mali's dietary preferences?
A) He provided a detailed description of Mali's daily meals
B) He said he doesn't pry into what another person eats or drinks
C) He admitted that Mali and Grace cook and eat meat at home
D) He changed the subject to avoid answering the question
Answer: B
Ex- When the cousin indirectly asked if Mali still likes coffee or asks for tea, Jagan said, "What another person eats or drinks never interests me; why should I pry into it?"
Q9: What did Jagan say about his duty towards Mali and Grace's food preferences?
A) He would cook whatever they liked and ensure they were happy
B) He could only provide what he was used to, and if they didn't like it, they could eat elsewhere
C) He would learn to cook European dishes to accommodate their tastes
D) He would ask Grace to teach him her favorite recipes
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan said he could only provide what he was used to, and if Mali and Grace didn't like it, they could go and eat where they pleased.
Q10: According to Jagan, where is the limit of one's duty well defined?
A) In the Indian Constitution
B) In the teachings of Mahatma Gandhi
C) In the Bhagavad Gita
D) In the laws of karma
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan said that even in the Bhagavad Gita, the limit of one's duty is well defined.
Q11: Why did Jagan's cousin change the subject from the Bhagavad Gita?
A) He found the topic boring and irrelevant
B) He had agreed with so much of the Gita day after day that he felt weary of it
C) He wanted to discuss Mali's future plans instead
D) He had to leave for an urgent appointment
Answer: B
Ex- The cousin changed the subject because he had agreed with so much of the Gita day after day that he felt weary of it.
Q12: According to the cousin, what did Jagan's return to quoting the Bhagavad Gita indicate?
A) Jagan was becoming more spiritual and detached
B) Jagan was trying to impress others with his knowledge
C) Jagan was becoming mentally disturbed once again
D) Jagan was preparing to renounce worldly life
Answer: C
Ex- The cousin felt that Jagan's return to quoting the Gita showed he was becoming mentally disturbed once again.
Q13: How did Mali converse with his old friends who came to meet him?
A) He spoke loudly and enthusiastically, sharing every detail of his life
B) He seated them in the hall and conversed in low tones, as became a gentleman
C) He took them out to restaurants and clubs to catch up
D) He avoided meeting them altogether, asking Grace to make excuses
Answer: B
Ex- When Mali's old friends came to meet him, he seated them in the hall and conversed in low tones, as became a gentleman.
Q14: What did Jagan suspect Mali was describing to his friends?
A) His academic achievements and career plans
B) His love story and marriage with Grace
C) The Grand Canyon, the Niagara, the Statue of Liberty, and traffic jams in New York
D) His political views and opinions on world affairs
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan thought Mali was perhaps describing the Grand Canyon, the Niagara, the Statue of Liberty, and the traffic jams in New York to his friends.
Q15: Why didn't Jagan join in the conversations between Mali and his friends?
A) He was not interested in their topics of discussion
B) He felt it might seem presumptuous unless he was invited
C) He disapproved of Mali's friends and wanted to avoid them
D) He was too busy with his own work to spare the time
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan felt it might seem presumptuous to join Mali's conversations with his friends unless he was invited.
Q16: What did Grace give Jagan as a gift from Mali?
A) A set of American novels
B) A pale yellow casket containing spoons, forks, and knives
C) A gold-plated wristwatch
D) A leather briefcase for his documents
Answer: B
Ex- Grace pressed a pale yellow casket containing spoons, forks, and knives into Jagan's hands, saying, "Father, this is for you."
Q17: What was Jagan's reaction to the gift from Mali and Grace?
A) He was thrilled and started using it immediately
B) He wondered how one ever used it and locked it up in his almirah
C) He politely declined the gift, saying he had no use for it
D) He asked Grace to teach him how to use it properly
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan received the picnic hamper from Mali and Grace, he wondered how one ever used it and locked it up in his almirah.
Q18: What did Mali wear at home after returning from America?
A) Traditional Indian attire like kurtas and dhotis
B) A pair of dark trousers over a white shirt, always with his feet in slippers
C) Formal suits and ties, even while relaxing
D) Casual jeans and t-shirts with sneakers
Answer: B
Ex- At home, Mali never wore a dhoti but a pair of dark trousers over a white shirt, and always had his feet in slippers.
Q19: How often did Mali leave his room or visit other parts of the house?
A) He spent most of his time exploring the house and garden
B) He seldom left his room or visited any other part of the house
C) He regularly spent time with Jagan in the puja room
D) He was constantly in and out of the house, meeting friends and relatives
Answer: B
Ex- Mali seldom left his room or visited any other part of the house after returning from America.
Q20: When did Mali usually go out of the house, and how did he dress?
A) He went out every morning in casual clothes to jog and exercise
B) He went out in the afternoons in formal attire to attend business meetings
C) He went out in the evenings in traditional Indian clothes to visit temples
D) He waited for darkness to descend on the town and then dressed elaborately in socks, shoes, jacket, and tie
Answer: D
Ex- Mali seldom went out, but if he did, he waited for darkness and then dressed elaborately in socks, shoes, jacket, and tie.
Q21: How did Mali carry himself when he went out with Grace?
A) He walked humbly, trying to blend in with the locals
B) He carried himself like a celebrity avoiding the attention of the rabble
C) He stopped to greet and chat with everyone he knew
D) He seemed nervous and uncomfortable in his new surroundings
Answer: B
Ex- When Mali stepped out with Grace, he carried himself like a celebrity avoiding the attention of the rabble.
Q22: What did Grace do one morning that surprised Jagan?
A) She cooked a lavish American breakfast for the family
B) She parted the mustard-coloured curtain dividing the house and tidied Jagan's quarters
C) She asked Jagan to teach her how to pray in the puja room
D) She invited Mali's friends over for a party without informing Jagan
Answer: B
Ex- One morning, Grace parted the mustard-coloured curtain which divided the house into two sections and tidied up Jagan's quarters.
Q23: How did Jagan feel when Grace started helping with the household chores?
A) He was relieved and grateful for her assistance
B) He was not used to being helped and felt uneasy
C) He was angry and told her to stop immediately
D) He was indifferent and continued with his own routine
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan was not used to being helped and felt uneasy while Grace tidied his room, washed vessels, and swept the floor.
Q24: What did Grace say when Jagan protested against her doing household work?
A) "I'm only doing this because Mali asked me to"
B) "I don't like to work, but I have no choice"
C) "I must not forget that I'm an Indian daughter-in-law"
D) "I'm just trying to impress you with my skills"
Answer: C
Ex- When Jagan protested against her doing household work, Grace said, "I must not forget that I'm an Indian daughter-in-law."
Q25: How did Grace react to Jagan's concern about what people would think of her doing household chores?
A) She agreed and stopped immediately
B) She said it's not Mali's business, as he is writing letters and she is doing the house
C) She started crying and complained about Jagan's attitude
D) She called Mali and asked him to intervene
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan expressed concern about what people would think of Grace doing household work, she said, "It's not his business anyway. He is writing letters, and I'm doing the house; that's all."
# Set 5
Q1: What habit had Jagan gotten into regarding his departure from home?
A) Leaving early to avoid Grace
B) Waiting for Grace before leaving
C) Sneaking out without informing anyone
D) Asking Mali for permission to leave
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan had gotten into the habit of waiting for Grace before leaving home.
Q2: What did Jagan appreciate about Grace's presence in the house?
A) The delicious meals she cooked
B) The intelligent conversations she had with him
C) The extreme air of orderliness that her feminine touch imparted
D) The way she decorated the house with flowers
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan was getting used to the extreme air of orderliness that Grace's feminine touch imparted to the surroundings.
Q3: What did Grace wish to do for Jagan one day?
A) Cook for him
B) Teach him American customs
C) Take him shopping for new clothes
D) Introduce him to her friends
Answer: A
Ex- One day, Grace said to Jagan, "I wish you would let me cook for you."
Q4: Why did Jagan refuse Grace's offer to cook for him?
A) He disliked her cooking
B) He was under a vow to eat only what he could cook with his own hands
C) He was fasting for religious reasons
D) He had already eaten before she offered
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan explained to Grace that he was under a vow to eat only what he could cook with his own hands.
Q5: How did Grace react to Jagan's explanation of his eating habits?
A) She found it strange and amusing
B) She was disappointed and upset
C) She said he sounded thrilling
D) She tried to convince him to change his ways
Answer: C
Ex- When Jagan explained his eating habits, Grace cried, "Oh, you sound thrilling!"
Q6: What did Jagan think was unique about Grace's reaction to his habits?
A) It was the first time someone had a good word to say about them
B) It was the most enthusiastic response he had ever received
C) It was the only time someone had fully understood his reasons
D) It was the last reaction he had expected from an American
Answer: A
Ex- Grace's enthusiasm was the first time someone had a good word to say about Jagan's habits.
Q7: What did Jagan expatiate on, encouraged by Grace's enthusiasm?
A) His travels around the world
B) His political views and opinions
C) His own creations of salt-free and sugar-free food
D) His experiences during the Indian independence movement
Answer: C
Ex- Encouraged by Grace's enthusiasm, Jagan expatiated on his own creations of salt-free and sugar-free food.
Q8: What did Jagan say Grace should look forward to?
A) Trying his salt-free and sugar-free recipes
B) Meeting his friends and relatives
C) Visiting his sweet shop and seeing how it operates
D) Reading his book when Truth Printing published it
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan concluded by saying that Grace should really look forward to reading his book when Truth Printing let it out of the press.
Q9: How did Grace respond to Jagan's mention of his book?
A) She said she had already read it
B) She seemed disinterested and changed the subject
C) She said ecstatically, "I'm sure it's going to be a bestseller"
D) She asked him to give her a copy as soon as possible
Answer: C
Ex- When Jagan mentioned his book, Grace said ecstatically, "I'm sure it's going to be a bestseller."
Q10: What did Jagan inquire about Mali, feeling very awkward?
A) If he had finished his studies and acquired a degree in America
B) If he was planning to stay in India permanently
C) If he had found a job in America
D) If he was happy with his marriage to Grace
Answer: A
Ex- Feeling very awkward, Jagan inquired if Mali had finished his studies and acquired a degree in America.
Q11: How did Grace react to Jagan's question about Mali's education?
A) She refused to answer and said it was none of his business
B) She seemed surprised and asked, "Why, didn't you know?"
C) She immediately told him all the details of Mali's qualifications
D) She said she would ask Mali to tell him directly
Answer: B
Ex- When Jagan asked about Mali's education, Grace looked up from a vessel she was scrubbing and asked, "Why, didn't you know?"
Q12: What did Jagan feel he must do after Grace's response to his question?
A) Admit that he had no idea about Mali's plans
B) Scold Mali for not keeping him informed
C) Cover up his relationship with his son and not betray the actual state of affairs
D) Ask Grace to leave the house and let him talk to Mali privately
Answer: C
Ex- After Grace's response, Jagan felt that he must cover up his relationship with his son and not betray the actual state of affairs.
Q13: What did Grace say Mali should have done regarding his education?
A) He should have continued studying in India
B) He should have chosen a different subject to study
C) He should have informed Jagan about his plans
D) He should have invited Jagan to his graduation ceremony
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "Still I say that Mali should have told you. Suppose I ask him to speak to you about it; it is pretty important, you know."
Q14: Why did Grace think it was important for Mali to talk to Jagan?
A) To seek his blessings for their marriage
B) To ask for financial support
C) To plan his future career
D) To apologize for not contacting him earlier
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "Unless he talks to you, what can he plan, really?" implying that it was important for Mali to discuss his future plans with Jagan.
Q15: What did Jagan say he had learned from Mali's letters?
A) Details about Mali's personal life
B) Information about Mali's academic achievements
C) A great deal about America
D) Nothing of significance
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan said, "I only learnt a great deal about your country from them," referring to Mali's letters from America.
Q16: How did Grace react to Jagan's statement about learning from Mali's letters?
A) She became angry and defensive
B) She seemed confused and asked for clarification
C) She rose to her feet with a peal of laughter
D) She ignored the comment and changed the subject
Answer: C
Ex- At Jagan's statement, Grace rose to her feet with a peal of laughter.
Q17: What did Grace ask Jagan to bring her?
A) A map of America
B) Mali's educational certificates
C) One of Mali's letters from America
D) Photos of Mali's life in America
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "Oh, oh, Father, Father, get me one of the letters and I will tell you something."
Q18: Where had Jagan kept Mali's letters?
A) In a locked safe
B) In a cardboard box in his favourite cupboard
C) In Mali's room
D) At his shop
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan went to his favourite cupboard and took out a cardboard box in which all the blue letters had been neatly treasured.
Q19: What was Jagan hesitant about when Grace asked for Mali's letters?
A) Letting anyone touch the valuable documents
B) Revealing the contents of the letters to Grace
C) Admitting that he had kept the letters
D) Allowing Grace to take the letters away
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan was hesitant about letting anyone touch Mali's letters, which he considered valuable documents.
Q20: What did Grace point out to Jagan in one of the letters?
A) Mali's description of his university
B) Details of Mali's wedding to Grace
C) The signature at the end, which read "GM"
D) A photograph of Mali and Grace together
Answer: C
Ex- Grace pulled out a letter at random and pointed to the signature at the end, which read "GM".
Q21: What did "GM" stand for in the letters?
A) Good Morning
B) Grace and Mali
C) God's Message
D) Greetings from Mali
Answer: B
Ex- Grace explained that "GM" stood for "Grace and Mali, that's me and him."
Q22: Who had composed the letters signed "GM"?
A) Mali
B) Jagan
C) Grace
D) Mali and Grace together
Answer: C
Ex- Grace revealed that she had composed all the letters signed "GM", though both she and Mali signed them.
Q23: How did Jagan react to the revelation that Grace had written the letters?
A) He was angry and felt betrayed
B) He was relieved and thanked Grace
C) He gulped down his saliva in awkwardness
D) He laughed and said he had known all along
Answer: C
Ex- When Grace said she had written the letters, Jagan gulped down the saliva in his awkwardness.
Q24: What did Jagan say when Grace asked if Mali had ever written to him himself?
A) He admitted that Mali had never written to him
B) He said Mali had written to him, but he did not know the letters were Grace's
C) He refused to answer the question
D) He said Mali had called him instead of writing
Answer: B

Ex- When Grace asked if Mali had ever written to Jagan himself, Jagan silently prayed to Gandhi's spirit to forgive the lie he was about to utter and said, "Yes, yes; but I did not know these letters were yours."
Q25: Why did Jagan think Mali was taking up a very difficult line?
A) By deciding to marry Grace
B) By choosing to study in America
C) By not communicating with his father
D) By wanting to be a writer
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan said, "Words after all convey so little; that's why I thought he was taking up a very difficult line when he said he wanted to be a writer."
# Set 6
Q1: What did Jagan say about Margaret's, the school Grace mentioned?
A) He had studied there himself
B) He had never heard of it
C) He thought it must be a good place
D) He knew someone who attended it
Answer: C
Ex- Out of his habit of picking up tidbits of American information and building on them, Jagan said Margaret's "must be a good place".
Q2: Where did Grace study domestic science?
A) At Margaret's
B) In New Jersey
C) At Michigan
D) In Korea
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said she "studied domestic science at Michigan".
Q3: Where did Grace meet Mali?
A) At a football game in Michigan
B) In a creative writing class
C) At a party in New Jersey
D) Through mutual friends
Answer: A
Ex- Grace met Mali when "he came there for his creative writing course. We sat side by side at a football game".
Q4: What did Grace ask Jagan about football games?
A) If he enjoyed watching them
B) If they have such things in India
C) If he had ever played football
D) If he knew the rules of the game
Answer: B
Ex- After mentioning the football games in Michigan, Grace asked Jagan, "do you have such things here?"
Q5: What did Jagan say about football in India?
A) It is not played in India
B) Only professional teams play it
C) All the schoolboys play it
D) It is a new sport in India
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan replied, "Yes, yes, we have football too. All the schoolboys play it."
Q6: What excuse did Jagan give when Grace said she thought Mali must have written to him about football?
A) He had been too busy to read Mali's letters
B) He had forgotten what Mali wrote
C) Sometimes letters get lost
D) Mali had not mentioned football in his letters
Answer: C
Ex- When Grace said she thought Mali must have written to Jagan about football, Jagan said, "Yes, yes, but you know sometimes letters get lost."
Q7: What did Grace suddenly ask Jagan?
A) If he was happy
B) If he liked her
C) If he approved of their marriage
D) If he would visit them in America
Answer: A
Ex- Grace suddenly asked Jagan, "You are happy, aren't you?"
Q8: What had Grace heard so much about in India that made her afraid to come?
A) The hot weather
B) The poverty
C) The caste system
D) The spicy food
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "I had heard so much about the caste system in this country. I was afraid to come here."
Q9: When did Grace shake with fear about being accepted?
A) When she first met Mali
B) When she arrived in India
C) When she first saw Jagan and his family at the railway station
D) When she entered Jagan's house
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "when I first saw you all at the railway station I shook with fear, I thought I might not be accepted."
Q10: What did Grace say was very courageous of Mali?
A) Studying in America
B) Marrying her
C) Bringing her to meet his family
D) Choosing to be a writer
Answer: C
Ex- Grace said, "It was very courageous of him to bring me here."
Q11: According to Jagan, who fought for the abolition of the caste system?
A) Jawaharlal Nehru
B) Rabindranath Tagore
C) Gandhi
D) Sardar Patel
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan said, "Gandhi fought for its abolition," referring to the caste system.
Q12: How did Jagan respond when Grace asked if the caste system was gone now?
A) He said it was completely abolished
B) He admitted it still existed in some parts of India
C) He said it was going and they don't think of it nowadays
D) He avoided answering the question directly
Answer: C
Ex- When Grace asked if the caste system was gone now, Jagan said, "It's going, we don't think of it nowadays."
Q13: What did Mali suddenly ask Jagan to get for the house?
A) A television
B) A telephone
C) A car
D) A computer
Answer: B
Ex- Mali suddenly dashed into Jagan's presence one day to ask, "Can't you get a telephone for the house?"
Q14: What was Jagan's initial response to Mali's request for a telephone?
A) He agreed immediately
B) He said he would think about it
C) He said he had not thought of it
D) He refused outright
Answer: C
Ex- When Mali asked for a telephone, Jagan said, "I've not thought of it."
Q15: According to Mali, how would a telephone help Jagan's business?
A) People could order by telephone
B) Jagan could advertise his shop
C) Jagan could communicate with suppliers more easily
D) Jagan could expand his business to other cities
Answer: A
Ex- Mali said, "Even in your business, if you had a telephone, more business would flow in. People might order by telephone."
Q16: What did Mali say he felt because he could not give his associates a telephone number?
A) Angry
B) Disappointed
C) Embarrassed
D) Confused
Answer: C
Ex- Mali said, "I felt embarrassed because I could not give my associates a telephone number."
Q17: What did Jagan want to say about his daily sales without a telephone?
A) They were decreasing steadily
B) They were the same as always
C) They were increasing rapidly
D) They were such and such, showing that when one wants sweets, one doesn't wait for a telephone
Answer: D
Ex- Jagan wanted to reply, "My daily sale is such and such even without a telephone, which shows that when one wants to eat sweets one doesn't wait for a telephone."
Q18: Whom did Mali call to join the discussion about business?
A) His friend
B) The shop assistant
C) Grace
D) The telephone company representative
Answer: C
Ex- Mali called, "Grace! Will you join us? We are discussing business now."
Q19: How did Jagan feel about the prospect of a business discussion with Mali?
A) Excited and eager
B) Nervous and apprehensive
C) Bored and disinterested
D) Angry and resentful
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan was seized with a cold dread at the prospect of a business discussion with Mali, although pleased that after all Mali was going to talk to him.
Q20: Where did Mali suggest they adjourn to for the discussion?
A) The shop
B) The kitchen
C) The hall
D) Mali's room
Answer: C
Ex- Mali suggested, "Father, let us adjourn to the hall. We have chairs there."
Q21: How had Grace transformed the hall?
A) With new furniture and appliances
B) With curtains, mats, tablecloth, and modern paintings
C) By knocking down walls to create more space
D) By changing the color scheme and lighting
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan noticed how Grace had transformed the hall with curtains, mats, tablecloth, and a couple of modern paintings on the walls.
Q22: What did Jagan find bewildering but say "Yes" to when Grace asked if they were marvelous?
A) The bamboo chairs with colored cushions
B) The modern paintings on the walls
C) The vase with margosa leaves
D) The new curtains
Answer: B
Ex- Jagan found the modern paintings bewildering, but said, "Yes," when Grace asked, "Aren't they marvellous?"
Q23: According to Jagan, what is margosa called in the Vedas?
A) The holy leaf
B) The king of herbs
C) The ambrosia
D) The nectar of immortality
Answer: C

Q24: What did Jagan say about the benefits of margosa leaves?
A) They are a natural antiseptic and purify the blood
B) They cure all diseases
C) They bring good luck and prosperity
D) They enhance mental clarity and focus
Answer: A
Ex- Jagan said, "It is a natural antiseptic, purifies the blood, supplies iron," when speaking of margosa leaves.
Q25: What did Jagan notice about Mali's appearance when observing his face at close quarters?
A) He looked healthier and more energetic
B) He had gained weight and looked well-fed
C) The freshness and glow of foreignness were gone; he looked a shade below par
D) He had grown a beard and mustache
Answer: C
Ex- Jagan noticed that the freshness and glow of foreignness that Mali had possessed when he arrived were gone; he looked even a shade below par.
