The text states that Jagan "girt himself for the task by tying his upper cloth around his head and tucking up his dhoti in a businesslike manner."
Q2: What did Jagan do after they reached the top of the steps with the stone?
A) He carefully placed the stone down
B) He asked the bearded man to take over
C) He let go of the stone and collapsed on the grass
D) He insisted they take a break before continuing
Answer: C
The text states that "When they reached the top of the steps, he just let go the stone, threw his entire length flat on the grass, and shut his eyes."
Q3: What did the bearded man do after Jagan let go of the stone?
A) He scolded Jagan for dropping it
B) He gently set the stone down and rested
C) He began rolling the stone over and examining it
D) He helped Jagan back to his feet
Answer: C

The text states that "When Jagan revived, he found the other rolling the stone over and explaining, 'This would be the top; come closer and you will see the lines marked by my master with the bodkin, the outline of the Goddess.'"
Q4: How did Jagan perceive the stone they were examining?
A) He was amazed by the intricate carvings
B) He could see the potential of the sculpture
C) He found it no different from any other block of stone
D) He was disappointed by the lack of progress on it
Answer: C
The text states that "To Jagan's eyes it was no different from any other block of stone; even the scratches originally made by the master were hardly convincing."
Q5: How did the bearded man react to seeing the stone?
A) He became frustrated and impatient
B) He became lost in contemplation and visions
C) He became excited and began singing and dancing
D) He became emotional and sentimental about his master
Answer: B
The text states that the bearded man "seemed to feel intoxicated at the sight of it" and "was lost in visions of the Goddess."
Q6: What did the bearded man say about the Goddess's appearance and attributes?
A) She had five heads of different colors
B) She had ten arms holding various divine objects
C) Both A and B
D) None of the above
Answer: C

The text states that the bearded man described the Goddess as "ten-armed, and except for the one which indicates protection and the one offering a blessing, all the other arms hold a variety of divine articles" and that "she combines in her all colours and every kind of radiance, symbolized by five heads of different colours."
Q7: How did the bearded man react when Jagan said he knew the story of the Goddess?
A) He became annoyed and dismissed Jagan
B) He insisted on telling the story anyway
C) He was pleased and allowed Jagan to tell it
D) He asked Jagan to tell the story instead
Answer: B

The text states that the bearded man replied, "But still it's always good to hear it over and over again; you will always have the protection of Devi, and everything you attempt will turn out successful."
Q8: What did the bearded man say he would do if he could devote his life to completing the Goddess image?
A) He would be able to retire in peace
B) He would gain the Goddess's divine blessings
C) He would be able to open a new sculpture workshop
D) He would be able to die peacefully on his 70th birthday
Answer: D
The text states that the bearded man said, "If I can devote my life to the completion of this task I will die in peace."
Q9: How old did the bearded man say he was?
A) 50 years old
B) 60 years old
C) 69 years old
D) 70 years old
Answer: C
The text states that the bearded man said, "I am sixty-nine."
Q10: What did the bearded man say about the possibility of the stone slab cracking during the water-seasoning process?
A) It was highly unlikely to crack
B) It was a certainty that it would crack
C) It was in God's hands whether it would crack
D) It would be an inauspicious event if it cracked
Answer: C
The text states that the bearded man said, "With all that water-seasoning, the slab may suddenly split in the middle, and then what does one do?" and "How can I say? It's in God's hands."
Q11: How did the bearded man react to the possibility of the second stone cracking?
A) He became hopeful and optimistic
B) He became fatalistic and resigned
C) He became dismissive and unconcerned
D) He became superstitious and fearful
Answer: D
The text states that the bearded man said, "That'd be an inauspicious thought and question," when Jagan asked about the possibility of the second stone cracking.
Q12: What did the bearded man say the Goddess's ten arms symbolized?
A) The five elements and five senses
B) The ten cardinal virtues and divine gifts
C) The ten stages of spiritual enlightenment
D) The ten attributes of supreme divinity
Answer: D

The text describes the bearded man explaining the symbolism of the Goddess's ten arms, including "a conch, which is the origin of sound, a discus, which gives the universe its motion, a goad to suppress evil forces, a rope that causes bonds, lotus flowers for beauty and symmetry, and a kapalam, a begging bowl made of a bleached human skull."
Q13: What did the bearded man say was his master's aim in wanting to create the image of the Goddess?
A) To earn wealth and prestige
B) To achieve personal enlightenment
C) To provide an object of contemplation for others
D) To fulfill a divine vision and prophecy
Answer: C
The text states that the bearded man said his master's "aim was to create the image for others to contemplate. That was his aim and if I can carry it out, I'll abandon all other work in life."
Q14: What did the bearded man suggest to Jagan about buying the garden and installing the Goddess image?
A) He asked Jagan to consider becoming his patron
B) He offered to sell the garden to Jagan at a discount
C) He encouraged Jagan to create a retreat for himself
D) He insisted that Jagan was the only one who could help
Answer: C
The text states that the bearded man said to Jagan, "Why don't you buy this garden and install the Goddess?"
Q15: How did Jagan respond to the bearded man's suggestion about buying the garden?
A) He enthusiastically agreed to the idea
B) He politely declined, citing lack of interest
C) He expressed uncertainty and hesitation
D) He became offended and shut down the conversation
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan replied, "'\[...\] I do not know,' replied Jagan, thickening his armour of self-defence, and tried to laugh the question off."
Q16: What did Jagan feel he needed at this stage in his life?
A) A new business venture
B) A more active social life
C) A retreat from his current circumstances
D) A reconciliation with his son Mali
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan felt "at some stage in one's life one must uproot oneself from the accustomed surroundings and disappear so that others may continue in peace."
Q17: What did the bearded man say about the scriptural guidance for a husband and wife to vanish into the forest?
A) It was a mandatory requirement
B) It was an optional spiritual practice
C) It was the most accredited procedure
D) It was a symbolic rather than literal act
Answer: C

The bearded man stated that "It would be the most accredited procedure according to our scriptures—husband and wife must vanish into the forest at some stage in their lives, leaving the affairs of the world to younger people."
Q18: Why did Jagan feel shy and reserved about talking about his son Mali?
A) He was embarrassed by Mali's strange behavior
B) He wanted to avoid burdening the bearded man
C) He preferred to keep his family matters private
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text states that Jagan "felt shy and reserved about talking of his son—like one not wishing to exhibit his sores."
Q19: How did the birds, frogs, and aquatic creatures react to the bearded man's sudden outbursts of singing?
A) They were attracted and drawn closer
B) They remained undisturbed and unaffected
C) They fluttered, sprang back, and left tracks
D) They became aggressive and territorial
Answer: C

The text states that "The birds in the trees fluttered at the sudden outbreak of noise. Frogs at the edge of the pond sprang back into the water, and Jagan's gaze was held by the delicate tracks on the surface left by aquatic creatures invisibly coursing."
Q20: What did the bearded man ask Jagan to do to help with the Goddess image?
A) Provide financial support for the project
B) Assist in the physical labor of carving the image
C) Offer ideas and suggestions for the design
D) Pray and meditate to bless the creation
Answer: B
The text states that the bearded man said to Jagan, "It's only a man like you that can help me."
Q21: How did Jagan initially respond to the bearded man's request for help?
A) He enthusiastically agreed to assist
B) He politely declined, citing his limitations
C) He asked for more details on what was required
D) He tried to change the subject and avoid the topic
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan said, "Don't think too much of me. No, no, after all, I'm a humble merchant."
Q22: What did the bearded man say would be the benefit for Jagan if he helped with the Goddess image?
A) He would gain spiritual enlightenment
B) He would be rewarded with wealth and prosperity
C) He would have a peaceful retreat to escape to
D) He would be remembered for his contributions
Answer: C
The bearded man suggested to Jagan, "Why don't you buy this garden and install the Goddess? ... I only thought it would do you good to have a retreat like this."
Q23: How did Jagan feel about the possibility of talking about his personal life and family issues?
A) He was eager to open up and share
B) He was hesitant and held back his thoughts
C) He was annoyed and wanted to change the subject
D) He was indifferent and felt it didn't matter
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan "felt shy and reserved about talking of his son—like one not wishing to exhibit his sores."
Q24: What did the bearded man say about the likelihood of the second stone cracking during the water-seasoning process?
A) It was a virtual certainty
B) It was highly unlikely
C) It would be an inauspicious event
D) It would require starting over from scratch
Answer: B
The bearded man stated that "The second stone does not generally crack."
Q25: How did the bearded man's demeanor and tone change when he was discussing the Goddess and the sculpture project?
A) He became more subdued and reflective
B) He became more animated and passionate
C) He became more authoritative and demanding
D) He became more lighthearted and casual
Answer: B
The text describes the bearded man becoming "lost in visions of the Goddess" and bursting "into another song in Sanskrit" when discussing the project.

mcqs.question: What was covering the pond?
options: Lotus
Water lilies
Algae
Duckweed
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that the pond was "covered with blue lotus".

mcqs.question: What was mantling the steps?
options: Grass
Ivy
Moss and crumbling
Pebbles
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "the steps were mantled with moss and crumbling in".

mcqs.question: What type of trees were looming over the small shrine?
options: Oak, pine, and maple
Banyan, peepul, and mango
Palm, coconut, and eucalyptus
Cedar, fir, and spruce
mcqs.explanation: The text describes "banyan, peepul, and mango trees" looming over the small shrine.

mcqs.question: What was intertwined and choking the vegetation on the surroundings?
options: Brambles, thorny bushes, lantana, and oleander
Vines, moss, and ferns
Weeds and wildflowers
Grass and shrubs
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions "brambles, thorny bushes, lantana, and oleander intertwined and choked each other".

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man describe the area in the past?
options: Crowded and bustling
Peaceful and quiet
Dangerous and unforgiving
Prosperous and thriving
mcqs.explanation: The text states that in the past "robbers hid themselves in the jungles, and tigers and elephants roamed the foothills".

mcqs.question: What was the bearded man's role in relation to the master?
options: He was the master's servant
He was the master's son
He was the master's apprentice
He was the master's business partner
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that the bearded man "came to him when I was five years old" and the master "supported me for years", suggesting he was the master's apprentice.

mcqs.question: Why did the bearded man choose to live in that location?
options: It was close to the town
It was near a major highway
They needed the stones from the nearby hills
It was a peaceful and remote area
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man states that "We needed all those stones" from the nearby hills, explaining why they chose to live in that location.

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the sales tax people?
options: They had not yet visited his business
They frequently inspected his records
They were unfairly targeting his business
They had already collected a large amount from him
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man says "the sales-tax people have still not come my way yet", indicating they had not yet visited his business.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's habitual, instinctive, and inexplicable uneasiness concerning?
options: Paying his employees
Keeping track of his inventory
Any tax
Dealing with government officials
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan had "a habitual, instinctive, and inexplicable uneasiness concerning any tax."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan inwardly wonder about the bearded man's relationship with his master?
options: If the master had been abusive towards him
If the master had been like a father to him
If the master had been a passing acquaintance
If the master had been his biological father
mcqs.explanation: The text suggests that Jagan "wanted to ask, but suppressed the question, whether he might not have been born of a passing concubine to his so-called master who never married."

mcqs.question: Why did the bearded man not apply hair dye to his own beard?
options: He could not afford it
He preferred the natural white color
It was against his religious beliefs
He was too busy dyeing other people's hair
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said "I like my white beard and keep it. There is no compulsion for anyone to blacken his hair."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man feel about the increased traffic and development in the area?
options: He was excited about the progress
He was indifferent to the changes
He was nostalgic for the past
He was openly critical of the developments
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that the bearded man "seemed rather depressed at the thought of their giving place to highway: buses" and described how it used to be "in those days" when it was more peaceful and quiet.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan notice about the bearded man's business?
options: He had a large customer base
He was struggling to make sales
He had a thriving hair dye business
He was evading sales tax
mcqs.explanation: The text suggests that Jagan was aware of the "cash that grew from out-of-hour sales at the counter and filled the smaller jug", implying the bearded man was evading sales tax.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about Gandhi's stance on sales tax?
options: Gandhi had strongly condemned it
Gandhi had advocated for its abolition
Gandhi had not made any specific comments about it
Gandhi had actively supported it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "If Gandhi had said somewhere, 'Pay your sales tax uncomplainingly,' he would have followed his advice, but Gandhi had made no reference to sales tax anywhere (to Jagan's knowledge)."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the likelihood of the sales tax people visiting his business?
options: They would never find out about his business
They were unlikely to visit in the near future
They were sure to visit once they noticed fewer grey hairs
They had already made multiple visits to his shop
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man says "But they are bound to wake up sooner or later, when they notice fewer grey hairs around", indicating he expects the sales tax people to eventually visit his business.

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about his choice to keep his white beard?
options: It was a family tradition
It was a religious requirement
It was a personal preference
It was a practical decision
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said "I like my white beard and keep it. There is no compulsion for anyone to blacken his hair."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about the bearded man's statement that he was an exception to his own rule?
options: He agreed with the bearded man
He disagreed with the bearded man
He did not understand the statement
He thought the bearded man was being hypocritical
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that Jagan "seized this opportunity to say, 'Anyway, you are an exception to your own rule'", suggesting he thought the bearded man was being hypocritical.

mcqs.question: What was the bearded man's explanation for why he ended up in the hair dye business?
options: It was his family's traditional occupation
He had a natural talent for working with hair
It was the only job available in the remote area
His master encouraged him to pursue it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said "My master supported me for years", implying his master encouraged him to work in the hair dye business.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan reflect on regarding the bearded man's past?
options: The bearded man's parents were unknown
The bearded man had a difficult upbringing
The bearded man had a privileged childhood
The bearded man was hiding something about his past
mcqs.explanation: The text suggests that Jagan "wanted to ask, but suppressed the question, whether he might not have been born of a passing concubine to his so-called master", indicating Jagan suspected the bearded man was hiding something about his past.

mcqs.question: What did the text describe about the surroundings of the small shrine?
options: It was situated in a bustling town
It was located near a busy highway
It was surrounded by dense vegetation
It was part of a well-maintained park
mcqs.explanation: The text describes the "surroundings were covered with vegetation of every type—brambles, thorny bushes, lantana, and oleander intertwined and choked each other."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the quality of the stone from the nearby hills?
options: It was not suitable for sculpting
It was perfect for all types of work
It was excellent for softer panel work
It was difficult to extract and work with
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that "for softer panel work that stone is excellent" from the nearby "nose of Mempi".

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the difficulty of obtaining stone for the inner sanctum?
options: It was readily available and easy to work with
It required venturing deeper into the hills
It could only be sourced from a distant quarry
It was of inferior quality compared to the other stone
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man explained that "for images of the inner sanctum, one has to cut the stone from the belly of the hill further up, though it is difficult to hew and there are more breakages than in other portions."

mcqs.question: What question did Jagan suppress regarding the bearded man's relationship with his master?
options: Whether the master had been abusive
Whether the master had been like a father
Whether the master had been a passing acquaintance
Whether the master had been his biological father
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "wanted to ask, but suppressed the question, whether he might not have been born of a passing concubine to his so-called master who never married."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about people's attitudes towards developing the nearby hills?
options: People were eager to explore the hills
People were cautious about venturing into the hills
People were actively working to protect the hills
People's attitudes towards the hills had changed over time
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man mentioned that "in those days people did not go up the mountain as much as they do now", indicating that people's attitudes had changed over time.

mcqs.question: What did the text suggest about Jagan's perspective on paying taxes?
options: He was diligently compliant
He was actively evasive
He was indifferent to the process
He had a habitual uneasiness about it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan had "a habitual, instinctive, and inexplicable uneasiness concerning any tax." Set 2

mcqs.question: Where did the bearded man say his master worked on the details of ornament?
options: In the quarry
In the pillared hall
In the backyard
In the sanctum
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man pointed to a "corer in the pillared hall" and said "He worked on those details of ornament".

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master lived his whole life doing?
options: Cooking rice
Carving images
Tending to the garden
Meditating in the sanctum
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that his master "lived his whole life here. All that he possessed could be contained within the palm of one's hand. I cooked a little rice for him in that corner, where you see the walls blackened. All day he sat here working on the image or we went to the quarry to hew slabs."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about people being afraid to come to the place?
options: They were afraid of the monkeys
They were afraid of the wild growth
They were afraid of the snakes
They were afraid of the cheetahs
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man said "People were afraid to come here because of the snakes, but my master loved them and never approved of clearing the wild growth around."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master used to say about sharing the fruits with the monkeys?
options: "I'll share the fruits of those trees with them."
"The monkeys can have the fruits."
"We must not monopolize the earth."
Both A and C
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that his master used to say "Tl share the fruits of those trees with them," and "We must not monopolize this earth. They won't harm us."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say happened when his master died?
options: He buried his master's body in the backyard
He cremated his master's body beyond the pond
He performed a ritual burial ceremony
He carried his master's body to the city
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man said "When he died one night I sat at vigil by a small oil lamp, and cremated his body beyond that pond, heaping on the dead wood and withered leaves."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master had dreamed of creating?
options: A five-faced Gayatri deity
A dancing figure of Nataraj
A new God for the temple
Both A and C
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man explained that his master "had dreamt of a five-faced Gayatri, to be seen nowhere else, the deity of Radiance. He had even hewn the slab for it and knocked the first dents. It used to be in that yard somewhere."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master did to ensure the image would not be too perfect?
options: He added a small flaw to every image
He chipped off a piece of the image
He placed the image in a protective case
He purposely damaged the image
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that "We always do it; no one ever notices it, but we always create a small flaw in every image; it's for safety."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan realize about his own existence compared to the bearded man's life?
options: His life was much more fulfilling
His life was much more narrow
His life was more active and diverse
His life was more financially stable
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "suddenly realized how narrow his whole existence had been—between the Lawley Statue and the frying shop; Mali's antics seemed to matter naught."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the true nature of one's being?
options: It is defined by one's material possessions
It is defined by one's physical body
It is not defined by the body or material things
It is defined by one's social status
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man declared "We should not let the body deceive us as to the true nature of our being. One is not really bone and meat. My master proved it in his days."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man do that startled the various creatures in the green shelter?
options: He built a fence around the area
He cleared out the wild growth
He beat down every bush with his bamboo stick
He tried to catch the animals
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man "seemed to enjoy their discomfiture and inhaled noisily, with relish, the smell of crushed greenery" after "beating down every bush with his bamboo stick".

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the cobras that lived in the area?
options: They were aggressive and dangerous
They had all been killed by his master
They had quietly slipped away when they arrived
They were mainly nocturnal creatures
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated "I'm sure the cobras that live here must have quietly slipped away when we came; they are uncanny in their habits. Very alert, very alert and watchful."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master did when he noticed a defect in a sculptural piece?
options: He repaired the defect immediately
He calmly explained the flaw to the bearded man
He became upset and flung the piece out the door
He refused to use the defective piece
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man recounted that when his master "noticed the defect that he flung it out through the door and remained speechless for three days".

mcqs.question: What was the story the bearded man mentioned about the dancing figure of Nataraj?
options: It was so perfect it began a cosmic dance
It was so heavy it could not be moved
It was stolen from the temple
It had a small flaw added intentionally
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man said "the story of the dancing figure of Nataraj, which was so perfect that it began a cosmic dance and the town itself shook as if an earthquake had rocked it, until a small finger on the figure was chipped off."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say he and his master always did to the images they created?
options: They always added a small flaw
They always polished them to perfection
They always ensured they were symmetrical
They always incorporated local materials
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man explained "We always do it; no one ever notices it, but we always create a small flaw in every image; it's for safety."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the pedestal of the Vishnu image and the arms of Saraswathi?
options: They were perfectly made and used
They were flawed and could not be used
They were stolen from the temple
They were still in the process of being carved
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man pointed out "This was the pedestal of Vishnu, meant for some temple; those are the arms of Saraswathi, the goddess of learning—they could not be used because of a slight crack in the stone."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the two-foot-square block that his master could not find?
options: It had been stolen
It had been used for another project
It had mysteriously disappeared
It was being kept in storage
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man recounted his master saying "The two-foot-square one? It could not have grown limbs and walked off—although, let me tell you, if an image is perfect, it cannot be held down on its pedestal."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan wonder about as he listened to the bearded man's story?
options: If he was on the verge of a new birth
If he should change his own way of life
If he should get involved in the sculpture business
If he should visit the temple the images were for
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "suddenly realized how narrow his whole existence had been—between the Lawley Statue and the frying shop; Mali's antics seemed to matter naught. 'Am I on the verge of a new janma?' he wondered."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man respond to Jagan's sudden remark?
options: He became defensive and changed the subject
He agreed with Jagan and expanded on the idea
He was surprised by the remark and tried to understand it
He dismissed Jagan's comment as irrelevant
mcqs.explanation: The text says "The bearded man, suppressing his surprise at this sudden remark, said, 'True, true, you must not lose sight of your real being, which is not mere bone and meat.'"

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man do after making the remark about one's true nature?
options: He meditated silently
He continued his story-telling
He led Jagan to another part of the site
He offered Jagan some fruit from the guava tree
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man "reached up to a branch of a guava tree, plucked a fruit and bit into it with the glee of a ten-year-old urchin. 'This tree always gave the best fruit. Monkeys thrive on it, and during certain seasons the treetop would be as full of monkeys as leaves, you know.' He pulled down the branch again, plucked off another fruit and held it for Jagan."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the guava tree providing the best fruit?
options: It was the only fruit tree on the property
It was his master's favorite tree to harvest from
It attracted many monkeys who also enjoyed the fruit
Both B and C
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated "This tree always gave the best fruit. Monkeys thrive on it, and during certain seasons the treetop would be as full of monkeys as leaves, you know."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master never approved of doing?
options: Leaving the temple to go to the quarry
Cooking food for himself in the corner
Clearing the wild growth around the property
Spending time with the monkeys and snakes
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that the bearded man's master "never approved of clearing the wild growth around."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say was stolen from the temple before they arrived?
options: The image of the five-faced Gayatri deity
The dancing figure of Nataraj
The God in the sanctum
The pedestal of Vishnu
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man mentioned "There used to be a God in the sanctum which had been stolen years before we came here."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man describe the state of the temple when he and his master arrived?
options: It was in good condition and well-maintained
It was in ruins and needed extensive repairs
It was locked and no longer in use
It was already missing the God in the sanctum
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that when the bearded man and his master arrived, "There used to be a God in the sanctum which had been stolen years before we came here."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master decided to do after realizing the God in the sanctum had been stolen?
options: He decided to abandon the temple
He decided to report the theft to the authorities
He decided to make a new God for the temple
He decided to pray for the stolen God's return
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man recounted that his master "woke me up and said, 'Let us make a new God for this temple. Then it will flourish again.'"

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man do after mentioning the spot where his master's body was cremated?
options: He fell to his knees and began to pray
He walked away from the spot in silence
He started beating the bushes with his staff
He offered a guava fruit to Jagan
mcqs.explanation: The text states that after mentioning the spot, "He stood under the palmyra with his eyes shut for a moment, muttering some holy verse. 'We should not let the body deceive us as to the true nature of our being. One is not really bone and meat. My master proved it in his days,' he declared, and as if seized with a sudden frenzy beat down every bush with his bamboo stick." Set 3

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan not eat the guava fruit the bearded man offered him?
options: He did not like guava fruit
He was allergic to guava
He kept off sweets and salt
He was saving it for later
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "took it out of courtesy, but did not eat it. 'I keep off sweets and salt.'"

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man react when Jagan mentioned the printer Nataraj?
options: He became excited and asked about Nataraj
He expressed interest in learning more about printing
He lost interest in the conversation and ignored Jagan
He criticized Jagan for mentioning something unrelated
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "the bearded man had lost interest in the subject totally by this time. Ignoring Jagan and talking on, he failed to observe that Jagan had overcome the temptation to take a bite and had let the fruit slip to the ground."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about the guava fruit he had let fall to the ground?
options: He was glad he had not eaten it
He regretted not eating it
He was unsure if it was good or bad to eat
He didn't care about the fruit anymore
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan was "unable to decide whether it would be good or bad from the point of view of dietetics."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's father do to the guava tree in their backyard?
options: He pruned and maintained it
He celebrated the tree's growth
He cut it down with an ax
He fenced it off to protect it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan's "father took an ax and cut it down, remarking, 'These little devils will eat nothing else as long as this cursed tree stands, See how one by one they are going down with colic!'"

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say was "very important" that he needed to find?
options: The slab for the five-faced Gayatri deity
The stolen God from the temple's sanctum
The pedestal of the Vishnu image
The arms of the Saraswathi goddess
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated "We have gone round and round, but not found the slab. It must be somewhere. Very important, very important, I tell you. When I have found it, you will know."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think the bearded man might do to him when he asked Jagan to come down into the pond?
options: Drown him
Push him into the pond
Make him retrieve something from the water
Wash his feet in the pond
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thought "Perhaps he is going to knock me into the pond and go back to the town and report, 'The maker of sweets has vanished.'"

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel as he descended the moss-covered steps into the pond?
options: Excited and eager
Nervous and reluctant
Fascinated and intrigued
Creeped out and uncomfortable
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "descended the moss-covered steps, which gave him a creepy feeling underfoot".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about as he stood in the pond with the water up to his waist?
options: His past life and future reincarnations
His son Mali and his business problems
The beauty of the blue lotus in the pond
The likelihood of catching a cold or illness
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that Jagan's "mind ran through various choices. Pet dog? Predatory cat? Street-corner donkey? Maharajah on an elephant? Anything but a money-making sweet-maker with a spoilt son."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man instruct Jagan to do when he was kneeling in the pond?
options: Retrieve a stone from the water
Catch and hold one of the pond's creatures
Help him lift a stone that was submerged
Swim across to the other side of the pond
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man told Jagan "Plunge your hand in here and feel..." and later said "If you could only make up your mind to lift it, it is only will power you lack."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the stone being in the water for water-seasoning?
options: It needed to be submerged for several years
It was meant to bring out the surface grains
It had to be placed in running water, not still
It was a technique used for all sculptural stones
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man explained that his master "put this stone into the water because it needed the water treatment to bring out its surface grains."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man describe the size of the stone they were trying to lift?
options: It was a massive, heavy statue
It was a small, delicate sculpture
It was a medium-sized block of stone
It was just large enough for a pedestal
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated it was "hardly a couple of feet—when it is fully worked it will hardly be eighteen inches".

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about Jagan's physical condition preventing him from lifting the stone?
options: Jagan was too old and frail
Jagan was too thin and malnourished
Jagan was too out of shape from lack of activity
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man said "If you ate normally like other human beings, or at least consumed some of the sweets that you sell, you would be in better shape."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man's demeanor and manner of speaking change when they entered the garden area?
options: He became more humble and deferential
He became more distant and distracted
He became more authoritarian and commanding
He became more emotional and excitable
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man "was no longer the tame hair-blackener on Kabir Street but a sort of leader of the forces, a petty chieftain used to having his orders carried out without question."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master had started to do to the stone they were trying to lift?
options: He had begun carving detailed designs on it
He had knocked the first dents into it
He had partially completed the sculpture
He had prepared it for water-seasoning
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man explained that his master "had started to work on it but suddenly decided that it needed water-seasoning".

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master always emphasized about the importance of water-seasoning stones?
options: It made the stone easier to carve
It brought out the natural beauty of the stone
It made the stone stronger and more durable
It was necessary for the stone to achieve perfection
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that his master "always said that the longer a stone stayed in water ... if an image is perfect, it cannot be held down on its pedestal."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think the bearded man might do if he refused to help lift the stone?
options: He might abandon the effort and leave
He might become angry and force Jagan to lift it
He might threaten Jagan with physical harm
He might seek help from someone else
mcqs.explanation: The text suggests Jagan thought "If you could only make up your mind to lift it, it is only will power you lack."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about his master's practice of intentionally creating small flaws in the sculptures?
options: It was to ensure the sculptures were unique
It was to protect the sculptures from theft
It was to make the sculptures more aesthetically pleasing
It was to prevent the sculptures from becoming too perfect
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man had earlier explained that "We always do it; no one ever notices it, but we always create a small flaw in every image; it's for safety."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master had dreamed of creating for the temple?
options: A five-faced Gayatri deity
A dancing figure of Nataraj
A new God to replace the stolen one
Both A and C
mcqs.explanation: The text states the bearded man said his master "had dreamt of a five-faced Gayatri, to be seen nowhere else, the deity of Radiance. He had even hewn the slab for it and knocked the first dents. It used to be in that yard somewhere. Let me look for it."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan realize about the bearded man's story and his own life as he listened?
options: His own life was more meaningful and fulfilling
His own life was more successful and prosperous
His own life was more narrow and limited in scope
His own life was more spiritually enlightened
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "suddenly realized how narrow his whole existence had been—between the Lawley Statue and the frying shop; Mali's antics seemed to matter naught."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the reason he ended up in the hair dye business?
options: It was his family's traditional occupation
It was the only job available in the remote area
His master had supported and encouraged him in it
He had a natural talent and passion for working with hair
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated "My master supported me for years" in reference to how he ended up in the hair dye business.

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man describe the changes that had occurred in the area over time?
options: It had become more crowded and bustling
It had become more peaceful and quiet
It had become more dangerous and unforgiving
It had become more developed with highways and buses
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates the bearded man said "Too many buses on the highway, ever since that project in the hills..."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the monkeys in the tree above them?
options: They were aggressive and territorial
They had all been driven away by humans
They would share the fruit with his master
They had become fewer in number over time
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that his master "used to say 'I'll share the fruits of those trees with them,' he used to say."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say his master had done when he noticed a defect in a sculptural piece?
options: He fixed the defect carefully
He became upset and flung the piece out
He decided not to use the defective piece
He kept working on it until it was perfect
mcqs.explanation: The text states the bearded man recounted that when his master "noticed the defect that he flung it out through the door and remained speechless for three days".

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about the possibility of his own death while standing in the pond?
options: He was eager for it to happen
He was fearful and wanted to escape
He was accepting and contemplative
He was indifferent to the prospect
mcqs.explanation: The text suggests that Jagan felt "It would be such a wonderful moment to die, leaving the perennial problems of life to solve themselves."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say was the reason they should not be deceived by the body?
options: The body is not the true nature of one's being
The body is impermanent and will eventually die
The body is simply a vessel for the soul
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man declared "We should not let the body deceive us as to the true nature of our being. One is not really bone and meat. My master proved it in his days." Set 4

mcqs.question: How did Jagan prepare himself to help lift the stone?
options: He rolled up his sleeves
He tied his upper cloth around his head
He removed his shoes and socks
He stretched and warmed up his muscles
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "girt himself for the task by tying his upper cloth around his head and tucking up his dhoti in a businesslike manner."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do after they reached the top of the steps with the stone?
options: He carefully placed the stone down
He asked the bearded man to take over
He let go of the stone and collapsed on the grass
He insisted they take a break before continuing
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "When they reached the top of the steps, he just let go the stone, threw his entire length flat on the grass, and shut his eyes."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man do after Jagan let go of the stone?
options: He scolded Jagan for dropping it
He gently set the stone down and rested
He began rolling the stone over and examining it
He helped Jagan back to his feet
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "When Jagan revived, he found the other rolling the stone over and explaining, 'This would be the top; come closer and you will see the lines marked by my master with the bodkin, the outline of the Goddess.'"

mcqs.question: How did Jagan perceive the stone they were examining?
options: He was amazed by the intricate carvings
He could see the potential of the sculpture
He found it no different from any other block of stone
He was disappointed by the lack of progress on it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "To Jagan's eyes it was no different from any other block of stone; even the scratches originally made by the master were hardly convincing."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man react to seeing the stone?
options: He became frustrated and impatient
He became lost in contemplation and visions
He became excited and began singing and dancing
He became emotional and sentimental about his master
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man "seemed to feel intoxicated at the sight of it" and "was lost in visions of the Goddess."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the Goddess's appearance and attributes?
options: She had five heads of different colors
She had ten arms holding various divine objects
Both A and B
None of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man described the Goddess as "ten-armed, and except for the one which indicates protection and the one offering a blessing, all the other arms hold a variety of divine articles" and that "she combines in her all colours and every kind of radiance, symbolized by five heads of different colours."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man react when Jagan said he knew the story of the Goddess?
options: He became annoyed and dismissed Jagan
He insisted on telling the story anyway
He was pleased and allowed Jagan to tell it
He asked Jagan to tell the story instead
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man replied, "But still it's always good to hear it over and over again; you will always have the protection of Devi, and everything you attempt will turn out successful."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say he would do if he could devote his life to completing the Goddess image?
options: He would be able to retire in peace
He would gain the Goddess's divine blessings
He would be able to open a new sculpture workshop
He would be able to die peacefully on his 70th birthday
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said, "If I can devote my life to the completion of this task I will die in peace."

mcqs.question: How old did the bearded man say he was?
options: 50 years old
60 years old
69 years old
70 years old
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said, "I am sixty-nine."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the possibility of the stone slab cracking during the water-seasoning process?
options: It was highly unlikely to crack
It was a certainty that it would crack
It was in God's hands whether it would crack
It would be an inauspicious event if it cracked
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said, "With all that water-seasoning, the slab may suddenly split in the middle, and then what does one do?" and "How can I say? It's in God's hands."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man react to the possibility of the second stone cracking?
options: He became hopeful and optimistic
He became fatalistic and resigned
He became dismissive and unconcerned
He became superstitious and fearful
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said, "That'd be an inauspicious thought and question," when Jagan asked about the possibility of the second stone cracking.

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say the Goddess's ten arms symbolized?
options: The five elements and five senses
The ten cardinal virtues and divine gifts
The ten stages of spiritual enlightenment
The ten attributes of supreme divinity
mcqs.explanation: The text describes the bearded man explaining the symbolism of the Goddess's ten arms, including "a conch, which is the origin of sound, a discus, which gives the universe its motion, a goad to suppress evil forces, a rope that causes bonds, lotus flowers for beauty and symmetry, and a kapalam, a begging bowl made of a bleached human skull."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say was his master's aim in wanting to create the image of the Goddess?
options: To earn wealth and prestige
To achieve personal enlightenment
To provide an object of contemplation for others
To fulfill a divine vision and prophecy
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said his master's "aim was to create the image for others to contemplate. That was his aim and if I can carry it out, I'll abandon all other work in life."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man suggest to Jagan about buying the garden and installing the Goddess image?
options: He asked Jagan to consider becoming his patron
He offered to sell the garden to Jagan at a discount
He encouraged Jagan to create a retreat for himself
He insisted that Jagan was the only one who could help
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said to Jagan, "Why don't you buy this garden and install the Goddess?"

mcqs.question: How did Jagan respond to the bearded man's suggestion about buying the garden?
options: He enthusiastically agreed to the idea
He politely declined, citing lack of interest
He expressed uncertainty and hesitation
He became offended and shut down the conversation
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan replied, "'[...] I do not know,' replied Jagan, thickening his armour of self-defence, and tried to laugh the question off."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan feel he needed at this stage in his life?
options: A new business venture
A more active social life
A retreat from his current circumstances
A reconciliation with his son Mali
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan felt "at some stage in one's life one must uproot oneself from the accustomed surroundings and disappear so that others may continue in peace."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the scriptural guidance for a husband and wife to vanish into the forest?
options: It was a mandatory requirement
It was an optional spiritual practice
It was the most accredited procedure
It was a symbolic rather than literal act
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that "It would be the most accredited procedure according to our scriptures—husband and wife must vanish into the forest at some stage in their lives, leaving the affairs of the world to younger people."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel shy and reserved about talking about his son Mali?
options: He was embarrassed by Mali's strange behavior
He wanted to avoid burdening the bearded man
He preferred to keep his family matters private
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "felt shy and reserved about talking of his son—like one not wishing to exhibit his sores."

mcqs.question: How did the birds, frogs, and aquatic creatures react to the bearded man's sudden outbursts of singing?
options: They were attracted and drawn closer
They remained undisturbed and unaffected
They fluttered, sprang back, and left tracks
They became aggressive and territorial
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "The birds in the trees fluttered at the sudden outbreak of noise. Frogs at the edge of the pond sprang back into the water, and Jagan's gaze was held by the delicate tracks on the surface left by aquatic creatures invisibly coursing."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man ask Jagan to do to help with the Goddess image?
options: Provide financial support for the project
Assist in the physical labor of carving the image
Offer ideas and suggestions for the design
Pray and meditate to bless the creation
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the bearded man said to Jagan, "It's only a man like you that can help me."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan initially respond to the bearded man's request for help?
options: He enthusiastically agreed to assist
He politely declined, citing his limitations
He asked for more details on what was required
He tried to change the subject and avoid the topic
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said, "Don't think too much of me. No, no, after all, I'm a humble merchant."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say would be the benefit for Jagan if he helped with the Goddess image?
options: He would gain spiritual enlightenment
He would be rewarded with wealth and prosperity
He would have a peaceful retreat to escape to
He would be remembered for his contributions
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man suggested to Jagan, "Why don't you buy this garden and install the Goddess? ... I only thought it would do you good to have a retreat like this."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel about the possibility of talking about his personal life and family issues?
options: He was eager to open up and share
He was hesitant and held back his thoughts
He was annoyed and wanted to change the subject
He was indifferent and felt it didn't matter
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "felt shy and reserved about talking of his son—like one not wishing to exhibit his sores."

mcqs.question: What did the bearded man say about the likelihood of the second stone cracking during the water-seasoning process?
options: It was a virtual certainty
It was highly unlikely
It would be an inauspicious event
It would require starting over from scratch
mcqs.explanation: The bearded man stated that "The second stone does not generally crack."

mcqs.question: How did the bearded man's demeanor and tone change when he was discussing the Goddess and the sculpture project?
options: He became more subdued and reflective
He became more animated and passionate
He became more authoritative and demanding
He became more lighthearted and casual
mcqs.explanation: The text describes the bearded man becoming "lost in visions of the Goddess" and bursting "into another song in Sanskrit" when discussing the project.

content.value: # Chapter 9
# Set 1
Q1: What was the name of the protagonist?
A) Nataraj
B) Jagan
C) Mali
D) Sivaraman
Answer: B
Explanation: The text mentions that the protagonist's name is Jagan.
Q2: What did Jagan do to cool himself down?
A) Took a cold shower
B) Drank cold water
C) Fanned himself with a cloth
D) Poured cold water over himself
Answer: D
Explanation: The text states that Jagan "poured a lot of cold water over himself" after coming from the back yard.
Q3: What was Jagan doing when his son Mali came to see him?
A) Cooking dinner
B) Spinning cotton
C) Praying to the Gods
D) Reading a book
Answer: B
Explanation: The text describes Jagan sitting in the courtyard, turning the spinning wheel and drawing a fine thread.
Q4: What was the purpose of Jagan's book that Nataraj had not published?
A) To establish the science of food-making
B) To promote the use of hair dye
C) To describe the process of spinning cotton
D) To advocate for economic reforms
Answer: A
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan "was trying to establish in his book" the importance of precision in food-making.
Q5: What was Jagan's initial reaction when Mali came to see him?
A) He was excited and welcomed him warmly
B) He quickly covered his bare chest with a towel
C) He ignored Mali and continued spinning
D) He scolded Mali for interrupting his work
Answer: B
Explanation: The text states that Jagan "quickly snatched a towel and hid his chest under it" when Mali arrived.
Q6: What was Jagan's profession?
A) Sculptor
B) Tailor
C) Sweets maker
D) Farmer
Answer: C
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan was "the maker of sweets and gatherer of money each day."
Q7: What did Jagan suspect about the bearded man who visited his shop?
A) He was a spy from another country
B) He was a visitation from another planet
C) He was trying to take over Jagan's sweet business
D) He was a con artist trying to steal Jagan's money
Answer: B
Explanation: The text states that Jagan "wondered if the bearded man might not be a visitation from another planet."
Q8: Why did Jagan feel that his identity was undergoing a change?
A) He was getting old and retiring from his business
B) He was considering taking up a new profession
C) He was inspired by the bearded man's vision
D) He was feeling guilty about neglecting his family
Answer: C
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan felt an "internal transformation had taken place" after his "latest contact" with the bearded man.
Q9: What was the purpose of the bearded man's visit to Jagan's shop?
A) To buy sweets
B) To install an image of the Goddess
C) To recruit Jagan as a sculptor
D) To sell hair dye products
Answer: B
Explanation: The text states that the bearded man had come to Jagan's shop to get help "for installing the image of the Goddess."
Q10: What was Jagan's initial reaction when the bearded man described the Goddess with five heads?
A) He was confused and skeptical
B) He was intrigued and found it thrilling
C) He was offended and asked the man to leave
D) He was indifferent and continued with his work
Answer: B
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan found the bearded man's description of the Goddess "a thrilling vision."
Q11: What was Jagan's main concern about helping the bearded man with his task?
A) He was worried about the impact on his sweet business
B) He was afraid the man might try to steal from him
C) He was unsure about trusting the man and his intentions
D) All of the above
Answer: D
Explanation: The text highlights Jagan's various concerns, including the impact on his sweet business, trusting the man, and what would happen after the image is completed.
Q12: What was Jagan's approach to cooking food?
A) He was indifferent to precision and timing
B) He believed food-making was an art, not a science
C) He preferred to cook food quickly for maximum nutrition
D) He believed precision and timing were crucial for proper cooking
Answer: D
Explanation: The text states that Jagan believed "in food, food-making and food-eating, what was important was precision. It was a science."
Q13: Why did Jagan feel unhappy about having to speak in a new tone to his son Mali?
A) He was afraid of losing his authority as a father
B) He felt he was betraying his old values and personality
C) He was worried Mali would not respect him anymore
D) All of the above
Answer: D
Explanation: The text indicates that Jagan felt unhappy about having to speak in a "new tone of voice" to Mali, as he was shedding the "awe" in which he had held his son.
Q14: What did Mali accuse Jagan of?
A) Neglecting his sweet business
B) Spending too much time spinning
C) Being the talk of the town
D) Ignoring his responsibilities at home
Answer: C
Explanation: The text states that Mali told Jagan "Everyone talks about you in the town."
Q15: What was Jagan's reaction when Mali told him about the townspeople's discussion?
A) He felt proud and wanted to know more
B) He dismissed it and said "Let them"
C) He became defensive and argued with Mali
D) He felt guilty and promised to change his behavior
Answer: B
Explanation: The text states that when Mali told Jagan about the townspeople's discussion, Jagan "did not wish to pursue the subject and so mumbled, 'Let them.'"
Q16: How did Jagan feel about the changing circumstances in his life?
A) He was resistant and wanted to maintain his old ways
B) He was excited and embraced the new changes
C) He was confused and unsure about the future
D) He was resigned and accepted the changes calmly
Answer: D
Explanation: The text suggests that Jagan felt "it's foolish to resist this fact" of entering a "new life at the appointed time."
Q17: What did Jagan use to light the oil wick in his house?
A) Matches
B) A flint and steel
C) A lighter
D) Not specified in the text
Answer: D
Explanation: The text does not mention the specific method Jagan used to light the oil wick.
Q18: How did Jagan feel about the sound of his spinning wheel?
A) It annoyed him and he wanted to stop it
B) It was a distraction that prevented him from thinking
C) It was a comforting and soothing sound
D) He was indifferent to the noise it made
Answer: C
Explanation: The text states that the "slight whirring noise of the wheel and the thread growing out of it" were "very comforting, stilling the nerves and thoughts" for Jagan.
Q19: What was the purpose of the low-wattage light bulbs in Jagan's house?
A) To save electricity
B) To create a cozy and intimate atmosphere
C) To benefit the human retina
D) To discourage unwanted visitors
Answer: C
Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan "had fitted only ten-watt bulbs 'in the light sockets in order to benefit the human retina."
Q20: What was Jagan's relationship with his printer, Nataraj?
A) They were close friends
B) Nataraj was indifferent to Jagan's ideas
C) Nataraj actively opposed Jagan's plans
D) Nataraj was Jagan's business partner
Answer: B
Explanation: The text suggests that Nataraj was "indifferent to this task" of publishing Jagan's book, while he had "printed the prospectus for Mali with alacrity."
Q21: What was the relationship between Jagan and his son Mali?
A) They were distant and disconnected
B) Mali was respectful and obedient towards Jagan
C) Jagan was in awe of Mali and sought his approval
D) Their relationship was strained and confrontational
Answer: C
Explanation: The text indicates that Jagan "used to pine for a word" from his son Mali, suggesting he was in awe of him and sought his approval.
Q22: What was Jagan's opinion on the monsoon that year?
A) He believed it would be delayed
B) He thought it would arrive earlier than usual
C) He was unsure about the timing of the monsoon
D) He did not have any specific thoughts about the monsoon
Answer: B
Explanation: The text states that Jagan "reflected. Perhaps the monsoon will be breaking earlier this year."
Q23: What was the significance of the coconut trees mentioned in the passage?
A) They provided shade and shelter for Jagan
B) They were important for the local economy
C) They represented the natural setting and environment
D) They were a source of food and raw materials
Answer: C
Explanation: The text describes the "sky-reaching coconut trees of the neighbourhood waving amidst the stars," suggesting they were part of the natural surroundings.
Q24: What was the purpose of Jagan's spinning wheel?
A) It was a hobby and source of relaxation
B) It was a tool for his book on food-making
C) It was a means of earning extra income
D) It was a way to follow Gandhi's advice on economic reform
Answer: A
Explanation: The text indicates that Jagan found the "slight whirring noise of the wheel and the thread growing out of it" to be "very comforting, stilling the nerves and thoughts."
Q25: How did Jagan feel about his changing identity and responsibilities?
A) He was overwhelmed and wanted to go back to his old life

Q1: What was Jagan's occupation?

C) He avoided using the front door.
D) All of the above.
Answer: B

Explanation: The text states that Jagan "shut the communicating door between his part of the dwelling and Mali's and locked it on his side" and "dragged up an old stool, and with the help of a long bamboo shut \[the ventilator\] tight" to isolate himself.
Q3: Why did Jagan's sister cut off contact with him?

B) Jagan's daughter-in-law Grace was a beef-eating Christian.
C) Jagan did shameful things like going to jail.
D) All of the above.

Explanation: The text states that Jagan's sister wrote to him saying she was ashamed to refer to him as a brother because of his actions like joining Gandhi, losing caste, and having a beef-eating Christian daughter-in-law.

A) They were close and supportive of each other.
B) They had a tense relationship and often argued.
C) They were estranged and had no contact.
D) They were indifferent towards each other.

Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan's brother "cut all contact after the division of their father's estate" and did not invite Jagan to participate in their father's anniversary ceremonies, indicating they were estranged.

Q13: What did Jagan's brother say about the kind of son Jagan could expect to have?

Q15: What did Jagan hear about his brother's remarks regarding him?

Q16: What did Jagan's sister say about their parents being spared the "indignity" of watching Jagan's "unsavoury activities"?

Q17: What did Jagan do to the path leading to the main street from his house?

Q18: How long had it been since Jagan had last used the side lane leading to the main street?
A) 10 years
B) 20 years
C) 30 years
D) Nearly 50 years

Q19: What did Jagan's elder brother used to do when they were hunting for grasshoppers?
A) He would let Jagan catch the grasshoppers himself.

Q20: What was Jagan's reaction when Mali and Grace drove past him?

Q22: What was Jagan's main reason for feeling grateful for being an outcast?
A) He could avoid attending family ceremonies and events.

Q23: What was the main reason for the estrangement between Jagan and his sister?
