She expressed concern about Mali's influence on Jagan.
She blamed Mali for the family's estrangement from Jagan.
She did not mention Mali in the postcard.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan's sister wrote "No one can blame Mali, with a father like you...", indicating she blamed Mali for the family's estrangement from Jagan.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when Mali and Grace offered him a lift?
options: He accepted the offer gratefully.
He declined the offer politely.
He asked them to take him to his shop.
He asked them about their relationship.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that when Grace asked Jagan, "Want a lift anywhere?", Jagan "said, 'No,' and tried to pass on", indicating he declined the offer politely. Set 2

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan use the back door to leave his house?
options: To avoid the common passage trodden by the feet of the "tainters"
To take a shortcut to his shop
To avoid interacting with Mali and Grace
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "took a side lane which led to the main street" after locking the back door of his house, as he wanted to avoid the common passage used by others.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan notice about the path leading to the main street?
options: It was well-maintained and clear of weeds.
It was overgrown with thorns and weeds.
It had been recently cleared.
It was a shortcut that Jagan used regularly.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text mentions that Jagan "noted that this path was overgrown with thorns and weeds."

mcqs.question: How long had it been since Jagan had last used the side lane?
options: 10 years
20 years
30 years
Nearly 50 years
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that "Nearly fifty years had elapsed since he had traversed this lane."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan plan to do about the overgrown path?
options: He planned to avoid using it altogether.
He planned to hire someone to clear it.
He planned to take his spade and clear the weeds himself.
He did not intend to do anything about it.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "said to himself, 'I must take out my spade and clear it,'" indicating he planned to clear the overgrown weeds himself.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he noticed Mali's window was open?
options: He knocked on the window to get Mali's attention.
He called out to Mali from the side lane.
He tried to tiptoe away without being noticed.
He asked Mali about Grace's whereabouts.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that after seeing Mali through the window, "Jagan tried to tiptoe away" instead of directly interacting with him.

mcqs.question: What did Mali do when he noticed Jagan outside?
options: He ignored Jagan and closed the window.
He invited Jagan to come inside.
He called out to Jagan, addressing him as "Father."
He asked Jagan why he was prowling around the house.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that "Mali opened his window, saying, 'Father!'" indicating he called out to Jagan.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan feel when Mali called him "Father"?
options: He was indifferent to being called "Father."
He was annoyed that Mali had addressed him that way.
He was thrilled to be called "Father" again after many days.
He was surprised, as Mali had not called him that in a long time.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan was "thrilled" when Mali called him "Father" after many days.

mcqs.question: Why did Mali ask Jagan why he was "prowling around like this"?
options: Because Jagan was spying on Mali and Grace.
Because Jagan had sealed himself off and was using the back door.
Because Jagan was acting suspiciously in the neighborhood.
Because Jagan was interfering in Mali's business.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Mali asked Jagan why he was "prowling around like this" after noting that Jagan had "sealed [himself] off and use[d] the back door."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about the neighbor who was watching them?
options: He praised the neighbor for being attentive.
He wished he had bought the neighbor's house.
He complained that the neighbor was always watching their house.
Both B and C.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan said the neighbor had "done nothing except watch our house" and that he "wished [he] had bought it when it was offered" so he could have given it to Mali.

mcqs.question: Why did Mali not want to talk to Jagan in the garden?
options: He was uncomfortable being in the bright sunlight.
He was worried about the neighbors watching them.
He preferred to have a private conversation indoors.
Both B and C.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Mali said "I don't like that guy over there watching us. Don't talk loudly" and "But all the passers-by will watch us," indicating he was concerned about privacy and the neighbors watching them.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan respond when Mali said people should respect others' privacy?
options: He agreed with Mali and suggested they move to a more private location.
He argued that people should not avoid each other's looks if they want to understand each other.
He ignored Mali's comment and continued pressing him to talk about Grace.
He acknowledged Mali's point but said they had nothing to hide from the neighbors.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan asked "If we avoided each other's looks, how should we under- .stand. each other? What is one ashamed of, that one's face must be hidden?" indicating he disagreed with Mali's view on privacy.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan suggest about Mali and Grace getting married?
options: He suggested they get married in a small temple with just the three of them and a priest.
He suggested they have a big wedding with all their family and friends invited.
He suggested they wait until Grace returned from her visit with friends.
He did not make any suggestions about Mali and Grace getting married.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan said "There is a very small temple, where you can go through a quick marriage. No one need be invited, just the three of us and a priest, and you can be done with the whole business in an hour."

mcqs.question: How did Mali respond to Jagan's suggestion about getting married?
options: He agreed with Jagan and said they would consider it.
He dismissed Jagan's suggestion as "nonsense" and said Grace had been getting "funny notions."
He accused Jagan of listening to gossip about their relationship.
Both B and C.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Mali "screamed" at Jagan's suggestion and said "You have been listening to nonsense. I never knew you could listen to such gossip."

mcqs.question: What did Mali say about Grace needing to see a psychiatrist?
options: Mali said Grace should see a psychiatrist because she was not in her right mind.
Mali said Grace should see a psychiatrist to get over her "funny notions."
Mali said Grace should see a psychiatrist because Jagan had refused to pay for her expenses.
Both A and B.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Mali said "Grace has been getting funny notions, that's why I told you to pack her off, but you grudged the expenditure. She is not in her right mind; she must go to a psychiatrist."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when Mali mentioned a psychiatrist?
options: Jagan immediately understood what a psychiatrist was.
Jagan asked Mali to explain what a psychiatrist was.
Jagan dismissed the idea of Grace seeing a psychiatrist.
Jagan became angry at Mali for suggesting it.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that after Mali said Grace "must go to a psychiatrist", Jagan asked "What's that?" indicating he did not know what a psychiatrist was.

mcqs.question: What did the neighbor say to Jagan about Mali's business?
options: The neighbor said Mali's business with American businessmen was not a good idea.
The neighbor asked Jagan about the nature of Mali's business.
The neighbor said it was good that Mali would be earning dollars for the country.
The neighbor expressed concern about Mali's unconventional business ventures.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that the neighbor said "Oh, that's very good. So he will earn dollars for our country. Very good, very good..."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when the neighbor started asking about Grace?
options: Jagan eagerly answered the neighbor's questions.
Jagan tried to change the subject to avoid talking about Grace.
Jagan told the neighbor it was none of his business.
Jagan got angry and walked away from the neighbor.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "felt that the next question was going to be about the daughter-in-law. Funny situation!—not knowing whether she is a daughter-in-law or not" and that he "tore himself away" from the neighbor to avoid the question.

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel "totally at a loss to decide who was lying"?
options: He was confused about whether Grace was Jagan's daughter-in-law or not.
He did not know if Mali was telling the truth about Grace visiting friends.
He was unsure if he had misunderstood the conversation with Mali.
All of the above.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan was "totally at a loss to decide who was lying" because he was uncertain about Grace's status as a daughter-in-law, as well as Mali's statements about her visiting friends.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan do after his conversation with Mali?
options: He went inside the house to talk to Grace.
He continued to keep watch on the house from the side lane.
He went to his shop, wanting to avoid further interactions.
He tried to make sense of the conversation with Mali.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that after the conversation, Jagan "tried to recollect the words that Mali had said and tried to make out their meaning. There was no meaning."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan use the back door to leave his house?
options: To avoid going through the common passage used by others.
To take a shortcut to his shop.
To avoid interacting with Mali and Grace.
All of the above.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "took a side lane which led to the main street" after locking the back door of his house, as he wanted to avoid the common passage used by others.

mcqs.question: How did Mali respond when Jagan asked about Grace's whereabouts?
options: Mali refused to answer Jagan's question.
Mali said Grace had gone to stay with some friends.
Mali accused Jagan of interfering in his business.
Both B and C.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that when Jagan asked about Grace, Mali replied "She is not here. She has gone to stay with some friends for a few days" and then accused Jagan of interfering in his business.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when Mali called out to him?
options: Jagan ignored Mali and continued walking away.
Jagan was annoyed that Mali had addressed him.
Jagan was thrilled to be called "Father" again.
Jagan was surprised, as Mali had not called him that in a long time.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan was "thrilled" when Mali called out to him and addressed him as "Father".

mcqs.question: Why did Mali not want to have the conversation with Jagan in the garden?
options: He was uncomfortable being in the bright sunlight.
He was worried about the neighbors watching them.
He preferred to have a private conversation indoors.
Both B and C.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Mali said "I don't like that guy over there watching us. Don't talk loudly" and "But all the passers-by will watch us," indicating he was concerned about privacy and the neighbors watching them.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan plan to do about Mali and Grace's relationship?
options: He planned to confront them directly about it.
He planned to have a discussion with Mali about it.
He planned to wait for another opportunity to "clear up this whole business once and for all."
He did not intend to do anything about it.
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The text states that Jagan "had half a mind to accost them then and there, but he let them go. I will find another opportunity to clear up this whole business once and for all", indicating he planned to address the issue of Mali and Grace's relationship at a later time.

content.value: # Chapter 12
# Set 1
Q1: What was Jagan's primary emotion throughout the day?
A) Excitement
B) Worry
C) Confusion
D) Indifference
Answer: B
Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan was worried, The entire day passed with his mind completely obsessed."
Q2: What did Jagan compare Mali to in the Bhagavad Gita?
A) The thousand-faced God
B) Arjuna the warrior
C) Krishna the charioteer
D) The endless universe
Answer: A

Explanation: The passage states that Jagan was "reminded of the concept of Viswarupa, that he read about in the Bhagavad Gita. When the warrior Arjuna hesitated to perform his duty on the battlefield, God came to him in the guise of his charioteer and then revealed Himself in all His immensity."
Q3: What was Jagan's initial mood when he traveled to meet his future bride?
A) Anxious
B) Annoyed
C) Happy
D) Skeptical
Answer: C
Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan was in a happy mood and laughed uncontrollably at the way they were progressing in the cross-country run."
Q4: What did Jagan's father advise him about regarding the bride?
A) Not to stare at her
B) To act mysterious
C) To ask about her education
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan's father had sent his elder son to accompany him and commanded Jagan, "Don't stare at the girl. I have seen her and I know she is good-looking. Don't imagine you are a big judge of persons." And it also states that "his brother had warned Jagan not to be too communicative, as a certain mysteriousness was invaluable in a son-in-law."
Q5: Why was Jagan unsure about the bride's appearance?
A) The photograph did not reveal her eyes
B) She was dressed in too many ornaments
C) He was not allowed to look at her for long
D) All of the above
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states all of these reasons for Jagan's uncertainty about the bride's appearance: "He had as yet no idea what she would look like. At home he had been shown a rather overtouched shiny photograph of her mounted within a floral border: a sharp-faced young person with tightly braided hair. The photographer had managed to achieve his task without revealing what the girl's eyes looked like, and Jagan, when presented with the photograph, had been unable to scrutinize it for long, because his father was watching him."
Q6: What did Jagan's elder brother advise him to say about his studies?
A) History
B) Mathematics
C) Engineering
D) Literature
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "Later, when they were alone, his brother nudged him and said, "You should have said 'mathematics,' because I know those people would prefer a mathematical son-in-law; all the boys in this part of the country are first-rate mathematicians."
Q7: How did Jagan's cousin react to Jagan's mood that day?
A) Tried to cheer him up
B) Avoided talking about Mali
C) Left early out of frustration
D) Didn't notice anything unusual
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "His cousin ate, spoke of various things, and waited as usual to talk of Mali, but Jagan was in no mood to encourage him, and the cousin gave up with resignation."
Q8: What did Jagan's house used to be like in the past?
A) Seethed with life, lamps burning in every room
B) Dark, silent, and sinister
C) Brightly lit during festivals
D) Both A and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage describes Jagan's house in the past as "seethed with life, lamps burning in every room, and during the festivals hundreds of mud lamps would be lit and arrayed all along the parapet. Theirs had been the brightest home in those days."
Q9: Where did Jagan travel to meet his future bride?
A) Kuppam
B) Myel
C) Trichy
D) Burma
Answer: B
Explanation: The passage states that "They had to go by train to Myel, a tiny red-tiled railway station set amidst emerald-green rice fields, two stations beyond Trichy."
Q10: Who accompanied Jagan on the journey to meet the bride?
A) His elder brother
B) His future father-in-law
C) His future brother-in-law
D) A and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan's father had sent his elder son to accompany him" and that "the future bride's younger brother, who had come to meet him as a piece of courtesy, was also in the carriage."
Q11: How did Jagan's future brother-in-law behave during the journey?
A) He was cheerful and friendly
B) He was grim and reserved
C) He was talkative and outgoing
D) He was dismissive and rude
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "the boy stuck to his seat and remained grim and silent. He had been trained to show respect to a brother-in-law by being reserved; that boy had the grimmest face in the country."
Q12: What did Jagan's father-in-law and his relations do when Jagan arrived?
A) They welcomed him warmly
B) They interrogated him extensively
C) They ignored him and discussed among themselves
D) They entertained him with music and dance
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "His future father-in-law and a number of his relations had assembled to have a look at the proposed bridegroom and measure him up from different angles. They all engaged him in conversation and tried to judge of his intelligence and outlook."
Q13: What did Jagan's brother advise him about how to behave?
A) To be talkative and engaging
B) To be mysterious and reserved
C) To be respectful and agreeable
D) To be confident and assertive
Answer: B
Explanation: The passage states that "his brother had warned Jagan not to be too communicative, as a certain mysteriousness was invaluable in a son-in-law."
Q14: What did Jagan's brother wish he had said about his studies?
A) History
B) Mathematics
C) Science
D) Literature
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "Later, when they were alone, his brother nudged him and said, "You should have said 'mathematics,' because I know those people would prefer a mathematical son-in-law; all the boys in this part of the country are first-rate mathematicians."
Q15: Where was Jagan's future brother-in-law eventually lost?
A) Kuppam
B) Myel
C) Trichy
D) Burma
Answer: D
Explanation: The passage states that "Ultimately he grew a long moustache as a commissioned air force officer, and was lost sight of in the Burma Campaign of 1942."
Q16: What was the main mode of transportation Jagan used to get to the bride's village?
A) Train
B) Cart drawn by bullocks
C) Walked
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "They had to go by train to Myel, a tiny red-tiled railway station set amidst emerald-green rice fields, two stations beyond Trichy. From Myel he had to go on in a cart drawn by a pair of bullocks over a bumpy mud track, and in some places even over cultivated fields."
Q17: How did Jagan feel about the bumpy cart ride?
A) Annoyed and irritated
B) Amused and entertained
C) Nervous and anxious
D) Indifferent and bored
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan was in a happy mood and laughed uncontrollably at the way they were progressing in the cross-country run. Every time the wheels sank into a sandy patch and the cartman got down and heaved them out with oaths, Jagan felt tickled."
Q18: What was Jagan's impression of the photograph of his future bride?
A) He thought she looked beautiful
B) He thought she looked sharp-faced
C) He wondered if she was squint-eyed
D) Both B and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that the photograph showed "a sharp-faced young person with tightly braided hair" and that Jagan "had been unable to scrutinize it for long, because his father was watching him. He was racked with a doubt whether the girl might not be squint-eyed, since it was well known that photographers tried to slur over such facts for purposes of marriage."
Q19: What did Jagan's father tell him not to do when meeting the bride?
A) Not to stare at her
B) Not to speak too much
C) Not to judge her appearance
D) All of the above
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan's father had sent his elder son to accompany him and commanded Jagan, "Don't stare at the girl. I have seen her and I know she is good-looking. Don't imagine you are a big judge of persons.""
Q20: What was the name of the railway station Jagan had to travel to?
A) Kuppam
B) Myel
C) Trichy
D) Burma
Answer: B
Explanation: The passage clearly states that "They had to go by train to Myel, a tiny red-tiled railway station set amidst emerald-green rice fields, two stations beyond Trichy."
Q21: What was the name of the village Jagan traveled to in order to meet his future bride?
A) Kuppam
B) Myel
C) Trichy
D) Burma
Answer: A
Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan had travelled to the village of Kuppam in order to take a look at the bride proposed for him by the elders of his family."
Q22: What was the relationship between Jagan and the younger brother of his future bride?
A) They were good friends
B) They were strangers
C) They were distant relatives
D) They were future brothers-in-law
Answer: D
Explanation: The passage clearly states that "the future bride's younger brother, who had come to meet him as a piece of courtesy, was also in the carriage."
Q23: What was the purpose of the visit to the bride's village?
A) To finalize the marriage arrangements
B) To see the bride for the first time
C) To discuss the bride's dowry
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage indicates that the purpose of the visit was both to see the bride for the first time and to finalize the marriage arrangements, as Jagan "had travelled to the village of Kuppam in order to take a look at the bride proposed for him by the elders of his family."
Q24: How did Jagan's father-in-law and his relations try to evaluate Jagan?
A) By asking him questions
B) By observing his behavior
C) By discussing among themselves
D) All of the above
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "His future father-in-law and a number of his relations had assembled to have a look at the proposed bridegroom and measure him up from different angles. They all engaged him in conversation and tried to judge of his intelligence and outlook."
Q25: What was the significance of the flowers and vase in the photograph of the bride?
A) They were used to decorate the bride
B) They were meant to distract from the bride's appearance
C) They were a symbol of the family's wealth
D) They were irrelevant details added by the photographer
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage states that "She had been decorated with so many ornaments that it was impossible to guess what she really looked like, and of course the photographer had imparted the appropriate complexion."
# Set 2
Q1: What was Jagan's reaction when the refreshments were served?
A) He eagerly ate the snacks
B) He politely refused the snacks
C) He discreetly enjoyed the snacks
D) He complained about the snacks
Answer: C

Explanation: The passage states that although "Left to himself he would have gobbled up the entire lot (his food theories had not yet begun), but a glance from his brother restrained him" and that he "mumbled this sentence with the utmost reluctance, jointly with his brother, who uttered it with great clarity."
Q2: How did Jagan's brother advise him to behave during the visit?
A) To be confident and assertive
B) To be polite and reserved
C) To be talkative and engaging
D) To be critical and skeptical
Answer: B

Explanation: The passage indicates that Jagan's brother "was literally keeping his eye on him, commanding and manipulating him by narrowing his eyelids or opening them wide" to ensure Jagan behaved with the expected restraint and reserve.
Q3: What was the purpose of the incense sticks lit in the hall?
A) To create a festive atmosphere
B) To cover up the smell of the cowshed
C) To purify the air for the guests
D) Both B and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "incense sticks were lit so as to overwhelm the smell of the cowshed at the back yard. 'These fellows from the city are fussy and don't know how to live with domestic animals,' her father had said, or so Jagan's wife reported later in life."
Q4: How did Jagan's previous experiences with prospective brides go?
A) He was impressed with their beauty
B) He was disappointed by their appearance
C) He was indifferent to their looks
D) Both B and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "On two occasions he had kept staring at the girls in open-mouthed wonder because they happened to be stunningly ugly; on another occasion he undisguisedly watched the legs of the girl as she walked in because she had been reputed to be lame."
Q5: What was Jagan's main concern during the visit?
A) Impressing the family
B) Evaluating the bride
C) Avoiding embarrassment
D) All of the above
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage indicates that Jagan was worried "lest he should perpetrate some silly faux pas and become a disgrace to his family" while also being eager to get a good look at the bride, despite his brother's advice.
Q6: How did Ambika's father introduce her to Jagan?
A) As his first daughter
B) As an excellent singer
C) As a shy and reserved girl
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that "The father mentioned a place six miles away. Jagan was certainly not in a critical enough mood to say they should have spared themselves the trouble. The music ceased. There were stirrings inside, some arguments and protests, and then a little girl with tightly plaited hair emerged grinning with the comment, 'Ambika refuses to come out, she feels shy,' at which all the elders joked and laughed. The master of the house raised his voice and called, 'Ambika, come on, come on, there's nothing to be afraid of in these days.' And he addressed the women inside in a general way, 'Don't make fun of her, she will be all right....' After this preamble a tall girl emerged swishing her lace sari, facing the assembly and smiling, and Jagan's heart gave a thump. 'Not at all like the photo, so tall! I can't believe ...' The master of the house saved further speculation by announcing, 'She is my first daughter,' and the tall girl said, 'Ambika is coming.'"
Q7: What was Jagan's initial impression of the bride when she entered the room?
A) She was taller than expected
B) She was shorter than expected
C) She was exactly as he expected
D) He could not make out her appearance
Answer: A

Explanation: The passage states that "The tall girl said, 'Ambika is coming.' The rest Jagan did not hear; he lost interest in the tall girl who was only a sort of advance guard for her younger sister, who came with downcast eyes and bowed head and moved across the arena so fast that Jagan could not take in any detail. 'Not short nor tall, nor fat nor puny ...' Jagan could not arrange her in any clear outline."
Q8: How did Jagan react when his and the bride's eyes met?
A) He was indifferent
B) He was embarrassed
C) He was fascinated
D) He was confused
Answer: C
Explanation: The passage states that "their eyes met, and Jagan's heart-palpitated and raced; and before he could do anything about it, it was all over."
Q9: What was the significance of the harmonium music played during the visit?
A) It was to entertain the guests
B) It was to showcase the bride's talent
C) It was to set a serene mood
D) Both B and C
Answer: D
Explanation: The passage indicates that the harmonium music, with Ambika singing a devotional song, was both to showcase her singing ability and to set a serene, spiritual mood for the occasion.
Q10: How did Jagan's brother try to control Jagan's behavior during the visit?
A) By commanding him verbally
B) By making subtle physical gestures
C) By ignoring him completely
D) Both A and B
Answer: D
Explanation: The passage states that Jagan's brother "was literally keeping his eye on him, commanding and manipulating him by narrowing his eyelids or opening them wide."
Q11: What was the reason for the numerous protocols and restraints observed during the visit?
A) To maintain the family's dignity
B) To impress the visiting groom
C) To make the bride feel comfortable
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage indicates that the strict protocols and restraints were observed both to maintain the family's dignity as "honoured visitors, on whose verdict would depend the future of the girl" and to impress the visiting groom, as "it was a highly serious and important role, and they were expected to carry themselves with dignity."
Q12: How did Jagan's family view his previous behavior during marriage visits?
A) They were proud of his boldness
B) They were amused by his mistakes
C) They were concerned about his manners
D) Both B and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that Jagan's "lapses" in behavior during previous visits "went into the repertory of family jokes" and that his family "had tried to prevent mistakes by sending his elder brother to chaperone him through this delicate mission."
Q13: What was the purpose of the elaborate preparations made in the hall?
A) To welcome the guests
B) To impress the prospective groom
C) To create a festive atmosphere
D) Both A and B
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage indicates that the preparations, such as moving furniture and lighting incense, were made "In honour of this visit" and to ensure the guests, especially the prospective groom Jagan, felt welcomed and impressed.
Q14: How did Ambika's father try to encourage her to come out and meet Jagan?
A) He scolded her for being shy
B) He praised her singing abilities
C) He assured her there was nothing to be afraid of
D) Both B and C
Answer: D

Explanation: The passage states that Ambika's father "raised his voice and called, 'Ambika, come on, come on, there's nothing to be afraid of in these days.' And he addressed the women inside in a general way, 'Don't make fun of her, she will be all right....'" This indicates he both praised her singing and tried to reassure her.
Q15: How did Jagan initially perceive the bride when she entered the room?
A) He found her physically unattractive
B) He was unable to make out her appearance
C) He was immediately captivated by her
D) He was disappointed by her appearance

Avoiding embarrassment

As an excellent singer
As a shy and reserved girl

And he addressed the women inside in a general way, 'Don't make fun of her, she will be all right....' After this preamble a tall girl emerged swishing her lace sari, facing the assembly and smiling, and Jagan's heart gave a thump. 'Not at all like the photo, so tall! I can't believe ...' She was shorter than expected
She was exactly as he expected
He could not make out her appearance

'Not short nor tall, nor fat nor puny ...' Jagan could not arrange her in any clear outline."

He was confused

The bride's family was given inferior seating

They were satisfied with the quality and weight
They were unsure about the value of the items

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's reaction when his family criticized the bride's gold waist-belt?
options: He angrily defended his wife's family
He agreed with his family's assessment
He tried to mediate between the two sides
He remained silent and did not get involved
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "Jagan had the temerity to reply, 'It is because they are criticizing my wife, poor girl!' At this demonstration of loyalty his brother left him with a 'wry smile, saying, 'You are obsessed, it is no use talking to you.'"

options: They personally handed out the invitations
They kept a meticulous list of all the guests

Both B and C

To keep him closer to the family activities
To accommodate his study area
Both A and C
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that Jagan "was given a room in the middle block. When he and his wife shut the door, they were in a world of their own within the confines of the heavy four posters. At the performance of the consummation ceremony, Jagan's father had insisted on the nuptial suite being furnished properly at the expense of the bride's party. In one corner of the room Jagan was supposed to have his study (he still had his examinations to face)."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's focus and priorities change after his marriage?
options: He became more dedicated to his studies
He spent most of his time with his wife
He maintained a balance between family and wife
He became more involved in household duties
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "At home Jagan spent very little time with his sister, mother, or brother, as he used to, but shut himself in and awaited his wife's arrival."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's family members react to his neglect of them?
options: They were understanding and supportive
They expressed disappointment and criticism
They ignored his behavior and focused on other matters
They tried to intervene and change his behavior

options: She happily complied with his requests
She firmly reminded him of her obligations
She ignored his demands and focused on her own duties
She threatened to leave him if he didn't change

He was irritated by the inconvenience
He encouraged her to hide it from the family
He ignored the situation and focused on other matters

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's brother try to advise him about balancing his time between his wife and the family?
options: He praised Jagan's devotion to his wife
He warned Jagan about becoming unpopular
He suggested Jagan spend more time with the family
Both B and C

If you spend four hours in your bedroom, at least give the others an hour now and then; otherwise you make yourself unpopular at home.'"

mcqs.question: What was the reason for Jagan's repeated failures in his academic exams?
options: He was disinterested in his studies
He was distracted by his marital relations
He faced financial difficulties
Both A and B

He was skeptical about the child bringing good fortune
He was concerned about the financial obligations involved
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "I was dreading Jagan would be without issue," said Jagan's father. "But I was in no doubt at any time. Barrenness Sm: known in our house."

mcqs.question: How did Ambika feel about the birth of Mali and the family's reaction?
options: She was overwhelmed and felt pressure to perform
She was annoyed by the excessive celebrations
She was proud to have fulfilled her duty as a daughter-in-law
She was indifferent to the whole situation
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "Ambika followed him, prostrated at the feet of the guests, and was also blessed by everyone. She held herself up proudly, having now attained the proper status in the family."

mcqs.question: What was the significance of the gifts and feast arranged for Mali's birth?
options: It was a display of the family's wealth and status
It was a traditional way to welcome the first-born child
It was a means to seek blessings and good fortune
Both B and C
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "when she came home, bringing the three-month-old baby, Ambika's parents sent with her an enormous load of gifts, as prescribed in the social code, for the first-born, and a huge feast was held for which a hundred guests were invited."

mcqs.question: How did the grandparents view the birth of Mali as a new addition to the family?
options: They were indifferent and saw it as a burden
They were overjoyed and considered it a blessing
They were skeptical about the child's future prospects
They were primarily concerned about the financial implications
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "A new son in the house is a true treasure in this life and beyond life." and that Jagan's father was "in no doubt at any time. Barrenness Sm: known in our house."

mcqs.question: What was the purpose of the gold, silver, and corn offerings made to the temple after Mali's birth?
options: To seek blessings and good fortune for the child
To fulfill a vow made during the earlier temple visit
To display the family's wealth and piety
Both A and B
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that the offerings were "according to the solemn vow made during their visit" to the temple, and were intended to bring good fortune to the newborn child.

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's father react to the high prices charged by the coconut sellers in the village?
options: He happily paid the asking price without bargaining
He politely negotiated with the sellers to lower the prices
He angrily accused the villagers of exploiting the pilgrims
He decided to bring the coconuts from home next time
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that Jagan's father "carried on interminable negotiations with the coconut-sellers over the price, trying to beat them down. Finally he yielded, grumbling that these villagers were spoilt nowadays and had become 171 172 exploiters of the worst kind and flourishing his fists in anger."

mcqs.question: What was the significance of weighing the newborn baby Mali immediately after birth?
options: It was a ritual to bring good fortune to the child
It was to determine the child's astrological chart
It was to calculate the gifts to be offered to the temple
It was a tradition to welcome the first-born child
mcqs.explanation: Explanation: The passage states that "the very minute he was delivered (in the village home of his mother) he was weighed on a scale pan, even before the midwife could -clean him up properly— and an equivalent weight in gold, silver, and corn was made up to be delivered to the God on Badri Hill, according to the solemn vow made during their visit."

They promised to give him a monthly allowance
