content.value: # Chapter 13
# Set 1
Q1: What is the name of Jagan's son?
A) Vinayak
B) Mali
C) Gaffur
D) Ambika
Answer: B
The text mentions that Jagan's son is named Mali.
Q2: Where did Jagan find himself when he woke up?
A) At the foot of a statue
B) In his house
C) In a forest
D) At his brother's house
Answer: A
The text states that Jagan "was awakened by the clamour of birds alighting on the head of Sir F. Lawley", indicating he had fallen asleep at the foot of a statue.
Q3: What did Jagan think about the state of his house?
A) It was bright and lively
B) It was tainted and unhappy
C) It was in need of renovation
D) It was well-kept by his son
Answer: B
The text describes Jagan thinking that his house "has an unhappy look" and that it "will never get back the light and laughter of other days".
Q4: Who did Jagan think could brighten up his house?
A) His son Mali and his daughter-in-law
B) His mother and his sister Ambika
C) The ghosts that might inhabit the house
D) No one, the house was beyond brightening
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan thinks "They are not the sort to make a home bright, unlike my mother or even Ambika when she was well."
Q5: Why did Jagan feel he could not go back to his house?
A) It was too expensive to maintain
B) It was haunted by evil spirits
C) His son and daughter-in-law had moved out
D) It was tainted by his son's actions
Answer: D
The text mentions that Jagan felt "It's tainted, but it is not my house that's tainted. It is his."
Q6: How long did Jagan think Mali had left to live?
A) 10-15 years
B) 50 years or more
C) 80 years
D) Jagan did not speculate on Mali's lifespan
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan thinks "Mali, with or without his story machine, will have to go on for fifty years or more in that house."
Q7: What did Jagan wonder about Grace's future?
A) Whether Mali would succeed in sending her back
B) Whether she would stay in the same situation
C) Whether she would move out of the house
D) Both A and B
Answer: D
The text mentions Jagan wondering "Where will Grace be when Mali is eighty? Still in the same situation?" and "Perhaps Mali would succeed in sending her back."
Q8: Why did Jagan think his sixtieth birthday would pass unnoticed?
A) He was too old to celebrate
B) His son and daughter-in-law were absent
C) He was a widower with no family
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text states that Jagan thought "A widower had no right to celebrate anything. He was fit only for retirement."
Q9: What did Jagan plan to do with the key to his house?
A) Keep it with himself
B) Leave it with his brother
C) Leave it with his neighbor
D) Throw it away
Answer: B
The text mentions that Jagan thought "Why can't I leave it with my brother? It will be a good excuse to visit him."
Q10: Why did Jagan feel nostalgic for his brother's company?
A) His brother had tears in his eyes when Jagan went to jail
B) His brother was the only one left from his generation
C) His brother had lost all his teeth
D) All of the above
Answer: D

The text describes Jagan's nostalgia for his brother, including mentioning that his brother had tears when Jagan went to jail, that he was the only one left from his generation, and that he had lost all his teeth.
Q11: What item did Jagan plan to take with him in his bundle?
A) His spectacles
B) His toothbrush
C) His charka
D) His wallet
Answer: C
The text states that "in the little bundle, in which among other things was included his charka."
Q12: Why did Jagan feel he had to keep spinning the charka?
A) It was a duty he owed Mahatma Gandhi
B) It was a tradition in his family
C) It helped him meditate
D) It was the only thing he could do at home
Answer: A
The text mentions that Jagan carried the charka because "I made a vow before him that I would spin every day of my life."
Q13: What was Jagan's usual time for his morning bath?
A) 4 o'clock
B) 5 o'clock
C) 6 o'clock
D) 7 o'clock
Answer: B
The text states that "It was five o'clock, his usual hour for the bath for half a century."
Q14: What did Jagan think might happen in his deserted house?
A) It would be haunted by evil spirits
B) It would be broken into by robbers
C) It would be taken over by his neighbors
D) It would fall into disrepair
Answer: A

The text mentions that Jagan thought "if he never opens the door again, well, it's his business: it's his house that is going to become haunted with evil spirits, which might throw things about with a clatter."
Q15: Who did Jagan hope would ask questions about the ghosts in his house?
A) The police
B) His son Mali
C) His inquisitive neighbor
D) No one, he did not want anyone to know
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan thought "Let him ask all the questions he likes of the ghost storming my house."
Q16: What did Jagan remember about his previous send-off when he went to jail?
A) His entire family accompanied him halfway
B) His brother had tears in his eyes
C) His family disapproved of his patriotic acts
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text describes all these details about Jagan's previous send-off when he went to jail.
Q17: Why did Jagan feel nostalgic for a similar send-off now?
A) He wanted his family to show him the same intense feelings
B) He wanted to relive the patriotic moments of the past
C) He wanted his brother to see him off one last time
D) Both A and C
Answer: D
The text indicates that Jagan longed for "a nice, crowded send-off now" and felt a "longing for a glimpse of his brother" as the only remaining member of his generation.
Q18: What did Jagan's cousin tell him about his brother's appearance?
A) His brother had lost all his teeth
B) His brother had grey hair
C) His brother had gained weight
D) His brother looked much older
Answer: A
The text states that "according to the cousin, \[Jagan's brother\] had lost all his teeth, and Jagan felt curious to know what he looked like now."
Q19: Which word does Jagan use to describe his planned withdrawal from life?
A) Retirement
B) Renunciation
C) Retreat
D) Rejection
Answer: C
The text mentions that Jagan thought "the withdrawal would not be different from death."
Q20: What does Jagan feel is the "best possible solution" for Grace's situation?
A) Mali sending her back
B) Grace moving out on her own
C) Jagan taking Grace in
D) Mali and Grace getting married
Answer: A
The text states that Jagan thinks "Perhaps Mali would succeed in sending her back, It was the best possible solution--if they still spurned his suggestion for a quick solemnization in the hills."
Q21: What ritual did Jagan remember people celebrating for a man's 60th birthday?
A) Pipe and drum playing
B) Feasting and ceremonies
C) Knotting of the thali
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text mentions all of these elements as part of the 60th birthday celebrations that Jagan remembered.
Q22: What does Jagan think about the need for ceremonials and rituals?
A) They are necessary for a meaningful life
B) They are an unnecessary burden
C) They are traditions that should be upheld
D) They hold no meaning for him anymore
Answer: D
The text states that Jagan feels "Mali had proved that there was no need for ceremonials, not even the business of knotting the thali around the bride's neck."
Q23: What does Jagan think about trying to understand his son Mali's actions?
A) It is an interesting puzzle to solve
B) It is a futile exercise that tires him
C) It is a necessary duty as a father
D) It is a source of great concern for him
Answer: B
The text describes Jagan thinking that "Puzzling over things was enervating. Reading a sense into Mali's actions was fatiguing, like the attempt to spell out a message in a half-familiar script."
Q24: What does Jagan think is the significance of turning 60?
A) It marks the beginning of retirement
B) It is a time of rebirth and new beginnings
C) It is a cause for grand celebrations
D) It is the end of one's meaningful life
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan believes "At sixty, one is reborn and enters a new janma."
Q25: What did Jagan think would happen if he never opened the door to his house again?
A) It would be occupied by his son and daughter-in-law
B) It would fall into disrepair and ruin
C) It would be haunted by evil spirits
D) It would be seized by the government
Answer: C

The text mentions that Jagan thought "if he never opens the door again, well, it's his business: it's his house that is going to become haunted with evil spirits, which might throw things about with a clatter."
# Set 2
Q1: Why did Jagan think his brother might not let him enter his house?
A) His brother disapproved of Jagan's actions
B) His brother feared Jagan's shadow would taint the threshold
C) His brother did not want Jagan to take the key
D) His brother was no longer living there
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan thought his brother "would probably keep him standing in the street and tell him to throw the key from a distance for fear Jagan's shadow might taint the threshold."
Q2: What did Jagan plan to tell his brother about Mali's situation?
A) That Mali and Grace were not really married
B) That Mali had been arrested for having alcohol in his car
C) That Mali was living a happy life with Grace
D) That Mali had moved out of the house
Answer: A

The text mentions that Jagan "might have to speak about Mali too. 'It's not only his marriage, but you must know the latest truth—that they are not married at all, but carry tales against each other, although they sit close in a motor car.'"
Q3: What was Jagan's cousin doing when Jagan saw him?
A) Riding a bicycle clumsily
B) Driving Jagan's green car
C) Walking down the street
D) Repairing a bicycle
Answer: A

The text describes Jagan's cousin "riding along clumsily on a bicycle, his tuft flying in the wind, his wheels zigzagging perilously onto the edge of the storm drain and retracting miraculously to the centre of the road."
Q4: Why did Jagan's cousin borrow the bicycle?
A) To go for a leisurely ride
B) To chase after Jagan's taxi
C) To meet Jagan urgently
D) To return the bicycle to his neighbor
Answer: C
The text states that the cousin "was in a hurry to meet you, so I borrowed the bicycle from my neighbour."
Q5: What did Jagan's cousin tell him about Mali?
A) Mali had been involved in a car accident
B) Mali had been arrested and was in the sub-jail
C) Mali had run away from home
D) Mali had fallen ill and was in the hospital
Answer: B
The text clearly states that "Mali is in prison since last evening."
Q6: Why was Mali arrested?
A) For speeding and reckless driving
B) For possession of illegal drugs
C) For having a bottle of alcohol in his car
D) For assaulting a police officer
Answer: C
The text explains that "He was found with half a bottle of alcohol in his car."
Q7: What was Jagan's initial reaction to the news of Mali's arrest?
A) Anger and disappointment
B) Shock and disbelief
C) Concern and worry
D) Indifference and resignation
Answer: B
The text describes Jagan's reaction as: "Jagan came to a dead stop on the road and screamed, 'Oh God! Why?'"
Q8: What did Jagan think about the conditions in the sub-jail where Mali was held?
A) It was a clean and comfortable place
B) It had improved since Jagan's own time there
C) It was a dirty and unpleasant place
D) It was not suitable for Mali's delicate constitution
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan "knew the place; it is very dirty, prisoners urinate in a corner of the lock-up—or have they improved the conditions since my days?"
Q9: Who did Jagan's cousin know that could help get Mali out of jail?
A) The District Collector
B) The Superintending Engineer
C) The police superintendent
D) The lawyer
Answer: A
The text mentions that the cousin said "I know the District Collector, and so we can get things done."
Q10: What did Jagan's cousin do to help Mali after learning about his arrest?
A) He went to the sub-jail and spoke to Mali
B) He arranged for a lawyer to defend Mali
C) He got Mali some food and coffee
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text states that the cousin "The first thing I did was to go out to the sub-jail and plead with the warders there. I saw the boy and spoke to him. I managed to get him a cup of coffee also."
Q11: Where was Mali's car when the police found the alcohol?
A) At the police station
B) At the Mempi outpost
C) At Mali's house
D) At the scene of the arrest
Answer: B
The text explains that "The green car was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."
Q12: Who else was in the car with Mali when he was arrested?
A) His friends
B) Grace
C) The driver
D) No one else
Answer: A
The text states that "Two of his friends" were in the car with Mali.
Q13: Where was Jagan when his cousin came to find him?
A) At home
B) At the police station
C) Sleeping at the foot of the statue
D) Visiting his brother
Answer: C
The text clearly states that Jagan "was only sleeping on the statue" when his cousin came to find him.
Q14: What did Jagan's cousin say about Jagan's philosophy when he was distressed?
A) It was useless if he couldn't handle this trial
B) It would help him get through this situation
C) It was outdated and no longer relevant
D) It was just talk without any real substance
Answer: A
The cousin says to Jagan, "Don't lose nerve, what is all your philosophy worth if you cannot bear this little trial?"
Q15: What did Jagan's cousin do to try to get Mali out of jail quickly?
A) Bribed the police officers
B) Contacted the District Collector
C) Hired a high-profile lawyer
D) All of the above
Answer: B
The text states that the cousin said "I know the District Collector, and so we can get things done."
Q16: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he learned Mali had been drinking?
A) He was not surprised
B) He was disappointed but not shocked
C) He was shocked and dismayed
D) He did not believe it
Answer: C
The text describes Jagan saying "I... I didn't know the boy drank," indicating it was a fresh discovery that shocked him.
Q17: What did Jagan think was the root cause of Mali's troubles?
A) Mali's friends
B) Mali's marriage to Grace
C) Mali's purchase of the green car
D) Mali's rebellious nature
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan "found an agreeable escape into this theme. 'Everything would have been well if he hadn't bought that car.'"
Q18: Where was the bottle of alcohol found in Mali's car?
A) In the glove compartment
B) Hidden somewhere in the car
C) In plain sight on the front seat
D) The text does not specify the exact location
Answer: B
The text mentions that "A policeman seems to have stopped Mali's car and found hidden in it half a bottle of some alcoholic drink."
Q19: What did Jagan's cousin do to try to help Mali while he was in jail?
A) Brought him a change of clothes
B) Arranged for a lawyer to represent him
C) Provided him with food and a cup of coffee
D) All of the above
Answer: C
The text states that the cousin "I managed to get him a cup of coffee also."
Q20: How long had Mali been in the sub-jail before Jagan found out?
A) A few hours
B) Overnight
C) Several days
D) The text does not specify
Answer: B
The text states that Mali "is in prison since last evening."
Q21: What was Jagan's main concern about Mali being in the sub-jail?
A) That he would be mistreated by the other inmates
B) That he would not be able to cope with the poor conditions
C) That he would be interrogated too harshly by the police
D) All of the above
Answer: B
The text notes that Jagan was worried because Mali "has always slept on a spring mattress, since he was seven. How can I get him out?"
Q22: What did Jagan's cousin say about the change in jail conditions since Jagan's time?
A) The conditions had deteriorated further
B) The conditions had improved significantly
C) The conditions were still as bad as before
D) The cousin did not comment on any changes
Answer: B
The cousin reassures Jagan that "Naturally, it is all different now."
Q23: Where did Jagan's cousin say he had been before coming to find Jagan?
A) At the house of the Superintending Engineer
B) At the police station to bail out Mali
C) At the District Collector's office
D) At his own home
Answer: A
The text states that the cousin had "gone to the house of the Superintending Engineer, where I had gone to fix up a home tutor for their son."
Q24: Why did the police stop and search Mali's car?
A) They received an anonymous tip-off
B) They were conducting routine checks for prohibition offenses
C) They had been tipped off about Mali's drinking habits
D) They were specifically looking for Mali's car
Answer: B
The text explains that the car "was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."
Q25: How did Jagan's cousin learn about Mali's arrest?
A) He heard it from an orderly at the Superintendent's house
B) Mali called him directly from the police station
C) The news was reported in the local newspaper
D) Jagan's wife informed the cousin
Answer: A
The text states that "At the turning near the General Post Office an orderly from the Superintendent's house gave me the news."
# Set 3
Q1: According to Jagan's cousin, what reason could the police have had for arresting Mali?
A) Mali's friends framed him
B) The police were bribed to arrest Mali
C) Mali was caught with drugs in the car
D) The police had a grudge against Jagan
Answer: D

The text states that the cousin suggested "He might have been demanding free packets of sweets from your shop; after all, poor fellows, they are so ill paid that they do seek favours from shop men. You might not remember it now; but you will have to try and recollect how you threatened to report him to his officers."
Q2: What did Jagan's cousin say about the lawyer handling Mali's case?
A) The lawyer was incompetent and inexperienced
B) The lawyer was the best in the district and knew Mali
C) The lawyer refused to take on Mali's case
D) The lawyer was only interested in getting paid
Answer: B
The text mentions that the lawyer "knows Mali and admires his plans. He seems to have promised to buy shares in Mali's company when the time comes."
Q3: What did Jagan's cousin suggest could have happened with the bottle of alcohol in Mali's car?
A) Mali had bought it himself
B) A stranger left it there after getting a lift
C) The police had planted it to frame Mali
D) Mali's friends had put it there as a prank
Answer: B
The text states the cousin's suggestion that "Someone left it there. A stranger stopped the car on the mountain road, asked for a lift, got off on the way, and perhaps left the bottle behind."
Q4: What did Jagan's cousin say the lawyer was looking into?
A) The background of the policeman who arrested Mali
B) Bribing the judge to get Mali acquitted
C) Finding witnesses to testify against the police
D) All of the above
Answer: A
The text mentions that the lawyer "is also looking into the antecedents of the policeman who checked Mali's car at the outpost."
Q5: What was Jagan's initial reaction to the news of Mali's arrest?
A) Anger and disappointment
B) Shock and disbelief
C) Concern and worry
D) Indifference and resignation
Answer: B
The text describes Jagan's reaction as: "Jagan came to a dead stop on the road and screamed, 'Oh God! Why?'"
Q6: What did Jagan's cousin say could happen if Mali was convicted?
A) He could be fined heavily
B) He could be sentenced up to 2 years in prison
C) He would be deported back to his country
D) He would have to do community service
Answer: B
The text states that the cousin said "They could sentence him up to two years under this act."
Q7: How did Jagan react to his cousin's insistence on getting Mali out of jail?
A) He agreed and helped with the legal process
B) He was indifferent and wanted no part in it
C) He was skeptical but went along with the plan
D) He refused to believe Mali was actually arrested
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan said "If what you say is true, well, truth will win. If it is not true, there is nothing I can do."
Q8: What did Jagan say about the policeman's potential grudge against him?
A) Jagan had threatened to report the policeman
B) Jagan had bribed the policeman in the past
C) Jagan had assaulted the policeman years ago
D) Jagan did not believe the policeman had any grudge
Answer: D
The text shows Jagan laughing at the idea, saying "If a grudge was to be borne, we had greater cause than the police."
Q9: What did Jagan's cousin say about Mahatma Gandhi's teachings?
A) Gandhi had never advocated non-resentment
B) Gandhi's teachings were outdated and irrelevant
C) Gandhi had trained them not to nurse resentment
D) Gandhi's teachings did not apply to dealing with the police
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan said "Mahatma Gandhi trained us not to nurse any resentment."
Q10: What did Jagan say about the role of truth in getting Mali out of jail?
A) Truth alone would not be enough, they needed a good lawyer
B) Truth would definitely get Mali out if the accusations were false
C) Truth was irrelevant, the lawyer would have to manipulate the case
D) Truth could not be established, so it was futile to try
Answer: B
The text shows Jagan saying "If what you say is true, well, truth will win."
Q11: What did Jagan's cousin say the lawyer was planning to do?
A) File a counter-case against the police
B) Bribe the judge to get Mali acquitted
C) Discredit the policeman's testimony
D) All of the above
Answer: A
The text states that the cousin said "If he is able to establish the malafides of the policeman, we may even file a counter case in order to strengthen ours."
Q12: Where did Jagan tell his cousin he was planning to go?
A) To his brother's house
B) To a retreat across the river
C) To the police station to see Mali
D) To the lawyer's office
Answer: B
The text describes Jagan telling his cousin about "the retreat across the river."
Q13: What did Jagan say he would be watching at the retreat?
A) A holy man perform rituals
B) A goddess emerge from a stone
C) The sunset over the river
D) Nothing, he just wanted to get away
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan said "I am going to watch a Goddess come out of a stone."
Q14: What did Jagan's cousin warn him about the place of the retreat?
A) It was haunted by evil spirits
B) It was run by a sorcerer who practiced black magic
C) It was too remote and isolated for Jagan's comfort
D) It was too close to the cremation ground
Answer: B
The text has the cousin saying "He is a sorcerer: knows black magic and offers to transmute base metals into gold...."
Q15: How did Jagan describe his determination to go away?
A) He said he had never felt more resolved in his life
B) He said he felt like his heart had failed and he was dying
C) He said he was finally free to do as he pleased
D) All of the above
Answer: D
The text includes all these descriptions of Jagan's determination, including "I've never felt more determined in my life" and "Think that my heart has failed, that's all."
Q16: What did Jagan instruct his cousin to do regarding his shop?
A) Keep it running and take care of the employees
B) Sell the shop and use the proceeds to help Mali
C) Close down the shop and donate the inventory
D) Hand over the shop to Mali to manage
Answer: A
The text states Jagan told the cousin to "Open the shop at the usual hour and run it. Mali will take charge of it eventually. Keep Sivaraman and the rest happy; don't throw them out."
Q17: What amount of money did Jagan give his cousin for Mali's legal expenses?
D) An open-ended cheque
Answer: D
The text describes Jagan writing out a cheque for the lawyer's "preliminary expenses" without specifying the amount.
Q18: What was Jagan's view on Mali spending time in jail?
A) He felt it would be good for Mali's character
B) He was worried it would be damaging for Mali
C) He thought it was unnecessary and unfair
D) He did not have an opinion on it
Answer: A
The text states that Jagan said "A dose of prison life is not a bad thing. It may be just what he needs now."
Q19: Where did Jagan's cousin say Grace had been placed?
A) In a women's hostel with a job
B) Back in her home country
C) Living with Mali's friends
D) The text does not specify her whereabouts
Answer: A
The text mentions the cousin saying Grace "has friends who have found a job for her in a women's hostel."
Q20: What did Jagan say he would do if Grace wanted to go back to her country?
A) Nothing, he washed his hands of her
B) He would arrange for her to go back
C) He would advise her to stay in India
D) He would ask Mali to make the arrangements
Answer: B
The text states that Jagan said "If she ever wants to go back to her country, I will buy her a ticket. It's a duty we owe her."
Q21: What was the name of the place Jagan mentioned where buses left for Mempi?
A) Market Gate
B) Mempi Outpost
C) General Post Office
D) The text does not specify the name
Answer: A
The text clearly states "At the Market Gate buses leave for Mempi every four hours starting from eight-thirty in the morning."
Q22: What did Jagan's cousin say about the lawyer's opinion on Mali's "story machine"?
A) The lawyer was highly skeptical of it
B) The lawyer thought it was an impressive idea
C) The lawyer refused to discuss it further
D) The cousin did not have time to discuss it with the lawyer
Answer: B
The text mentions that when the cousin mentioned Mali's "story machine", the lawyer "said, 'Why not?' when I mentioned it."
Q23: What did Jagan's cousin say was the reason the police stopped and searched Mali's car?
A) They received a tip-off about illegal activities
B) They were conducting routine prohibition checks
C) They were specifically looking for Mali's car
D) They had a vendetta against Mali
Answer: B
The text states the car "was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."
Q24: What did Jagan say about the possibility of the policeman having a grudge against him?
A) He was certain the policeman had a grudge
B) He was willing to investigate the possibility
C) He dismissed the idea as unlikely
D) He said it was irrelevant to Mali's case
Answer: C
The text shows Jagan "laughing at this idea" of the policeman having a grudge against him.
Q25: What did Jagan say about the world continuing without him?
A) The world would collapse without him
B) The world would not miss him at all
C) The world would go on with or without him
D) The world would mourn his absence
Answer: C
The text states that Jagan said "Everything can go on with or without me. The world doesn't collapse even when a great figure is assassinated or dies of heart failure."

mcqs.question: What is the name of Jagan's son?
options: Vinayak
Mali
Gaffur
Ambika
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan's son is named Mali.

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan find himself when he woke up?
options: At the foot of a statue
In his house
In a forest
At his brother's house
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "was awakened by the clamour of birds alighting on the head of Sir F. Lawley", indicating he had fallen asleep at the foot of a statue.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about the state of his house?
options: It was bright and lively
It was tainted and unhappy
It was in need of renovation
It was well-kept by his son
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan thinking that his house "has an unhappy look" and that it "will never get back the light and laughter of other days".

mcqs.question: Who did Jagan think could brighten up his house?
options: His son Mali and his daughter-in-law
His mother and his sister Ambika
The ghosts that might inhabit the house
No one, the house was beyond brightening
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thinks "They are not the sort to make a home bright, unlike my mother or even Ambika when she was well."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel he could not go back to his house?
options: It was too expensive to maintain
It was haunted by evil spirits
His son and daughter-in-law had moved out
It was tainted by his son's actions
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan felt "It's tainted, but it is not my house that's tainted. It is his."

mcqs.question: How long did Jagan think Mali had left to live?
options: 10-15 years
50 years or more
80 years
Jagan did not speculate on Mali's lifespan
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thinks "Mali, with or without his story machine, will have to go on for fifty years or more in that house."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan wonder about Grace's future?
options: Whether Mali would succeed in sending her back
Whether she would stay in the same situation
Whether she would move out of the house
Both A and B
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions Jagan wondering "Where will Grace be when Mali is eighty? Still in the same situation?" and "Perhaps Mali would succeed in sending her back."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan think his sixtieth birthday would pass unnoticed?
options: He was too old to celebrate
His son and daughter-in-law were absent
He was a widower with no family
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thought "A widower had no right to celebrate anything. He was fit only for retirement."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan plan to do with the key to his house?
options: Keep it with himself
Leave it with his brother
Leave it with his neighbor
Throw it away
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan thought "Why can't I leave it with my brother? It will be a good excuse to visit him."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel nostalgic for his brother's company?
options: His brother had tears in his eyes when Jagan went to jail
His brother was the only one left from his generation
His brother had lost all his teeth
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan's nostalgia for his brother, including mentioning that his brother had tears when Jagan went to jail, that he was the only one left from his generation, and that he had lost all his teeth.

mcqs.question: What item did Jagan plan to take with him in his bundle?
options: His spectacles
His toothbrush
His charka
His wallet
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "in the little bundle, in which among other things was included his charka."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel he had to keep spinning the charka?
options: It was a duty he owed Mahatma Gandhi
It was a tradition in his family
It helped him meditate
It was the only thing he could do at home
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan carried the charka because "I made a vow before him that I would spin every day of my life."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's usual time for his morning bath?
options: 4 o'clock
5 o'clock
6 o'clock
7 o'clock
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "It was five o'clock, his usual hour for the bath for half a century."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think might happen in his deserted house?
options: It would be haunted by evil spirits
It would be broken into by robbers
It would be taken over by his neighbors
It would fall into disrepair
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan thought "if he never opens the door again, well, it's his business: it's his house that is going to become haunted with evil spirits, which might throw things about with a clatter."

mcqs.question: Who did Jagan hope would ask questions about the ghosts in his house?
options: The police
His son Mali
His inquisitive neighbor
No one, he did not want anyone to know
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thought "Let him ask all the questions he likes of the ghost storming my house."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan remember about his previous send-off when he went to jail?
options: His entire family accompanied him halfway
His brother had tears in his eyes
His family disapproved of his patriotic acts
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text describes all these details about Jagan's previous send-off when he went to jail.

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan feel nostalgic for a similar send-off now?
options: He wanted his family to show him the same intense feelings
He wanted to relive the patriotic moments of the past
He wanted his brother to see him off one last time
Both A and C
mcqs.explanation: The text indicates that Jagan longed for "a nice, crowded send-off now" and felt a "longing for a glimpse of his brother" as the only remaining member of his generation.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin tell him about his brother's appearance?
options: His brother had lost all his teeth
His brother had grey hair
His brother had gained weight
His brother looked much older
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "according to the cousin, [Jagan's brother] had lost all his teeth, and Jagan felt curious to know what he looked like now."

mcqs.question: Which word does Jagan use to describe his planned withdrawal from life?
options: Retirement
Renunciation
Retreat
Rejection
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan thought "the withdrawal would not be different from death."

mcqs.question: What does Jagan feel is the "best possible solution" for Grace's situation?
options: Mali sending her back
Grace moving out on her own
Jagan taking Grace in
Mali and Grace getting married
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thinks "Perhaps Mali would succeed in sending her back, It was the best possible solution--if they still spurned his suggestion for a quick solemnization in the hills."

mcqs.question: What ritual did Jagan remember people celebrating for a man's 60th birthday?
options: Pipe and drum playing
Feasting and ceremonies
Knotting of the thali
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions all of these elements as part of the 60th birthday celebrations that Jagan remembered.

mcqs.question: What does Jagan think about the need for ceremonials and rituals?
options: They are necessary for a meaningful life
They are an unnecessary burden
They are traditions that should be upheld
They hold no meaning for him anymore
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan feels "Mali had proved that there was no need for ceremonials, not even the business of knotting the thali around the bride's neck."

mcqs.question: What does Jagan think about trying to understand his son Mali's actions?
options: It is an interesting puzzle to solve
It is a futile exercise that tires him
It is a necessary duty as a father
It is a source of great concern for him
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan thinking that "Puzzling over things was enervating. Reading a sense into Mali's actions was fatiguing, like the attempt to spell out a message in a half-familiar script."

mcqs.question: What does Jagan think is the significance of turning 60?
options: It marks the beginning of retirement
It is a time of rebirth and new beginnings
It is a cause for grand celebrations
It is the end of one's meaningful life
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan believes "At sixty, one is reborn and enters a new janma."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think would happen if he never opened the door to his house again?
options: It would be occupied by his son and daughter-in-law
It would fall into disrepair and ruin
It would be haunted by evil spirits
It would be seized by the government
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan thought "if he never opens the door again, well, it's his business: it's his house that is going to become haunted with evil spirits, which might throw things about with a clatter." Set 2

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan think his brother might not let him enter his house?
options: His brother disapproved of Jagan's actions
His brother feared Jagan's shadow would taint the threshold
His brother did not want Jagan to take the key
His brother was no longer living there
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan thought his brother "would probably keep him standing in the street and tell him to throw the key from a distance for fear Jagan's shadow might taint the threshold."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan plan to tell his brother about Mali's situation?
options: That Mali and Grace were not really married
That Mali had been arrested for having alcohol in his car
That Mali was living a happy life with Grace
That Mali had moved out of the house
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that Jagan "might have to speak about Mali too. 'It's not only his marriage, but you must know the latest truth—that they are not married at all, but carry tales against each other, although they sit close in a motor car.'"

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's cousin doing when Jagan saw him?
options: Riding a bicycle clumsily
Driving Jagan's green car
Walking down the street
Repairing a bicycle
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan's cousin "riding along clumsily on a bicycle, his tuft flying in the wind, his wheels zigzagging perilously onto the edge of the storm drain and retracting miraculously to the centre of the road."

mcqs.question: Why did Jagan's cousin borrow the bicycle?
options: To go for a leisurely ride
To chase after Jagan's taxi
To meet Jagan urgently
To return the bicycle to his neighbor
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin "was in a hurry to meet you, so I borrowed the bicycle from my neighbour."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin tell him about Mali?
options: Mali had been involved in a car accident
Mali had been arrested and was in the sub-jail
Mali had run away from home
Mali had fallen ill and was in the hospital
mcqs.explanation: The text clearly states that "Mali is in prison since last evening."

mcqs.question: Why was Mali arrested?
options: For speeding and reckless driving
For possession of illegal drugs
For having a bottle of alcohol in his car
For assaulting a police officer
mcqs.explanation: The text explains that "He was found with half a bottle of alcohol in his car."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction to the news of Mali's arrest?
options: Anger and disappointment
Shock and disbelief
Concern and worry
Indifference and resignation
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan's reaction as: "Jagan came to a dead stop on the road and screamed, 'Oh God! Why?'"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think about the conditions in the sub-jail where Mali was held?
options: It was a clean and comfortable place
It had improved since Jagan's own time there
It was a dirty and unpleasant place
It was not suitable for Mali's delicate constitution
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "knew the place; it is very dirty, prisoners urinate in a corner of the lock-up—or have they improved the conditions since my days?"

mcqs.question: Who did Jagan's cousin know that could help get Mali out of jail?
options: The District Collector
The Superintending Engineer
The police superintendent
The lawyer
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that the cousin said "I know the District Collector, and so we can get things done."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin do to help Mali after learning about his arrest?
options: He went to the sub-jail and spoke to Mali
He arranged for a lawyer to defend Mali
He got Mali some food and coffee
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin "The first thing I did was to go out to the sub-jail and plead with the warders there. I saw the boy and spoke to him. I managed to get him a cup of coffee also."

mcqs.question: Where was Mali's car when the police found the alcohol?
options: At the police station
At the Mempi outpost
At Mali's house
At the scene of the arrest
mcqs.explanation: The text explains that "The green car was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."

mcqs.question: Who else was in the car with Mali when he was arrested?
options: His friends
Grace
The driver
No one else
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "Two of his friends" were in the car with Mali.

mcqs.question: Where was Jagan when his cousin came to find him?
options: At home
At the police station
Sleeping at the foot of the statue
Visiting his brother
mcqs.explanation: The text clearly states that Jagan "was only sleeping on the statue" when his cousin came to find him.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about Jagan's philosophy when he was distressed?
options: It was useless if he couldn't handle this trial
It would help him get through this situation
It was outdated and no longer relevant
It was just talk without any real substance
mcqs.explanation: The cousin says to Jagan, "Don't lose nerve, what is all your philosophy worth if you cannot bear this little trial?"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin do to try to get Mali out of jail quickly?
options: Bribed the police officers
Contacted the District Collector
Hired a high-profile lawyer
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin said "I know the District Collector, and so we can get things done."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's initial reaction when he learned Mali had been drinking?
options: He was not surprised
He was disappointed but not shocked
He was shocked and dismayed
He did not believe it
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan saying "I... I didn't know the boy drank," indicating it was a fresh discovery that shocked him.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan think was the root cause of Mali's troubles?
options: Mali's friends
Mali's marriage to Grace
Mali's purchase of the green car
Mali's rebellious nature
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan "found an agreeable escape into this theme. 'Everything would have been well if he hadn't bought that car.'"

mcqs.question: Where was the bottle of alcohol found in Mali's car?
options: In the glove compartment
Hidden somewhere in the car
In plain sight on the front seat
The text does not specify the exact location
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that "A policeman seems to have stopped Mali's car and found hidden in it half a bottle of some alcoholic drink."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin do to try to help Mali while he was in jail?
options: Brought him a change of clothes
Arranged for a lawyer to represent him
Provided him with food and a cup of coffee
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin "I managed to get him a cup of coffee also."

mcqs.question: How long had Mali been in the sub-jail before Jagan found out?
options: A few hours
Overnight
Several days
The text does not specify
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Mali "is in prison since last evening."

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's main concern about Mali being in the sub-jail?
options: That he would be mistreated by the other inmates
That he would not be able to cope with the poor conditions
That he would be interrogated too harshly by the police
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text notes that Jagan was worried because Mali "has always slept on a spring mattress, since he was seven. How can I get him out?"

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the change in jail conditions since Jagan's time?
options: The conditions had deteriorated further
The conditions had improved significantly
The conditions were still as bad as before
The cousin did not comment on any changes
mcqs.explanation: The cousin reassures Jagan that "Naturally, it is all different now."

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan's cousin say he had been before coming to find Jagan?
options: At the house of the Superintending Engineer
At the police station to bail out Mali
At the District Collector's office
At his own home
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin had "gone to the house of the Superintending Engineer, where I had gone to fix up a home tutor for their son."

mcqs.question: Why did the police stop and search Mali's car?
options: They received an anonymous tip-off
They were conducting routine checks for prohibition offenses
They had been tipped off about Mali's drinking habits
They were specifically looking for Mali's car
mcqs.explanation: The text explains that the car "was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan's cousin learn about Mali's arrest?
options: He heard it from an orderly at the Superintendent's house
Mali called him directly from the police station
The news was reported in the local newspaper
Jagan's wife informed the cousin
mcqs.explanation: The text states that "At the turning near the General Post Office an orderly from the Superintendent's house gave me the news." Set 3

mcqs.question: According to Jagan's cousin, what reason could the police have had for arresting Mali?
options: Mali's friends framed him
The police were bribed to arrest Mali
Mali was caught with drugs in the car
The police had a grudge against Jagan
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin suggested "He might have been demanding free packets of sweets from your shop; after all, poor fellows, they are so ill paid that they do seek favours from shop men. You might not remember it now; but you will have to try and recollect how you threatened to report him to his officers."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the lawyer handling Mali's case?
options: The lawyer was incompetent and inexperienced
The lawyer was the best in the district and knew Mali
The lawyer refused to take on Mali's case
The lawyer was only interested in getting paid
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that the lawyer "knows Mali and admires his plans. He seems to have promised to buy shares in Mali's company when the time comes."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin suggest could have happened with the bottle of alcohol in Mali's car?
options: Mali had bought it himself
A stranger left it there after getting a lift
The police had planted it to frame Mali
Mali's friends had put it there as a prank
mcqs.explanation: The text states the cousin's suggestion that "Someone left it there. A stranger stopped the car on the mountain road, asked for a lift, got off on the way, and perhaps left the bottle behind."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say the lawyer was looking into?
options: The background of the policeman who arrested Mali
Bribing the judge to get Mali acquitted
Finding witnesses to testify against the police
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that the lawyer "is also looking into the antecedents of the policeman who checked Mali's car at the outpost."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say could happen if Mali was convicted?
options: He could be fined heavily
He could be sentenced up to 2 years in prison
He would be deported back to his country
He would have to do community service
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin said "They could sentence him up to two years under this act."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan react to his cousin's insistence on getting Mali out of jail?
options: He agreed and helped with the legal process
He was indifferent and wanted no part in it
He was skeptical but went along with the plan
He refused to believe Mali was actually arrested
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "If what you say is true, well, truth will win. If it is not true, there is nothing I can do."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about the policeman's potential grudge against him?
options: Jagan had threatened to report the policeman
Jagan had bribed the policeman in the past
Jagan had assaulted the policeman years ago
Jagan did not believe the policeman had any grudge
mcqs.explanation: The text shows Jagan laughing at the idea, saying "If a grudge was to be borne, we had greater cause than the police."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about Mahatma Gandhi's teachings?
options: Gandhi had never advocated non-resentment
Gandhi's teachings were outdated and irrelevant
Gandhi had trained them not to nurse resentment
Gandhi's teachings did not apply to dealing with the police
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "Mahatma Gandhi trained us not to nurse any resentment."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about the role of truth in getting Mali out of jail?
options: Truth alone would not be enough, they needed a good lawyer
Truth would definitely get Mali out if the accusations were false
Truth was irrelevant, the lawyer would have to manipulate the case
Truth could not be established, so it was futile to try
mcqs.explanation: The text shows Jagan saying "If what you say is true, well, truth will win."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say the lawyer was planning to do?
options: File a counter-case against the police
Bribe the judge to get Mali acquitted
Discredit the policeman's testimony
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text states that the cousin said "If he is able to establish the malafides of the policeman, we may even file a counter case in order to strengthen ours."

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan tell his cousin he was planning to go?
options: To his brother's house
To a retreat across the river
To the police station to see Mali
To the lawyer's office
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan telling his cousin about "the retreat across the river."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say he would be watching at the retreat?
options: A holy man perform rituals
A goddess emerge from a stone
The sunset over the river
Nothing, he just wanted to get away
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "I am going to watch a Goddess come out of a stone."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin warn him about the place of the retreat?
options: It was haunted by evil spirits
It was run by a sorcerer who practiced black magic
It was too remote and isolated for Jagan's comfort
It was too close to the cremation ground
mcqs.explanation: The text has the cousin saying "He is a sorcerer: knows black magic and offers to transmute base metals into gold...."

mcqs.question: How did Jagan describe his determination to go away?
options: He said he had never felt more resolved in his life
He said he felt like his heart had failed and he was dying
He said he was finally free to do as he pleased
All of the above
mcqs.explanation: The text includes all these descriptions of Jagan's determination, including "I've never felt more determined in my life" and "Think that my heart has failed, that's all."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan instruct his cousin to do regarding his shop?
options: Keep it running and take care of the employees
Sell the shop and use the proceeds to help Mali
Close down the shop and donate the inventory
Hand over the shop to Mali to manage
mcqs.explanation: The text states Jagan told the cousin to "Open the shop at the usual hour and run it. Mali will take charge of it eventually. Keep Sivaraman and the rest happy; don't throw them out."

mcqs.question: What amount of money did Jagan give his cousin for Mali's legal expenses?
options: An open-ended cheque
mcqs.explanation: The text describes Jagan writing out a cheque for the lawyer's "preliminary expenses" without specifying the amount.

mcqs.question: What was Jagan's view on Mali spending time in jail?
options: He felt it would be good for Mali's character
He was worried it would be damaging for Mali
He thought it was unnecessary and unfair
He did not have an opinion on it
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "A dose of prison life is not a bad thing. It may be just what he needs now."

mcqs.question: Where did Jagan's cousin say Grace had been placed?
options: In a women's hostel with a job
Back in her home country
Living with Mali's friends
The text does not specify her whereabouts
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions the cousin saying Grace "has friends who have found a job for her in a women's hostel."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say he would do if Grace wanted to go back to her country?
options: Nothing, he washed his hands of her
He would arrange for her to go back
He would advise her to stay in India
He would ask Mali to make the arrangements
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "If she ever wants to go back to her country, I will buy her a ticket. It's a duty we owe her."

mcqs.question: What was the name of the place Jagan mentioned where buses left for Mempi?
options: Market Gate
Mempi Outpost
General Post Office
The text does not specify the name
mcqs.explanation: The text clearly states "At the Market Gate buses leave for Mempi every four hours starting from eight-thirty in the morning."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say about the lawyer's opinion on Mali's "story machine"?
options: The lawyer was highly skeptical of it
The lawyer thought it was an impressive idea
The lawyer refused to discuss it further
The cousin did not have time to discuss it with the lawyer
mcqs.explanation: The text mentions that when the cousin mentioned Mali's "story machine", the lawyer "said, 'Why not?' when I mentioned it."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan's cousin say was the reason the police stopped and searched Mali's car?
options: They received a tip-off about illegal activities
They were conducting routine prohibition checks
They were specifically looking for Mali's car
They had a vendetta against Mali
mcqs.explanation: The text states the car "was halted at the Mempi outpost where they generally check for prohibition offences."

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about the possibility of the policeman having a grudge against him?
options: He was certain the policeman had a grudge
He was willing to investigate the possibility
He dismissed the idea as unlikely
He said it was irrelevant to Mali's case
mcqs.explanation: The text shows Jagan "laughing at this idea" of the policeman having a grudge against him.

mcqs.question: What did Jagan say about the world continuing without him?
options: The world would collapse without him
The world would not miss him at all
The world would go on with or without him
The world would mourn his absence
mcqs.explanation: The text states that Jagan said "Everything can go on with or without me. The world doesn't collapse even when a great figure is assassinated or dies of heart failure."
